### FAQ
Q: What does a quick commerce agency do?
A: A quick commerce agency gets a brand listed on 10-minute delivery platforms and then runs the account: catalogue and images, city and dark-store availability, purchase orders and replenishment, promotions and ads, ratings and monthly reporting. gaa-tha does this for Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket from one team.

Q: What is quick commerce and which platforms matter in India?
A: Quick commerce is delivery of groceries, FMCG, beauty and everyday items in roughly 10–30 minutes from local dark stores. In India the platforms that matter are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket with BB Now. Each has different category strengths and city coverage, which is why we plan by platform and city rather than treating them as one channel.

Q: Which quick commerce platform should I launch on first?
A: Start where your category and target cities overlap best. Blinkit and Zepto lead in metro grocery and FMCG, Swiggy Instamart adds strong snack and impulse demand, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now bring their marketplace shoppers, and BigBasket suits staples and larger packs. We map your SKUs and cities against each platform before recommending an order.

Q: Do I need to be on all six platforms?
A: No. Most brands do better launching on two platforms, proving availability and sell-through in a few cities, and then expanding. Each platform adds purchase orders, stock commitments and ad budget, so spreading thin before the operation is stable usually costs more than it earns.

Q: How do you keep products in stock on quick commerce?
A: By tracking availability at dark-store level every week, forecasting from sell-through so purchase orders are raised before stock runs out, and chasing dispatch and receipt on every PO. Out-of-stock on quick commerce means losing the search rank and the shelf, so availability is the first number we manage.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
A: Platforms work on margins, listing or onboarding charges and sometimes marketing contributions, and these vary by category and change over time. We share the current structure for your category before you sign anything, and plan pack sizes and pricing so the margin works after those charges.

Q: Can you manage D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce together?
A: Yes. The same team runs Shopify stores, Amazon and Flipkart accounts and quick commerce, with one content library and one monthly review. That keeps pricing, pack sizes and creative consistent across channels and stops one channel undercutting another.

Q: How do you price quick commerce management?
A: A one-time onboarding fee per platform and a monthly management retainer that scales with platforms, cities and SKUs. Ad spend and any platform charges are paid by you directly to the platform, so there is no markup on media.


## Blinkit Seller Onboarding
https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-onboarding
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha handles Blinkit seller onboarding for brands in India: registration on the Blinkit seller and brand portals, GST, FSSAI and brand documentation, category approvals, catalogue and thumbnails built to Blinkit's specifications, city and dark-store mapping, and a go-live checklist that ends with your first purchase order rather than a pending application.

Best for: FMCG, snacks and beverages, beauty, baby care, pet care, home and kitchen brands entering Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and other metros
Timeline: 3–6 weeks from complete documents to first purchase order, depending on category
Engagement model: One-time onboarding fee; optional monthly Blinkit account management after go-live
Channels/platforms: Blinkit app and website across its dark-store network

### What it is
Blinkit seller onboarding is the process of getting a brand approved, listed and stocked on Blinkit, the 10-minute delivery platform owned by Eternal (formerly Zomato). It covers business and brand documentation, category and licence checks, commercial terms, catalogue creation to Blinkit's image and attribute standards, and the first purchase order that puts stock into Blinkit's dark stores. Blinkit is inventory-led for most brands, so onboarding is as much a supply arrangement as a listing.

gaa-tha runs the whole sequence for you. We prepare the document pack, present the range and pack sizes in the way Blinkit's category team expects, build the catalogue and thumbnails, map which cities and dark stores to stock first, and stay on the application until the first PO is raised and received. Blinkit's strongest markets are Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Kolkata, with a growing tier-2 footprint, so we plan the launch cities from where your category already sells.

### What's included
- Eligibility review of your category, pack sizes and margins against Blinkit's current requirements
- Document pack: GST, PAN, bank proof, brand ownership or authorisation letter, FSSAI and other category licences
- Registration on Blinkit's seller and brand portals and follow-up with the category team
- Commercial terms review — margins, listing charges and marketing contributions explained before you sign
- Catalogue creation: titles with pack size, thumbnails, secondary images, attributes and descriptions
- City and dark-store mapping for the launch, matched to your distribution and warehouse locations
- First purchase order coordination: quantities, packaging and labelling, dispatch and receipt
- Go-live checklist covering live listings, search visibility, pricing and initial availability
- Handover to monthly Blinkit account management, or a self-management SOP if you prefer

### How we work
1. Eligibility and economics — We check your category, licences, shelf life and pack sizes against Blinkit's requirements and model the margin per SKU before applying.
2. Documents and registration — The document pack is assembled and verified, the seller and brand registration submitted, and every query from Blinkit's team answered by us.
3. Catalogue and content — Titles, thumbnails, secondary images and attributes are built to Blinkit's specifications so listings pass QC the first time.
4. Cities, stores and first PO — Launch cities and dark stores are agreed, the first purchase order is raised and we coordinate packaging, labelling and dispatch to Blinkit's warehouse.
5. Go-live and handover — Listings are checked live in every launch city, availability is verified, and the account moves into monthly management or your own team's hands.

### Deliverables
- Blinkit-ready document checklist with every item verified
- Approved seller and brand registration on Blinkit
- Live catalogue with thumbnails and attributes for every launch SKU
- City and dark-store launch map
- First purchase order tracked from raise to receipt
- Go-live report and account-management SOP

Tools & platforms: Blinkit Seller Hub, Blinkit Ads, Google Sheets, WhatsApp Business, Adobe Photoshop, AI image tools
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to SKU count and categories; platform margins and charges are paid by you to Blinkit directly and shared in writing before you sign.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need to sell on Blinkit?
A: Typically GST registration, PAN, a cancelled cheque or bank proof, brand ownership proof such as a trademark certificate or a brand authorisation letter, FSSAI licence for food and beverages, and any other category licence such as cosmetics or drug licences where relevant. Blinkit may also ask for product data, MRP labels and pack images. Requirements change, so we share a current checklist before you apply.

Q: How long does Blinkit onboarding take?
A: Usually 3–6 weeks from a complete document pack to the first purchase order. Registration and category approval take the first one to two weeks, catalogue build and QC another one to two, and the first PO and dispatch the rest. Missing licences or incomplete product data are the most common causes of delay.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on Blinkit?
A: Blinkit works on margins and may charge listing, onboarding or marketing contributions that vary by category and change over time. We do not quote fixed figures because they differ brand to brand; we obtain the current structure for your category and walk you through it before you commit.

Q: Which categories does Blinkit accept?
A: Grocery and staples, snacks and beverages, dairy and fresh, personal care and beauty, baby and pet care, home and kitchen, health and wellness, stationery, electronics accessories and seasonal or festive ranges. Each category has its own licence and shelf-life requirements, and some are invite-only or capacity-limited by city.

Q: How does the Blinkit dark-store model work for a brand?
A: Blinkit raises purchase orders, receives stock at its warehouses and distributes it to dark stores across a city, so every store carries only a curated range. A brand needs to be reliable on supply and packaging, and to earn its place on the shelf with sell-through. We plan quantities city by city so the first PO is realistic.

Q: Which cities should I launch on Blinkit first?
A: Start where your brand already has distribution and demand — often Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad or Pune — and add cities as sell-through proves the range. Launching everywhere at once spreads stock thin and creates availability gaps that hurt ranking.

Q: What happens at go-live?
A: We verify every listing is live and searchable in each launch city, check pricing, thumbnails and pack-size titles, confirm stock is showing as available in the dark stores that received it, and set up the availability tracker. Then the account moves to monthly management or to your own team with an SOP.

Q: Should I onboard Blinkit or Zepto first?
A: If your priority cities are Delhi NCR and the north, Blinkit usually comes first; if Mumbai, Bengaluru or Hyderabad, Zepto is a close call. Many brands onboard both within the same quarter. We compare category demand in your cities before recommending, and the document pack for one is largely reusable for the other.


## Blinkit Account Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-account-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs Blinkit account management for brands in India as a monthly operation: dark-store availability and fill rate tracked by city, purchase orders chased from raise to receipt, catalogue and thumbnails kept sharp, pricing and promotions planned to margin, Blinkit Ads optimised to a target ROAS, ratings monitored, settlements reconciled and one monthly review.

Best for: FMCG, food and beverage, beauty, baby and pet care brands already live on Blinkit
Timeline: Audit and setup in 1–2 weeks, then monthly
Engagement model: Monthly management retainer; ad spend and platform charges paid directly to Blinkit
Channels/platforms: Blinkit app and website, Blinkit Ads

### What it is
Blinkit account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's account on Blinkit after go-live: keeping SKUs available across dark stores, forecasting and coordinating purchase orders, maintaining catalogue content, planning pricing and promotions, running Blinkit Ads, monitoring ratings and reconciling what Blinkit pays against what was supplied. On a 10-minute platform an out-of-stock SKU loses its search rank within days, so availability is managed weekly rather than monthly.

At gaa-tha a named account manager owns the Blinkit account and reports on one dashboard. We track availability and fill rate by city and dark store, keep the PO cycle moving with your warehouse, plan promotions around Blinkit's sale days and festivals, and run ads only where stock can support the demand. The month ends with a review that shows sales, availability, ad ROAS, ratings and reconciled settlements side by side.

### What's included
- Weekly dark-store availability and fill-rate tracking by city, with out-of-stock alerts
- Purchase-order forecasting, follow-up, dispatch coordination and receipt confirmation
- Catalogue upkeep: titles with pack size, thumbnails, secondary images, attributes and new SKU additions
- Pricing and promotion planning to margin, including Blinkit sale days and festive events
- Blinkit Ads management — product listing ads on search and category, plus banner campaigns — to a target ROAS
- Ratings and customer-feedback monitoring with product, packaging and delivery issues routed to you
- Settlement reconciliation: PO versus goods receipt, short receipts, damages, debit notes and marketing invoices
- Account-health and compliance checks on labelling, MRP and shelf-life requirements
- Monthly review report covering sales, availability, POs, ads, promotions, ratings and reconciliation

### How we work
1. Audit and baseline — We review current listings, availability by city, PO history, ad performance and past settlements, then agree the numbers the account is run against.
2. Availability and PO rhythm — A weekly availability check and a PO forecast are set up with your warehouse so stock is raised before dark stores run dry.
3. Content and pricing — Thumbnails, titles and attributes are fixed, pricing checked against margin, and a promotion calendar aligned to Blinkit's events.
4. Ads and visibility — Blinkit Ads campaigns are structured by SKU and city, run only where stock supports them, and optimised weekly against ROAS.
5. Reconcile and review — Settlements are reconciled against POs and receipts, disputes raised, and a monthly review covers every number in one report.

### Deliverables
- Weekly availability and fill-rate tracker by city and dark store
- Purchase-order log with forecast, raise, dispatch and receipt dates
- Maintained Blinkit catalogue with current thumbnails and attributes
- Promotion calendar and Blinkit Ads campaign structure
- Monthly reconciliation statement with disputes and claims status
- Monthly Blinkit account review report

Tools & platforms: Blinkit Seller Hub, Blinkit Ads, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, WhatsApp Business, Adobe Photoshop
Pricing model: Monthly management retainer scoped to SKU count, cities and ad activity; Blinkit Ads spend and platform charges are paid by you directly to Blinkit.

### FAQ
Q: How do you manage availability and fill rate on Blinkit?
A: We check availability at dark-store level every week, flag SKUs that are out of stock or low in any city, and measure supplier fill rate as quantity received against quantity ordered on each PO. Low availability is fixed by forecasting earlier and correcting quantities; low fill rate is fixed at your warehouse with packaging, labelling and dispatch discipline.

Q: How do purchase orders work on Blinkit and what do you handle?
A: Blinkit raises POs for its warehouses based on demand and current stock, and the brand dispatches within the PO window. We forecast expected POs from sell-through, follow up when a PO is late, coordinate quantities and packaging with your team, track dispatch and receipt, and log short receipts or rejections so they can be disputed.

Q: Do you maintain the catalogue and content?
A: Yes. Titles with pack size, thumbnails, secondary images, attributes and descriptions are kept current, new SKUs and pack variants are added, and listings are checked after every Blinkit template change. Content that stops a shopper in a two-second scroll is produced by the same in-house team.

Q: How do you handle pricing and promotions on Blinkit?
A: Every promotion is planned to margin first: we model the discount, the platform's share and the expected uplift before agreeing to a sale day or festive event. Pricing is also checked across Zepto, Instamart and your own store so one channel does not undercut another.

Q: Do you run Blinkit Ads?
A: Yes. Blinkit Ads offers product listing ads on search and category pages and banner placements, and we run them by SKU and city against a target ROAS. Ads are switched off in cities where the SKU is out of stock, because paying for clicks that cannot convert is the fastest way to waste budget on quick commerce.

Q: How do you manage ratings on Blinkit?
A: We monitor ratings and feedback weekly, separate product complaints from packaging and delivery issues, and route each to the right owner — your production team, your warehouse or Blinkit's support. Recurring themes are reported monthly so pack or label changes can be made.

Q: What does reconciliation involve?
A: Matching Blinkit's settlements to POs, goods receipt notes, short receipts, damages, returns, debit notes and marketing or ad invoices. Discrepancies are raised with Blinkit within the dispute window and tracked until closed, so your books reflect what was actually supplied and sold.

Q: What is in the monthly review?
A: Sales and units by city and SKU, availability and fill rate, PO status, catalogue changes, promotions run and their margin impact, Blinkit Ads spend and ROAS, ratings trends and the reconciliation summary — followed by decisions on SKUs, cities and budget for the next month.

Tools & platforms: Instamart Seller Hub, Swiggy Instamart Ads, Google Sheets, WhatsApp Business, Adobe Photoshop, AI image tools
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to SKU count and categories; Instamart's margins and charges are paid by you directly and shared in writing before you sign.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need to sell on Swiggy Instamart?
A: Usually GST registration, PAN, bank proof, a trademark certificate or brand authorisation letter, FSSAI licence for food and beverages, and any category-specific licence such as cosmetics approvals. Swiggy also asks for product master data with MRP, barcodes, shelf life and pack images. We share a current checklist because requirements change by category.

Q: How long does Swiggy Instamart onboarding take?
A: Typically 3–6 weeks from a complete document pack to the first purchase order. Vendor registration and category review take the first stretch, then catalogue QC, then the first PO and dispatch. Incomplete product data and missing licences are the usual causes of delay, so we verify everything before submission.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on Swiggy Instamart?
A: Instamart works on category margins and may ask for listing, onboarding or marketing contributions that vary by category and change over time. We do not quote fixed figures; we obtain the current terms for your category and explain them before you commit.

Q: Which categories sell best on Instamart?
A: Snacks, beverages, ice cream, ready-to-eat and instant food, dairy and bakery, party supplies, personal care and beauty, and household essentials all do well because Instamart shoppers often buy for the next hour rather than the week. Fresh, staples and larger packs also sell, but the impulse categories are where a new brand is most likely to be noticed.

Q: How does Instamart's dark-store model work for a brand?
A: Swiggy raises purchase orders to its city warehouses and distributes stock to Instamart dark stores that each carry a curated range. Brands earn and keep shelf space through sell-through and reliable supply, so a focused range with dependable fill rate beats a long list of SKUs.

Q: Which cities should I launch on Instamart first?
A: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi NCR and Mumbai are Instamart's deepest markets, with Chennai, Pune and Kolkata close behind and a growing tier-2 network. Start where your brand already has distribution and demand, and expand as sell-through proves the range.

Q: What happens at go-live?
A: We confirm every listing is live and searchable in each launch city, check pricing, thumbnails and pack-size titles, verify stock is showing as available in the dark stores that received it, and set up the availability tracker. The account then moves into monthly management or to your own team with an SOP.

Q: Should I onboard Instamart before Blinkit and Zepto?
A: If your range is snack, beverage or ready-to-eat led, Instamart can be the best first platform because of the food-delivery audience beside it. For broader grocery and FMCG, Blinkit or Zepto usually come first. We map your SKUs and cities against all three before recommending, and most of the document pack carries across.


## Instamart Account Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/instamart-account-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs Swiggy Instamart account management for brands in India as a monthly operation: dark-store availability and fill rate tracked by city, purchase orders forecast and chased, catalogue and thumbnails maintained, pricing and promotions planned to margin, Instamart ads run to a target ROAS, ratings monitored, settlements reconciled and one monthly review across every city.

Channels/platforms: Swiggy Instamart, Swiggy Instamart Ads

### What it is
Instamart account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's account on Swiggy Instamart after go-live: keeping SKUs in stock across dark stores, forecasting and coordinating purchase orders, maintaining catalogue content, planning pricing and promotions, running Instamart ads, monitoring ratings and reconciling settlements against what was supplied. Instamart demand spikes around meals, evenings, weekends and cricket and festival days, so availability planning has to account for those peaks rather than a flat weekly average.

At gaa-tha a named account manager owns the Instamart account. We track availability and fill rate by city and dark store, keep the PO cycle moving with your warehouse ahead of peak days, plan promotions around Swiggy's sale events and festive periods, and run ads only for SKUs and cities with stock to sell. The month ends with a review that puts sales, availability, ads, ratings and reconciled settlements side by side.

### What's included
- Weekly dark-store availability and fill-rate tracking by city, with out-of-stock alerts before peak days
- Purchase-order forecasting, follow-up, dispatch coordination and receipt confirmation
- Catalogue upkeep: titles with pack size, thumbnails, secondary images, attributes and combo or new SKU additions
- Pricing and promotion planning to margin, including Swiggy sale events, festive campaigns and basket-builder offers
- Instamart ads management — sponsored listings on search and category, and banner placements — to a target ROAS
- Ratings and customer-feedback monitoring with product, packaging and delivery issues routed to the right owner
- Settlement reconciliation: PO versus goods receipt, short receipts, damages, debit notes and ad invoices
- Compliance checks on labelling, MRP, barcodes and shelf-life rules
- Monthly review report covering sales, availability, POs, ads, promotions, ratings and reconciliation

### How we work
1. Audit and baseline — We review listings, availability by city, PO history, ad performance and settlements, then agree the numbers the account is run against.
2. Availability and PO rhythm — A weekly availability check and a PO forecast are set up with your warehouse, timed ahead of weekends, match days and festivals.
3. Content and pricing — Thumbnails, titles and attributes are fixed, pricing checked against margin, and a promotion calendar aligned to Swiggy's events.
4. Ads and visibility — Instamart ad campaigns are structured by SKU and city, run only where stock supports them, and optimised weekly against ROAS.
5. Reconcile and review — Settlements are matched to POs and receipts, disputes raised, and a monthly review brings every number into one report.

### Deliverables
- Weekly availability and fill-rate tracker by city and dark store
- Purchase-order log with forecast, raise, dispatch and receipt dates

Tools & platforms: Instamart Seller Hub, Swiggy Instamart Ads, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, WhatsApp Business, Adobe Photoshop
Pricing model: Monthly management retainer scoped to SKU count, cities and ad activity; Instamart ad spend and platform charges are paid by you directly to Swiggy.

### FAQ
Q: How do you manage availability and fill rate on Instamart?
A: We check availability at dark-store level every week, flag SKUs that are out of stock or low in any city, and measure fill rate as quantity received against quantity ordered on each PO. Because Instamart demand peaks on evenings, weekends and event days, we forecast against those peaks rather than a flat average, and fix fill rate at your warehouse with packaging and dispatch discipline.

Q: How do purchase orders work on Instamart?
A: Swiggy raises POs to its city warehouses based on demand and stock on hand, and the brand dispatches within the PO window. We forecast expected POs from sell-through, chase late ones, coordinate quantities and packaging with your team, track dispatch and receipt, and log short receipts or rejections for dispute.

Q: Do you maintain the catalogue and content?
A: Yes. Titles with pack size, thumbnails, secondary images, attributes and descriptions are kept current, combos and new pack variants added, and listings rechecked after Instamart template changes. Thumbnails are produced in-house to stand out in a fast scroll.

Q: How do you plan pricing and promotions on Instamart?
A: To margin first. We model the discount, Swiggy's share and the expected uplift before committing to a sale event, festive campaign or basket-builder offer, and keep pricing aligned across Blinkit, Zepto and your own store so no channel undercuts another.

Q: Do you run Instamart ads?
A: Yes. Instamart offers sponsored listings on search and category pages and banner placements, and we run them by SKU and city against a target ROAS, weighted towards the hours and days when your category sells. Ads are paused in any city where the SKU is out of stock.

Q: How do you manage ratings on Instamart?
A: Ratings and feedback are monitored weekly, product complaints separated from packaging and delivery issues, and each routed to the right owner. Recurring themes are reported monthly so pack, label or formulation changes can be made before they hurt sell-through.

Q: What does reconciliation involve?
A: Matching Swiggy's settlements to POs, goods receipt notes, short receipts, damages, returns, debit notes and ad or marketing invoices. Discrepancies are raised within the dispute window and tracked to closure so your books reflect what was actually supplied and sold.

Q: What is in the monthly review?
A: Sales and units by city and SKU, availability and fill rate, PO status, catalogue changes, promotions and their margin impact, ad spend and ROAS, ratings trends and the reconciliation summary, followed by decisions on SKUs, cities and budget for the next month.

Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now onboarding is the process of getting a brand's products stocked and visible on the 10-minute delivery services run by Flipkart and Amazon. Unlike Blinkit or Zepto, both are extensions of an existing marketplace: a brand needs an approved seller account with the right brand and category approvals, then enrols into the quick-commerce programme and arranges stock for the platform's local dark stores. Flipkart Minutes launched in 2024 and Amazon Now followed in 2025, and both are still expanding city by city.

gaa-tha runs the whole sequence, starting from wherever you are. If you already sell on Flipkart or Amazon we audit the account, brand approvals and listings, then handle programme enrolment, catalogue adaptation, stocking and go-live. If you do not, we set up the seller account and brand approvals first. Flipkart Minutes reaches beyond grocery into electronics accessories, mobiles, fashion basics and gifting; Amazon Now leans on Amazon's everyday-essentials and beauty range and its Prime base, so we plan the lead SKUs per platform.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need for Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now?
A: The same core pack as the parent marketplaces: GST registration, PAN, bank proof, a trademark certificate or brand authorisation letter, FSSAI licence for food and beverages, and any category licence such as cosmetics approvals. Brand-gated categories on Amazon need Brand Registry or brand approval, and Flipkart needs its brand approval for restricted categories. We share a current checklist per programme.

Q: Do I need an existing Flipkart or Amazon seller account?
A: Yes. Both programmes sit on top of the marketplace seller systems, so an approved seller account with the right category and brand approvals comes first. If you already have one, onboarding is faster; if not, we set it up as the first step and it adds a few weeks.

Q: How long does Flipkart Minutes or Amazon Now onboarding take?
A: Usually 2–5 weeks per platform for an existing seller with approvals in place, and 4–8 weeks if the seller account and brand approvals have to be created first. Programme availability in your category and cities is the main variable, because both services are still opening cities.

Q: Are there fees for Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now?
A: Both run on marketplace commissions plus quick-commerce specific charges or stocking arrangements that vary by category, city and programme and change over time. We do not quote fixed figures; we get the current structure for your category and explain it before you commit.

Q: Which categories work on Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now?
A: Grocery, snacks and beverages, personal care and beauty, baby and pet care, home and kitchen essentials on both. Flipkart Minutes also carries electronics accessories, mobiles, fashion basics and gifting, and Amazon Now draws on Amazon's everyday-essentials and beauty catalogue. We choose lead SKUs per platform rather than copying one range to both.

Q: Which cities are Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now live in?
A: Flipkart Minutes operates in major metros including Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata and Pune and keeps adding cities. Amazon Now launched in Bengaluru and has been expanding to Delhi NCR, Mumbai and further cities. Coverage changes quickly, so we confirm live cities for your category at the time of onboarding.

Q: What happens at go-live?
A: We confirm the quick-commerce listings are live and searchable in each launch city, check pricing, thumbnails and pack-size titles, verify stock is showing as available at the local fulfilment points, and set up the availability tracker. The account then moves into monthly management or to your own team with an SOP.

Q: Should I prioritise Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now over Blinkit and Zepto?
A: If you already sell on Flipkart or Amazon, adding their quick-commerce programmes is the lowest-effort expansion because the seller account, brand approvals and catalogue already exist. If you are new to all of them, Blinkit and Zepto usually come first for grocery and FMCG. We plan the order by platform and city with you.

## Quick Commerce Ads
https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-ads
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs quick commerce ads for brands in India: sponsored search and product listing ads, category placements and banner campaigns on Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart, structured by SKU and city, switched off where stock is out, and optimised weekly against a target ROAS — with spend paid directly to each platform and reported alongside availability and sales.

Best for: FMCG, food and beverage, beauty and personal care brands live on at least one quick-commerce platform
Timeline: Setup in 1–2 weeks, then monthly
Engagement model: Monthly management fee; ad spend paid directly to each platform
Channels/platforms: Blinkit Ads, Zepto Ads, Swiggy Instamart Ads, with Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now via Flipkart Ads and Amazon Ads

### What it is
Quick commerce ads are the paid placements inside 10-minute delivery apps — sponsored products on search results, sponsored slots on category pages and banner placements on the home and category screens — on Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart, with Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now reached through their parent marketplaces' ad systems. Because the shopper is minutes from buying, these ads convert on stock and price as much as on creative, and they only work where the SKU is actually available in that city.

At gaa-tha quick-commerce ads are run by the same team that tracks your availability, so budget follows stock. We structure campaigns by SKU, city and platform, agree a target ROAS from your margin, bid on the search terms shoppers actually type for your category, and pause any city where the product is out of stock. Reporting shows spend, ROAS and sales next to availability and organic rank, because a good ad month on quick commerce is usually a good availability month.

### What's included
- Ad account setup or audit on Blinkit Ads, Zepto Ads and Swiggy Instamart Ads
- Campaign structure by SKU, city and platform with a target ROAS derived from margin
- Keyword research per platform: category terms, competitor terms, occasions and pack-size searches
- Sponsored product and search campaigns with weekly bid and budget optimisation
- Category-page and banner campaigns for launches, festive periods and platform sale events
- Availability-linked pausing so ads do not run in cities where the SKU is out of stock
- Creative for banners and thumbnails produced in-house to each platform's specifications
- Coordination with promotions so ads and offers land in the same week
- Monthly report on spend, ROAS, sales attributed, organic rank movement and availability by city

### How we work
1. Audit and targets — We review current ad accounts, availability by city, margins and past performance, then agree the target ROAS and the SKUs to lead with.
2. Structure and keywords — Campaigns are built by SKU, city and platform, with keyword lists researched per platform and negative terms set from day one.
3. Creative and placements — Banners and thumbnails are produced to each platform's specifications and placements chosen for launches, sale events and always-on search.
4. Launch and optimise — Campaigns go live with daily checks in week one, then weekly optimisation of bids, budgets and keywords, and pausing wherever stock runs out.
5. Report and scale — Monthly reporting on spend, ROAS, sales and rank next to availability, with scaling rules for the SKUs and cities that are working.

### Deliverables
- Configured ad accounts on each platform with campaign naming conventions
- Keyword and negative-keyword lists per platform and category
- Banner and thumbnail creative sets for each campaign
- Weekly optimisation log with availability-linked pauses
- Monthly quick-commerce ads report with spend, ROAS, sales and rank by city

Tools & platforms: Blinkit Ads, Zepto Ads, Swiggy Instamart Ads, Flipkart Ads, Amazon Ads, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, Adobe Photoshop
Pricing model: Monthly management fee scoped to platforms, SKUs and cities; ad spend is paid by you directly to each platform with no markup.

### FAQ
Q: What ad formats are available on Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart?
A: All three offer sponsored product placements on search results and category pages, and banner placements on the home screen and category pages, with some platforms adding brand pages or takeover formats for larger campaigns. Search ads drive most day-to-day sales; banners and category placements suit launches, festive periods and platform sale events. We pick the mix by SKU and objective.

Q: How much should I spend on quick commerce ads?
A: Enough to be visible on your core search terms in your live cities without exceeding what your margin allows — usually a few thousand rupees a day across platforms to start, scaled by city as ROAS holds. We size the budget from your margin and target ROAS rather than a fixed rule, and never spend in a city where the SKU is out of stock.

Q: Do you charge a percentage of ad spend?
A: No. Our fee is a flat monthly management fee scoped to platforms, SKUs and cities. Ad spend is paid by you directly to Blinkit, Zepto or Swiggy from your own ad account, so you always see exactly what was spent.

Q: Why do you link ads to availability?
A: Because on quick commerce a click on an out-of-stock SKU is wasted money and can hurt your rank. We track availability at dark-store level every week and pause campaigns by city as soon as stock runs low, then resume when the next purchase order lands.

Q: How do you measure ROAS on quick commerce?
A: Each platform reports attributed sales against ad spend, and we read it alongside total sales, organic rank and availability so that a rise in ad sales is not simply cannibalising organic ones. Monthly reports show ROAS by platform, SKU and city and the margin left after ads and platform charges.

Q: Can you run ads on Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now?
A: Yes, through Flipkart Ads and Amazon Ads, where quick-commerce listings inherit the marketplace's sponsored-product and display formats. We manage them from the same plan so budget across all five platforms follows availability and margin.

Q: Should I run ads before my listings are stable?
A: Only once thumbnails, titles with pack size and pricing are right and stock is reliable in the target cities. Ads amplify whatever the listing already is; fixing the catalogue first usually costs less and lifts both organic and paid results.

https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content

On quick commerce the shopper scrolls a grid of small tiles on a phone and decides in about two seconds, so a thumbnail has to show the product, the variant and the size at a glance, and a title has to carry the pack size because that is how people search.

gaa-tha builds this content to each platform's specifications from one master library, so the same SKU looks consistent on Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket without six separate shoots. - Attributes, descriptions and category mapping completed for every SKU
- Combo, multipack and pack-size strategy planned with margin and platform price points
- Banner and category-page creative for launches, sale events and quick-commerce ads
- Packshots via studio shoot or AI-assisted production for large or fast-changing ranges
- Master content library so every platform and your own store use the same approved assets

### How we work
1. Audit and specifications — We review your current listings against each platform's requirements and how competitors in your category appear in the grid.
2. Pack and combo strategy — Pack sizes, combos and multipacks are planned with your margin and the price points that move on quick commerce.
3. Shoot and design — Packshots are produced in studio or with AI-assisted production, then thumbnails and secondary images designed and checked at grid size.
4. Titles and attributes — Titles with pack size, descriptions, attributes and category mapping are written per platform and uploaded or handed over in the platform's template.
5. Test and refresh — Click-through and conversion are watched after upload, thumbnails revised where they underperform, and new SKUs, combos and festive variants added monthly.

### Deliverables
- Catalogue audit with platform-by-platform fixes
- Thumbnail and secondary-image sets for every SKU, in each platform's format
- Title, description and attribute sheet per platform
- Combo and pack-size plan with price points
- Banner creative sets for launches and sale events
- Master content library with approved assets

Tools & platforms: Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, Figma, AI image tools, Studio photography, Google Sheets, Blinkit Seller Hub, Zepto Brand Portal
Pricing model: Per-SKU or batch pricing for catalogue creation and a monthly retainer for ongoing updates, scoped to SKU count, platforms and whether a studio shoot is needed.

### FAQ
Q: What makes a good thumbnail on Blinkit, Zepto or Instamart?
A: One that reads at grid size on a phone: a clean packshot filling the frame, the variant and pack size visible, a plain background that meets the platform's specification and no clutter. Shoppers decide in about two seconds, so the thumbnail's job is recognition, not persuasion.

Q: Why should the pack size be in the title?
A: Because shoppers search and compare by size — 200 g, 1 L, pack of 3 — and the app truncates titles on small tiles, so the size has to come early. Titles that lead with brand, product, variant and pack size are also easier for the platform's search to match.

Q: Do you follow each platform's image specifications?
A: Yes. Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket each have their own dimensions, background and content rules, and listings that break them fail QC or get suppressed. We build from one master file and export to each specification so the SKU stays consistent everywhere.

Q: What is combo and pack strategy on quick commerce?
A: Deciding which sizes, multipacks and bundles to list so the basket value works for you and the platform: a trial size for first purchase, a regular size for repeat, and a combo or multipack that lifts order value. We plan it with your margin and the price points that move in your category, and check it against what sells on Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart.

Q: Can you photograph a large catalogue quickly?
A: Yes. For ranges of dozens to hundreds of SKUs we combine a studio shoot for hero products with AI-assisted packshot production for the long tail, keeping art direction human so everything looks like one brand. This is usually the fastest way to get a full catalogue live without a multi-week shoot.

Q: Do you upload the content to the platforms?
A: Yes, where we manage the account, and otherwise we hand over everything in each platform's upload template with a checklist. Either way we recheck the live listings after upload, because platforms crop, compress and reorder images differently.

Q: How often should quick commerce content be refreshed?
A: Review monthly, refresh when a thumbnail underperforms, a pack changes, a festival or season approaches, or the platform updates its template. Combos and seasonal variants usually need new tiles each quarter, and a stale thumbnail is one of the quieter reasons a listing loses rank.

## FAQ

Q: Custom-coded, WordPress, Webflow or Shopify — which should I choose?

## Portfolio & Brand Website Design
https://gaa-tha.com/services/portfolio-brand-website-design
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha designs and builds portfolio websites for designers, architects, photographers, creators, founders and consultants, and launch websites for new brands — story-led case-study layouts, considered motion, fast image-heavy pages and a CMS you can update yourself, custom-coded or on Webflow or WordPress. Most portfolio sites go live in three to five weeks.

Best for: Architects, interior and product designers, photographers, creators, founders, consultants and new brands preparing a launch
Timeline: Personal portfolios 2–4 weeks; studio and brand launch sites 4–8 weeks
Engagement model: Project fee, with an optional monthly care plan for updates
Channels/platforms: Custom-coded (Next.js or Astro), Webflow or WordPress; hosted on Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare or Webflow hosting

### What it is
A portfolio or brand website is a site whose main job is to make someone believe in a person, studio or new brand — through the work, the story behind it and a clear point of view — and then make it easy for the right client, collaborator, employer or investor to get in touch. Unlike a corporate site that lists services, it is judged on taste, pacing and proof: how the work is framed, how quickly the images load and whether a stranger understands what you do within ten seconds.

At gaa-tha these sites start as a story, which is what our name means. We choose the projects that win the work you want next, write each case study as a brief, an approach and an outcome, design the layout around your visuals rather than a template, and add motion only where it helps the story. For new brands, the launch site carries the identity, the founder story and a waitlist or pre-order, ready for the first campaign.

### What's included
- Positioning and project selection — which work to show, in what order, for which audience
- Story-led case-study templates: brief, process, outcome, credits and image or video galleries
- Custom visual design in your identity, or a brand identity created alongside by our branding team
- Considered motion — scroll reveals, page transitions and hover states that stay light and respect reduced-motion settings
- Media handling for image-heavy portfolios: AVIF and WebP, responsive sizes, lazy loading and streamed video
- A CMS for adding projects, press and journal posts without a developer — Webflow CMS, WordPress or a headless CMS such as Sanity
- Brand launch pages: founder story, product teaser, waitlist or pre-order, press kit and social preview images
- Contact and booking flows with WhatsApp, calendar booking or email routing, and spam protection
- Search and AI visibility: Person or Organization structured data, CreativeWork markup for projects, sitemap and llms.txt
- Domain, hosting, analytics and a handover session so you can run the site yourself

### How we work
1. Story and selection — We interview you, review your body of work and the clients you want next, and agree the projects, the narrative and the one action the site should drive.
2. Structure and case studies — The sitemap and case-study structure are planned, and we write or edit each project story with you so it reads as a brief, an approach and an outcome.
3. Design and motion — Home, project and about pages are designed around your visuals, with motion prototyped early so it feels intentional rather than decorative.
4. Build and CMS — The site is built custom-coded or on Webflow or WordPress, the CMS is set up for projects and posts, and media is optimised so heavy pages still load quickly on a phone.
5. Launch and hand over — Domain, SSL, analytics and Search Console are connected, social previews are checked, you are trained on the CMS, and an optional care plan covers later updates.

### Deliverables
- Story outline, sitemap and case-study framework
- Approved designs for home, project, about and contact pages, with motion notes
- Live website on your domain with SSL and optimised media
- CMS set up with your first projects loaded
- Structured data, XML sitemap, social preview images and llms.txt
- Training session, handover document and all logins in your name

Tools & platforms: Figma, Webflow, WordPress, Next.js, Astro, GSAP, Sanity, Vercel, Google Analytics 4
Pricing model: Project fee scoped to the number of page templates and case studies, the depth of motion and whether copy and photography are included; hosting and any platform subscription are paid by you directly.

### FAQ
Q: How much does a portfolio website cost?
A: The cost of a portfolio website depends mainly on whether the design is custom or template-based, how many case studies need writing and laying out, how much motion and video is involved, and which platform it runs on. A single-page personal portfolio and a studio site with a CMS, journal and custom animation are very different jobs, so gaa-tha scopes each one after a short call. Platform subscriptions such as Webflow hosting are billed by the platform, separately from the build.

Q: Webflow, WordPress or custom code — which is best for a portfolio site?
A: Webflow suits most designers and studios who want visual control and an easy CMS; WordPress suits people who publish often or need specific plugins; custom code in Next.js or Astro suits sites with unusual interactions or strict performance goals. The right choice depends on who will update the site and how often, so we recommend after seeing your content and team rather than defaulting to one platform.

Q: Is Behance, Instagram or Dribbble enough, or do I need my own website?
A: Platforms are good for discovery, but your own website is where serious clients check you before they commit. It lets you control the order and story of your work, appear for your name in Google and AI assistants, and send enquiries straight to you instead of into a feed. Most people keep both and link their platform profiles to the site.

Q: How long does a portfolio or brand launch website take?
A: Personal portfolios usually take two to four weeks, and studio or brand launch sites four to eight. The biggest variable is content — choosing projects, collecting high-resolution images and writing case studies — so we draft the stories with you rather than wait for a finished brief.

Q: Will heavy images and animation make my site slow?
A: Not if they are built carefully. We serve modern image formats at the right size for each screen, lazy-load media below the fold, stream video instead of embedding large files, and keep animation light with a reduced-motion fallback. Speed is tested on mid-range phones before launch, because that is where many clients first see your work.

Q: Do you build launch websites for new brands?
A: Yes. A brand launch site usually carries the new identity, the founder story, a product teaser and a waitlist, pre-order or enquiry form, and is ready for the first ad and influencer campaign. If the brand will sell online, we can build it on Shopify from day one so you do not rebuild after launch.

Q: What makes a good portfolio website, and how do I choose who builds it?
A: A good portfolio website shows fewer, stronger projects, explains each one in plain words, loads fast on a phone and makes contacting you obvious. When choosing a designer or agency, look at portfolio sites they have actually built, ask who writes the case studies, check which platform you will be left with, and confirm you will own the domain and logins. gaa-tha writes the case studies with you as part of the project, because that is where most portfolios fall short.

Q: Who owns the website, and can I update it myself?
A: You own it. The domain, hosting account, CMS and code are set up in your name, and every login is handed over at launch. You are trained to add projects, swap images and post updates without a developer, and an optional care plan covers larger changes.


## Web & Mobile App Design
https://gaa-tha.com/services/app-design-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha designs web and mobile apps, admin consoles and analytics dashboards: user flows and wireframes, UI design in Figma, clickable prototypes for user testing, and a developer-ready design system with components and tokens. The same in-house team then builds the web or mobile app, or hands a complete specification to your developers and stays on through build and QA.

Best for: Startups, D2C brands, distributors, real-estate and education businesses that need an app, customer portal, admin console or dashboard
Timeline: UX and UI in 3–6 weeks; web app development 6–12 weeks depending on scope
Engagement model: Project fee by phase (discovery, design, build); optional monthly support
Channels/platforms: Web apps, iOS and Android, admin consoles, dashboards, progressive web apps

### What it is
Web and mobile app design is the work of deciding what an app does for its users and how it feels to use — the flows, screens, states, interactions and visual system — and documenting it so developers can build it exactly. UI is what the user sees; UX is whether they get where they need to go without thinking. Good app design is decided in flows and prototypes, long before code.

At gaa-tha app design is treated as a product problem with a brand on top. We map the jobs the app must do, wireframe the flows, test a clickable prototype with real users, then design the full UI in your identity as a component-based system with tokens developers can implement. Admin consoles and dashboards get the same care, because the people running the business use them every day.

### What's included
- Discovery — users, jobs to be done, business rules, existing systems and success metrics
- User flows, information architecture and low-fidelity wireframes
- Clickable prototype in Figma for user testing and stakeholder sign-off
- UI design for every screen and state — empty, loading, error, success — on mobile and desktop
- Design system with components, colour and type tokens, spacing and icon set
- Admin console and analytics dashboard design, including data tables, filters and charts
- Developer handover — specifications, assets, interaction notes and Figma dev mode access
- Web app development in-house (front end, back end, database, authentication and integrations)
- Design QA during development — by our engineers or yours — and design fixes after launch
- App store listing assets — icons, screenshots and copy — where the app is published

### How we work
1. Discovery — We interview users and stakeholders, list the jobs the app must do and the business rules behind them, and agree scope and success metrics.
2. Flows and wireframes — User flows and low-fidelity wireframes are drawn for every journey, reviewed with your team and corrected before any visual design.
3. Prototype and test — A clickable prototype is tested with a handful of real users; confusion and dead ends are fixed while they are still cheap to fix.
4. UI and design system — Every screen and state is designed in your brand as a component-based system with tokens, ready for development.
5. Build and handover — Our engineers build and launch the web or mobile app from the design system, or we hand specifications and assets to your developers and support them through build and QA.

### Deliverables
- User flows, information architecture and wireframes
- Clickable Figma prototype with user-testing notes
- Full UI designs for all screens and states
- Design system with components and tokens
- Developer handover package (specs, assets, interaction notes)
- Launched web or mobile app, or QA support for your developers

Tools & platforms: Figma, FigJam, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, React, Firebase, Node.js, Google Analytics 4, Notion
Pricing model: Project fee quoted by phase — discovery, design, development — based on the number of screens, roles and integrations; monthly support after launch is optional.

### FAQ
Q: What is UI/UX design?
A: UX (user experience) design decides how an app works — the flows, structure and logic that get a user to their goal without friction. UI (user interface) design decides how it looks — layout, colour, type, components and states. gaa-tha does both, testing the UX in a clickable prototype before the UI is finalised in your brand.

Q: What is the difference between a website and a web app?
A: A website presents information and captures enquiries; a web app lets logged-in users do things — place orders, track jobs, manage inventory, view dashboards. Web apps need user roles, data, integrations and many more screen states, which is why they are designed as systems rather than pages.

Q: How long does app design take?
A: Three to six weeks for UX and UI on a typical app or admin console: about a week each for discovery and flows, one to two for the prototype and testing, and one to three for full UI and the design system. Web app development then takes six to twelve weeks depending on scope and integrations.

Q: Do you develop the app as well as design it?
A: Yes. Web apps, admin consoles, dashboards and iOS and Android apps (Flutter, React Native or native) are built in-house by the same team — see Mobile App Development and SaaS Product Development. If you have your own developers, we deliver a complete developer-ready package and stay on through their build and QA.

Q: How much does app design cost in India?
A: It depends on the number of screens, user roles, integrations and whether you need design only or design plus development, so we quote by phase after a discovery call rather than a flat rate. Design-only engagements can start small with a prototype and grow as the product is validated.

Q: What do we receive at the end?
A: Editable Figma files with flows, prototype, all screens and a design system; a handover package with specifications, assets and interaction notes; and, if we build it, a launched web app with documentation and all credentials in your name.

Q: Can you redesign an existing app or admin panel?
A: Yes. We audit the current product with real users and analytics, keep what works, fix the flows that cause drop-off or support tickets, and rebuild the UI as a consistent system. Redesigns are phased so development can ship improvements without a big-bang relaunch.

Q: Do you design internal tools like admin consoles and dashboards?
A: Yes, and they are often the most valuable work: order-management consoles, distributor portals, sales dashboards and content admins that your team uses every day. For smaller, single-purpose tools see Custom Tools & Automations.


## Mobile App Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/mobile-app-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha develops iOS and Android apps for startups and businesses — in Flutter or React Native for one shared codebase, or native Swift and Kotlin where the product demands it — with the backend and APIs, push notifications, UPI and Razorpay payments, analytics, App Store and Play Store publishing, and maintenance after launch. A focused first version typically ships in eight to fourteen weeks.

Best for: Startups launching an app-first product, D2C and retail brands, service, education and healthcare businesses, and companies moving a web tool onto phones
Timeline: MVP in 8–14 weeks; fuller products in 4–6 months, released in phases
Engagement model: Fixed-scope phases (discovery, design, build) or a monthly product team; optional maintenance retainer
Channels/platforms: iOS and Android via Flutter, React Native or native Swift and Kotlin; Node.js, Firebase or Supabase backends

### What it is
Mobile app development is the work of turning a product idea into an app people install and keep using: deciding what the first release must do, designing the screens, writing the app and the backend it talks to, connecting payments, notifications and analytics, getting it approved on the Apple App Store and Google Play, and keeping it working as phones and operating systems change. The app on the phone is usually half the job; the backend, admin panel and release process are the other half.

At gaa-tha we start by cutting the first version down to the few journeys that prove the idea, then build cross-platform unless there is a clear reason to go native. Design, development, testing and the store launch sit with one in-house team, and every app ships with crash reporting and analytics, so the second release is decided by how people actually use the first.

### What's included
- Product discovery — users, core journeys, MVP scope, platform choice and a phased release plan
- UX flows and UI design for iOS and Android that respect each platform's conventions
- Cross-platform development in Flutter or React Native, or native Swift (SwiftUI) and Kotlin (Jetpack Compose)
- Backend and APIs on Node.js, Firebase or Supabase — authentication, user roles and a database designed to grow
- Admin panel for your team to manage users, content, orders and notifications
- Payments with Razorpay, Cashfree or PayU (UPI intent, cards, wallets), plus Apple and Google in-app purchases where store rules require them
- Push notifications through Firebase Cloud Messaging and Apple Push Notification service, deep links and in-app messages
- Analytics and stability monitoring with Firebase Analytics or Mixpanel, Crashlytics or Sentry, and funnel events for key journeys
- App Store and Play Store publishing — developer accounts, listing copy, screenshots, privacy disclosures and review
- Maintenance — OS and SDK updates, bug fixes, performance monitoring and new feature releases

### How we work
1. Discovery and scope — We map the users and core journeys, choose the platform approach, and agree a first release small enough to ship in weeks rather than months.
2. Design and prototype — Flows and screens are designed and tested as a clickable prototype, so changes happen in Figma, where they are cheap, rather than in code.
3. Build in sprints — The app, backend and admin panel are built in two-week sprints, with a test build on your phone through TestFlight and Play Console testing at the end of each.
4. Test and launch — We test on real budget and flagship devices, fix crashes and edge cases, prepare store listings and privacy details, and take the app through App Store and Play Store review.
5. Measure and maintain — Analytics and crash reports shape the next release, and a maintenance retainer covers OS updates, fixes and new features.

### Deliverables
- MVP scope, user flows and a phased release plan
- Figma designs and a clickable prototype
- iOS and Android apps live on the App Store and Google Play under your developer accounts
- Backend, APIs and admin panel with documentation
- Analytics, crash reporting and push notifications configured
- Full source code in your repository, with build and release instructions

Tools & platforms: Flutter, React Native, Swift, Kotlin, Firebase, Node.js, Supabase, Razorpay, Figma, Sentry
Pricing model: Quoted by phase after discovery, based on screens, user roles, integrations and platforms; developer accounts, hosting and third-party services are paid by you directly, and maintenance is an optional monthly retainer.

### FAQ
Q: How much does it cost to develop a mobile app in India?
A: The cost of a mobile app is driven by the number of screens and user roles, the backend and admin panel, integrations such as payments, maps or an ERP, whether you need one cross-platform codebase or two native apps, and how polished the first release must be. A focused MVP and a marketplace app with three user types sit in very different budgets, so gaa-tha quotes by phase after discovery. Our guide to mobile app development cost in India explains indicative 2026 market ranges.

Q: Flutter or React Native — which should we choose?
A: Both Flutter and React Native are mature ways to build iOS and Android apps from one codebase, and for most business apps either will do the job well. Flutter, from Google and written in Dart, gives very consistent UI and smooth custom animation; React Native, from Meta and written in JavaScript or TypeScript, usually with Expo, suits teams that already work in React or want to share logic with a web app. We go native in Swift and Kotlin when an app leans heavily on device hardware, background processing or the newest platform features.

Q: Do we need a native app, or will a PWA do?
A: A progressive web app (PWA) is enough when people use the product occasionally, mostly arrive through links and do not need deep phone features; it costs less and needs no store approval. A native or cross-platform app is worth it when users return often, or you need dependable push notifications, offline use, in-app payments, hardware such as camera, GPS or Bluetooth, or the trust of being in the App Store and Play Store. Many products start as a web app or PWA and add a store app once retention proves the case.

Q: How long does it take to build and publish an app?
A: A focused MVP usually takes eight to fourteen weeks from discovery to store launch, and larger products four to six months released in phases. Store review typically adds a few days, and new personal Google Play developer accounts must run a closed test before publishing to production, so we set up organisation developer accounts early. A tight first scope and quick approvals matter more to the timeline than team size.

Q: Can the app accept UPI and Razorpay payments?
A: Yes — for physical goods and real-world services an app can use Razorpay, Cashfree or PayU with UPI intent, cards, net banking and wallets. Digital content and subscriptions used inside the app are generally required to go through Apple's and Google's in-app billing, with some regional exceptions, so we confirm the right route for your product before building the checkout.

Q: Who owns the app and the source code?
A: You own the app and its source code. The apps are published under your own Apple and Google developer accounts, the code lives in your Git repository, and cloud accounts are in your company's name. If you change teams later, everything needed to build and release the app goes with you.

Q: Is app maintenance necessary after launch?
A: Yes, app maintenance is necessary, because Apple and Google update their operating systems and store policies every year and the SDKs for payments, maps and notifications change with them. A maintenance retainer covers those updates, crash and bug fixes, security patches, backend monitoring and small improvements. Without it, apps tend to break quietly or get flagged by the stores within a year or two.

Q: How do we choose the best app development company for our project?
A: The best app development company for you is one that has shipped apps to both stores and still maintains them, challenges your scope instead of quoting every feature, and writes code you will own. Ask who designs, who tests on real devices and who handles store review, and whether the backend and admin panel are included. Freelancers suit small, fixed apps; offshore development shops suit large builds where you have strong in-house product management; a design-and-engineering studio such as gaa-tha suits founders who want product, design, development and launch handled together.


## Ecommerce & Sales App Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-app-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds ecommerce and sales apps for brands and distributors: D2C shopping apps connected to Shopify through the Storefront API or to a custom catalogue, B2B ordering apps for retailers and distributors, and field-sales apps with beat plans, order booking, schemes, offline mode and Tally or ERP sync — plus loyalty, push and WhatsApp journeys that bring buyers back.

Best for: D2C brands with strong repeat purchase, FMCG and consumer brands selling through distributors, wholesalers and B2B suppliers, and teams booking orders in the field
Timeline: Shopify-connected shopping apps 6–10 weeks; B2B ordering and field-sales apps 8–16 weeks
Engagement model: Project fee by phase, then an optional monthly maintenance and growth retainer
Channels/platforms: iOS and Android (Flutter or React Native), Shopify Storefront API, Tally Prime, ERP and DMS integrations, WhatsApp Business API

### What it is
Ecommerce and sales app development covers mobile apps that take orders: shopping apps that let consumers browse and buy from a brand directly, B2B ordering apps that let retailers and distributors reorder from their own price lists, and sales-force automation (SFA) apps that field reps use to visit outlets, book orders and log collections. All three share a core — catalogue, prices, cart and order — but each serves a different user with different business rules.

At gaa-tha these apps are built around the system that already runs the business. A D2C app reads products, stock and customers from Shopify so the store and the app never disagree; a B2B or field-sales app syncs with Tally or your ERP so prices, schemes and outstanding balances are right before a rep walks into a shop. Because we also run D2C marketing, push, WhatsApp and loyalty journeys are planned with the app, not bolted on later.

### What's included
- D2C shopping app on Shopify via the Storefront API — collections, search, filters, wishlist, cart and customer accounts in sync with your store
- Custom catalogue backend where there is no Shopify store, with product, price and inventory management
- Checkout with UPI, cards, wallets and COD through Razorpay or your existing checkout provider, with coupons and offers
- B2B ordering app: customer-specific price lists, minimum order quantities, credit limits, quick reorder, order history and invoice downloads
- Field-sales app: beat plans, GPS check-in, outlet onboarding, order booking, schemes and discounts, collections and shelf photos
- Offline mode for weak-network areas, with conflict-safe sync when the phone reconnects
- Tally Prime, ERP and distributor management system (DMS) sync for items, rates, stock, orders and outstanding balances
- Loyalty points, referrals and tiered rewards, with push notifications segmented by buying behaviour
- WhatsApp Business API messages for order confirmations, dispatch updates and reorder reminders
- Manager dashboards for sales by rep, beat, outlet and SKU, plus App Store and Play Store publishing

### How we work
1. Map the order flow — We follow an order from the buyer or rep through to dispatch and invoice, list the rules for prices, schemes, credit and GST, and decide which system is the source of truth.
2. Design for the real user — Screens are designed for the person holding the phone: a shopper on a mid-range Android, a retailer reordering between customers, or a rep with one hand free and patchy signal.
3. Build and integrate — The app, backend and admin are built in sprints, and the Shopify, Tally or ERP, payment and WhatsApp integrations are tested with real data, not samples.
4. Pilot — A shopping app goes first to a small group of loyal customers and a sales app to one territory or a few reps; we fix what they find before the wider rollout.
5. Launch and grow — Store publishing, team training and rollout follow, then push, loyalty and reorder journeys are tuned month by month from usage data.

### Deliverables
- Order-flow map with business rules and an integration plan
- Designed and tested screens for each type of user
- iOS and Android apps published under your developer accounts
- Admin panel and manager dashboard
- Working integrations with Shopify, Tally or ERP, payments and WhatsApp
- Source code, API documentation and rollout training material

Tools & platforms: Flutter, React Native, Shopify Storefront API, Firebase, Node.js, Razorpay, Tally Prime, WhatsApp Business API, Google Maps Platform
Pricing model: Quoted by phase based on the type of app, user roles, integrations and offline needs; platform, messaging and developer-account fees are paid by you directly, and a monthly retainer covers maintenance and growth.

### FAQ
Q: Does my D2C brand need an app, or is the Shopify website enough?
A: Most D2C brands should wait on an app until repeat customers are a meaningful share of revenue, because an app mainly serves people who already buy from you. It earns its cost when products are reordered often — food, beauty, pet care, household essentials — and when push notifications and loyalty can replace part of your remarketing spend. Until then, a fast mobile website and WhatsApp journeys usually return more.

Q: How does a Shopify-connected app stay in sync with my store?
A: A Shopify-connected app reads products, collections, prices, inventory and customer accounts from Shopify's Storefront API, so anything you change in the Shopify admin appears in the app without double entry. Orders placed in the app land in Shopify like any other order, so fulfilment, Shiprocket and your reports keep working as they do today.

Q: Should we use an app builder or build a custom app?
A: A subscription app builder is a sensible start when you want a standard shopping app quickly and your store has no unusual logic. A custom app makes sense when you need your own features — kit builders, subscriptions, B2B pricing, loyalty linked to offline stores — or want to stop paying a fee that grows with your revenue. We compare both against your roadmap before recommending either.

Q: What is a field-sales app, and what does it do?
A: A field-sales or sales-force automation app is what sales reps use on their phones to follow their beat, check in at outlets, show the catalogue, book orders with the right scheme, record payments and capture shelf photos. Managers see orders, visits and productivity by rep and territory as they happen, instead of collecting orders on paper or WhatsApp at the end of the day.

Q: Will the sales app work without internet?
A: Yes. The catalogue, prices, schemes and each rep's outlet list are stored on the phone, orders are saved offline, and everything syncs when the network returns, with checks so the same order is not booked twice. This matters in tier-2 and tier-3 towns, rural beats and inside large stores where signal drops.

Q: Can the app sync orders with Tally or our ERP?
A: Yes. We connect apps to Tally Prime, Zoho, Odoo, ERPNext, SAP Business One or a custom ERP so items, rates, stock, customer balances and orders flow both ways. The method — an API, a connector or a scheduled sync — depends on your system and version, which we check during discovery.

Q: How long does an ecommerce or sales app take, and what drives the cost?
A: A Shopify-connected shopping app usually takes six to ten weeks, and a B2B ordering or field-sales app eight to sixteen. Cost is driven by the number of user roles, the depth of Tally or ERP integration, offline sync, pricing and scheme rules, and how much loyalty and reporting the first release needs. We scope a pilot version first so you see the app working before committing to the full build.

Q: Who owns the app, the code and the customer data?
A: You own all of it. The apps are published under your developer accounts, the backend runs in cloud accounts in your name, and the source code is handed over in your repository. Customer and sales data stays in your systems rather than a shared platform.


## SaaS Product Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/saas-product-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds SaaS products for founders and businesses turning an idea or internal tool into software they sell: idea validation and MVP, multi-tenant architecture, authentication and roles, subscription billing with Stripe or Razorpay, admin and analytics, AI features, cloud and DevOps on AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel or Firebase, and security practices that stand up to customer reviews.

Best for: Founders validating a SaaS idea, funded startups needing an MVP or a rebuilt v2, and established businesses productising an internal tool or their expertise
Timeline: Validation 2–4 weeks; MVP 10–16 weeks; continuous releases after launch
Engagement model: Fixed phases for validation and MVP, then a monthly product-team retainer
Channels/platforms: Web apps in Next.js and React, Node.js or Python APIs, PostgreSQL, AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel, Firebase and Supabase

### What it is
SaaS product development is the work of building software that many customers use on subscription: one codebase serving many separate accounts, called tenants, each with its own users, roles, data and billing plan, running reliably in the cloud and improving through frequent releases. Beyond features, a SaaS product needs sign-up and onboarding, billing and invoicing, an internal admin, usage analytics, security and room to scale without a rewrite.

At gaa-tha we treat the first months as a search for proof, not a build of everything. We test the problem with real buyers, ship the smallest product someone will pay for, and design the foundations — tenancy, data model, auth and billing — so the next hundred customers do not force a rebuild. For Indian founders selling abroad and international founders building with an Indian team, billing, tax and data-protection choices are made early, because they are expensive to change later.

### What's included
- Idea validation — problem interviews, competitor and pricing research, landing-page and waitlist tests
- MVP scoping, user flows and UI design, with a design system that scales to later features
- Multi-tenant architecture: tenant isolation, data model, row-level security and per-tenant settings
- Authentication and authorisation — email, Google and SSO sign-in, organisations, roles and permissions
- Subscription billing with Stripe, Razorpay Subscriptions, Chargebee or Paddle — plans, trials, usage-based pricing, invoices and GST or VAT handling
- Internal admin console, customer-support tools and product analytics with PostHog or Mixpanel
- AI features using Claude, GPT or Gemini — search and answers over customer data, summaries, drafting and AI agents — with cost and safety controls
- Cloud infrastructure on AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel, Firebase or Supabase, with CI/CD, staging and infrastructure as code
- Security and privacy practices aligned with SOC 2, GDPR and India's DPDP Act — audit logs, encryption, backups and access reviews
- Monitoring, performance tuning and scaling as usage grows

### How we work
1. Validate — We test the problem and the price with real prospects through interviews, a landing page and, where useful, a manual or no-code prototype, before any production code is written.
2. Scope and architect — The MVP is cut to the workflows that prove value, and tenancy, data model, auth, billing and cloud choices are made with the next two years in mind.
3. Design — Onboarding, core workflows, settings and billing screens are designed and prototyped so a first-time user reaches value in the first session.
4. Build and ship — The product is built in two-week sprints with automated tests, staging and CI/CD, and released to design partners before a public launch.
5. Measure and scale — Product analytics, support tickets and revenue data drive the roadmap, while security, performance and infrastructure are hardened as customers arrive.

### Deliverables
- Validation report with interview notes, pricing hypothesis and MVP scope
- Architecture document covering tenancy, data model, auth, billing and cloud
- Figma designs and a product design system
- Live SaaS application with billing, admin console and analytics
- CI/CD pipeline, staging and production environments, monitoring and backups
- Source code, technical documentation and a security practices handbook, all in your accounts

Tools & platforms: Next.js, React, Node.js, Python, PostgreSQL, Stripe, Razorpay Subscriptions, AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel
Pricing model: Validation and MVP are quoted as fixed phases after a discovery call; ongoing development runs as a monthly product-team retainer, and cloud, billing and third-party API costs are paid by you directly.

### FAQ
Q: How much does it cost to build a SaaS MVP?
A: The cost of a SaaS MVP depends on the number of core workflows, user roles and integrations, whether billing is simple plans or usage-based, how much AI is involved, and the level of security your buyers expect. A single-workflow tool for small businesses and an enterprise product with SSO and audit logs are very different builds. gaa-tha quotes validation and MVP as fixed phases after discovery, and our SaaS product development guide covers what moves the number.

Q: How long does it take to launch a SaaS product?
A: A SaaS MVP typically takes ten to sixteen weeks to build after two to four weeks of validation and scoping. The fastest launches cut the first version to one workflow that a specific customer will pay for, then add the rest once real usage data arrives.

Q: Which tech stack do you use for SaaS products?
A: Our default SaaS stack is TypeScript end to end — Next.js or React on the front end, Node.js APIs and PostgreSQL — with Python where AI or data work is central, hosted on AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel or Supabase depending on scale and team. We pick well-supported, widely used tools so you can hire for them later, and document every choice.

Q: What is multi-tenant architecture, and do we need it?
A: Multi-tenant architecture means one application serves many customer organisations while keeping each one's data separate.
