Almost every SaaS product needs it; the real question is how strict the separation is — a shared database with tenant-level security for most products, or separate schemas or databases for customers with stricter requirements. Getting this right at the start avoids a painful migration later.

Q: Which billing setup should a SaaS company in India use?
A: Indian SaaS companies commonly use Razorpay Subscriptions with UPI Autopay and card mandates for domestic customers, and Razorpay's international payments, Paddle as a merchant of record, or Stripe where their entity is eligible for overseas customers. The right setup depends on where your company is registered, where customers are and how much tax handling you want to outsource. Eligibility and RBI recurring-payment rules change, so we confirm current terms with each provider before wiring billing.

Q: Will the product be SOC 2, GDPR or DPDP compliant?
A: Compliance is something your company achieves through an audit or assessment, not something code alone provides, but we build with the practices those frameworks expect: access controls, encryption, audit logs, backups, retention rules, consent records and documented processes. That makes a SOC 2 audit, a GDPR review or India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) obligations far easier when customers start asking. We do not issue certifications; we prepare the product and the paperwork for your auditor.

Q: Can you add AI features to our SaaS product?
A: Yes. We add AI where it saves users real time — answering questions over their own data, drafting, classification, summaries and agents that complete multi-step tasks — using Claude, GPT or Gemini models through their APIs. Each feature ships with usage limits, cost tracking, evaluation tests and tenant-level data separation, so AI does not become an uncontrolled bill or a data leak.

Q: Who owns the code and IP, and what happens after launch?
A: You own the code, the IP and every cloud and billing account from day one; the repository and infrastructure sit in your organisation. After launch most clients keep a monthly product-team retainer for releases, monitoring and scaling, while some move development in-house — the system is documented so that handover is straightforward.


# AI & Software Engineering
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-software-engineering

AI agents, automations, ERPs and systems that run the business.

AI & Software Engineering is the gaa-tha practice that builds the systems behind a business: AI agents that research, qualify, reply and act; AI workflow automations across your apps; AI chatbots for websites and WhatsApp; custom ERPs and Odoo or ERPNext implementations; and custom software, APIs and integrations that connect sales, inventory, accounts and operations.

## FAQ
Q: What does an AI and software engineering agency do?
A: It designs and builds the software that runs a business rather than markets it: AI agents and chatbots, automated workflows between apps, ERP systems for inventory, production and accounts, and custom software and integrations. gaa-tha scopes each system around a measurable business outcome, builds it in phases and hands over the code, accounts and documentation.

Q: What is the difference between an AI agent, a chatbot and an automation?
A: An automation follows fixed rules (when a form is filled, add a row and send a WhatsApp). A chatbot answers questions in a conversation. An AI agent is given a goal and tools — your CRM, catalogue, email or ERP — and decides the steps itself, within the guardrails and approvals you set. Many real systems combine all three.

Q: Do we need a custom ERP or an off-the-shelf one like Odoo or ERPNext?
A: Most small and mid-sized businesses should start with Odoo or ERPNext configured to their process, plus custom modules where the business is genuinely different. A fully custom ERP makes sense when your workflow is your competitive advantage or off-the-shelf licences and workarounds cost more than building. We recommend after mapping your process.

Q: Which AI models and tools do you build with?
A: We are model-agnostic: Claude, GPT, Gemini and open-source models are chosen per task on accuracy, cost, speed and data-residency needs, and orchestrated with tools such as n8n, Make, LangGraph or custom code. Your data stays in your accounts, and every agent is logged and evaluated.

Q: Is our business data safe with AI systems?
A: Systems are built with role-based access, encrypted connections, audit logs and human approval for sensitive actions, and use model providers' business terms that do not train on your data. Customer data stays in your own cloud accounts, and we document exactly what each agent can read and do.

Q: How long does an AI agent or ERP project take?
A: A focused AI agent or automation is usually live in two to six weeks. An Odoo or ERPNext implementation takes six to sixteen weeks depending on modules and data migration, and a custom ERP or software platform is delivered in phases, with the first module live in eight to twelve weeks.


## AI Agent Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-agent-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds custom AI agents for businesses in India and abroad: sales and lead-qualification agents, customer-support agents, research agents, operations agents that check orders, stock and reports, and marketing content agents. Each runs on Claude, GPT, Gemini or an open-source model, connects to your systems through tool calling and MCP, and works within guardrails, approvals and logs.

Best for: Sales, support and operations teams with repeatable knowledge work — D2C brands, manufacturers, distributors, B2B services and SaaS companies
Timeline: Pilot agent live in 2–6 weeks; wider rollout in phases after evaluation
Engagement model: Fixed fee per agent, then an optional monthly plan for monitoring, evaluation and improvements
Channels/platforms: Claude, GPT, Gemini and open-source models; MCP servers, RAG, LangGraph or custom orchestration; CRM, ERP, email, Slack and WhatsApp

### What it is
AI agent development is the design and engineering of software that is given a goal, works out the steps, and uses tools — your CRM, catalogue, inbox, ERP or the web — to complete the task, asking a person for approval where the stakes are high. A chatbot answers and an automation follows fixed rules; an agent decides what to do next based on what it finds.

At gaa-tha every agent starts as a written job description: what it may read, which actions it may take, what it must escalate and how success is measured. We choose the model per task, connect tools through function calling and MCP servers, ground answers in your documents with retrieval (RAG), and ship with an evaluation set, cost limits and a trace of every step, so you can always see why the agent did what it did.

### What's included
- Use-case discovery — candidate tasks ranked by volume, value, risk and the data available
- Agent job description: goal, permitted tools and actions, escalation rules and success measures
- Model selection across Claude, GPT, Gemini and open-source models such as Llama, Mistral or Qwen, tested on your own examples
- Tool use and function calling into your CRM, ERP, Shopify store, Google Workspace, email and WhatsApp
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that expose your systems to agents in a standard, permissioned way
- Retrieval (RAG) over company documents — catalogues, SOPs, policies, contracts and past tickets — with source citations
- Orchestration with LangGraph or custom code for multi-step and multi-agent workflows
- Guardrails and human-in-the-loop approvals for refunds, discounts, outbound messages and data changes
- Evaluation sets, tracing and run logs, with accuracy and cost reporting
- Cost control through model routing, prompt caching, token budgets and rate limits, plus documentation and handover

### How we work
1. Pick the job — We map one workflow with the people who do it today and choose the task where an agent saves the most time at an acceptable level of risk.
2. Design and benchmark — We write the agent's job description, collect real past cases as an evaluation set and test candidate models against it before building anything.
3. Build and connect — Tools, MCP servers, retrieval and orchestration are built with permissions, guardrails and approval steps wired in from the first version.
4. Pilot with a human in the loop — The agent works on live tasks while a person approves its actions; we study the traces, fix failure cases and tune prompts, tools and cost.
5. Roll out and monitor — Approvals are relaxed only where accuracy is proven, monitoring and alerts go live, and an optional monthly plan covers model updates, new tools and re-evaluation.

### Deliverables
- Use-case shortlist and agent job description
- Working agent deployed in your own cloud and model-provider accounts
- Tool integrations and MCP servers for your systems
- Evaluation set with baseline accuracy and cost-per-task report
- Tracing, run logs and an approvals view for your team
- Architecture, prompt and runbook documentation, with all credentials

Tools & platforms: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Open-source models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen), Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, Python and Node.js, pgvector and vector databases, n8n, Langfuse
Pricing model: Fixed fee per agent from a written scope; model and API usage is billed to your own provider accounts, and monitoring and improvement run on an optional monthly plan.

### FAQ
Q: What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot or an automation?
A: An AI agent is software that is given a goal and a set of tools and decides the steps itself to reach it. A chatbot answers questions in a conversation, and an automation follows fixed if-this-then-that rules; an agent can look up a CRM record, check stock, draft a reply and ask for approval without each step being scripted. Most production systems combine all three, with the agent handling only the steps that need judgement.

Q: What kinds of AI agents can gaa-tha build?
A: We build lead-qualification and sales agents that research inbound enquiries and draft follow-ups, support agents that resolve order and policy questions, research agents that compile market or competitor briefs, operations agents that check order status and inventory and generate reports, and content agents that draft listings and posts in your brand voice. Each starts with one narrow job and expands once it performs on measured tests.

Q: Which AI model is best for building an agent — Claude, GPT or Gemini?
A: There is no single best model; the right choice depends on the task, so we test candidates on your own examples before deciding. Claude, GPT and Gemini differ in tool use, long-document handling, language coverage, speed and price, and smaller or open-source models are often good enough for classification and extraction at a fraction of the cost. We build model-agnostic so you can switch when a better or cheaper model ships.

Q: How much does an AI agent cost to build and run?
A: Build cost is driven by the number of tools and systems the agent connects to, the data preparation and retrieval it needs, the approval and security requirements, and how many edge cases must be handled. Running cost is mostly model usage per task, which we control with model routing, caching and token budgets and report monthly. A narrow agent on one system costs far less than a multi-agent workflow spanning ERP, CRM and WhatsApp.

Q: Is our data safe, and will the AI models train on it?
A: Agents are built on the paid API and business tiers of the major model providers, which by default do not use your inputs to train their models; free consumer apps can have different terms, so we never build on them. Agents run in your own cloud and provider accounts, read only what their permissions allow, and log every action. For highly sensitive data we can use region-specific hosting or an open-source model on your own servers.

Q: How do you deal with hallucinations and accuracy?
A: AI agents can make mistakes, so accuracy is engineered and measured rather than assumed. We ground answers in your documents with citations, restrict actions to defined tools, instruct the agent to say when it does not know, and re-run an evaluation set of real cases after every change. High-impact actions such as refunds, price changes or outbound messages stay behind human approval until measured accuracy justifies relaxing it.

Q: Who owns the agent, the prompts and the code?
A: You do. Code, prompts, evaluation sets and MCP servers live in a repository in your name, model and cloud accounts are yours, and everything is documented at handover. You can run, change or move the agent without gaa-tha.

Q: How do I choose an AI agent development company?
A: Choose a team that starts from a business process rather than a model, shows how it measures accuracy, explains cost per task, and builds in your accounts with no lock-in. Ask how they handle permissions, approvals and logging, which models they tested for your use case, and what happens when a model is updated or retired. Be cautious of anyone promising full autonomy or guaranteed results before seeing your data.


## AI Workflow Automation
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-workflow-automation
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds AI workflow automations that connect your apps and add AI where a person used to read, sort or type: lead routing and enrichment, invoice and document extraction, email triage, report generation, content pipelines, CRM clean-up and WhatsApp follow-ups. We build on n8n, Make, Zapier or custom code, across Google Workspace, Zoho, HubSpot, Tally and Shopify.

Best for: Teams moving data between apps by hand — sales and marketing operations, accounts, D2C operations, agencies and back offices
Timeline: First workflows live in 1–4 weeks; larger programmes delivered in batches
Engagement model: Fixed fee per workflow or batch, with an optional monthly run-and-improve plan
Channels/platforms: n8n (self-hosted or cloud), Make, Zapier and custom code; Google Workspace, Zoho, HubSpot, Tally, Shopify and WhatsApp

### What it is
AI workflow automation is the use of automation platforms or code to move data between business apps whenever something happens — a new lead, an email, an uploaded invoice, an order — with AI models handling the steps that used to need a person to read, classify, extract or write. The workflow stays predictable; the AI step does the reading and drafting inside it.

At gaa-tha we list every manual hand-off in a process, automate the rule-based parts first and add AI only where it earns its place, with confidence checks that send unclear cases to a person. The platform is chosen on volume, data sensitivity and budget — n8n for self-hosting and control, Make or Zapier for speed and breadth of connectors, custom code for heavy or sensitive workloads — and every workflow ships with error alerts and a run log.

### What's included
- Process audit — each manual hand-off, how often it happens and what it costs in hours and errors
- Lead capture, routing and enrichment from website forms, Meta and Google lead ads, IndiaMART and email into your CRM
- Invoice, purchase-order and document extraction into Tally, Zoho Books or Google Sheets, with a review queue for exceptions
- Email and shared-inbox triage — classify, tag, summarise, draft replies and assign to the right person
- Scheduled reports that pull from Shopify, ad accounts, CRM and accounts and arrive as a written summary on email or WhatsApp
- Content pipelines from brief to draft to approval to publishing, for blogs, product listings and social posts
- CRM hygiene in HubSpot or Zoho CRM: de-duplication, missing-field enrichment, stage updates and follow-up reminders
- WhatsApp follow-ups for leads, quotes, abandoned carts, payments and dispatch through the WhatsApp Business API
- Platform setup on n8n (self-hosted or cloud), Make, Zapier or custom code, with credentials held in your accounts
- Error handling, retries, failure alerts, run logs and documentation for every workflow

### How we work
1. Map the hand-offs — We walk through the process with the people who run it and list every place where data is copied, checked or chased by hand.
2. Prioritise and design — Workflows are ranked by time saved and risk, and each gets a short design: trigger, steps, AI prompts, exceptions and who reviews what.
3. Build on the right platform — We build in n8n, Make, Zapier or code, connect your apps, and test every AI step on a sample of your real emails, invoices or leads.
4. Run in shadow mode — The workflow runs alongside the manual process for a short period so outputs can be compared and edge cases fixed before it takes over.
5. Switch over and maintain — The workflow goes live with alerts and a run log, your team is trained, and an optional monthly plan covers fixes when an app changes and new workflows as you grow.

### Deliverables
- Process audit and a ranked automation backlog
- Live workflows on your n8n, Make, Zapier or cloud account
- AI prompts and extraction schemas tested on your sample data
- Review queues for low-confidence cases
- Failure alerts, run logs and a cost-per-run estimate
- Workflow documentation, team training and all credentials

Tools & platforms: n8n, Make, Zapier, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Google Workspace and Apps Script, Zoho and HubSpot, TallyPrime, WhatsApp Business API
Pricing model: Fixed fee per workflow or batch of workflows; platform subscriptions, AI usage and WhatsApp messaging are billed to your own accounts, and monthly maintenance is optional.

### FAQ
Q: What is AI workflow automation?
A: AI workflow automation connects your business apps so data moves automatically when something happens, with an AI model handling the steps that need reading or judgement, such as extracting an invoice, classifying an email or drafting a reply. It differs from an AI agent because the steps are fixed in advance; the AI works inside a predictable workflow rather than deciding what to do next. That predictability is why it is usually the safest first use of AI in a business.

Q: n8n vs Make vs Zapier — which should we use?
A: Use Zapier for the fastest setup and the widest range of app connectors, Make for visual multi-step logic at a lower cost per run on many workloads, and n8n when you want self-hosting, custom code steps and control over where data goes. Zapier and Make bill by tasks or operations, so cost rises with volume; self-hosted n8n trades licence cost for running and maintaining your own server, or you can use n8n Cloud. Check each platform's current pricing, as plans change often.

Q: Which processes should we automate first?
A: Start with high-volume, rule-heavy tasks where a mistake is easy to spot: lead routing, invoice data entry, daily or weekly reports and follow-up reminders. These pay back quickly and build trust in the system. Processes that need negotiation, judgement on money or sensitive customer conversations are better left with a person, or automated only up to a draft for approval.

Q: Can AI read our invoices and post them into Tally?
A: Yes. AI extraction can read PDF or photographed invoices, pull the vendor, GSTIN, line items, tax and totals, validate them and post entries into TallyPrime, Zoho Books or a sheet. Tally is connected through its integration interface or a connector, depending on how your Tally is set up, and low-confidence documents go to a review queue so a person checks the exceptions rather than every invoice.

Q: How accurate is AI extraction and classification?
A: Accuracy is high on clean, consistent documents and lower on handwritten, poorly scanned or unusual formats, so we measure it on your own samples before go-live. Each AI step is backed by validation rules — totals must add up, a GSTIN must match its format, a lead must have a phone or email — and anything that fails goes to a person. Error and exception rates are visible in the run log, not just in a demo.

Q: What does AI workflow automation cost?
A: Build cost depends on the number of workflows, the apps involved, how many AI steps need testing and how exceptions are handled. Running cost depends on volume, your automation platform plan and AI model usage. We quote a fixed fee per workflow or batch and estimate the monthly running cost before you approve, so you can weigh it against the hours saved.

Q: Is our data safe in these automations?
A: Yes, when the workflow is designed for it: credentials stay in your accounts, data passes only through platforms you approve, and AI steps use provider API terms under which inputs are not used for model training by default. For sensitive financial or customer data, self-hosted n8n on your own server or cloud keeps the whole data path inside your infrastructure, which also helps with obligations under India's DPDP Act and similar laws abroad.

Q: Who maintains the workflows when an app changes?
A: Apps update their APIs and fields, so workflows need occasional fixes, and failure alerts tell you the moment a run breaks. You can maintain workflows in-house with the documentation and training we provide, or use our optional monthly plan for fixes, monitoring and small new workflows. Everything runs in your accounts, so there is no lock-in.


## AI Chatbot Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-chatbot-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds AI chatbots for websites and the WhatsApp Business API, trained on your catalogue, FAQs and policies. They recommend products, track orders, capture and qualify leads, reply in English, Hindi, Gujarati or Hinglish, and hand the conversation to your team when a person is needed — with Shopify integration and analytics on what customers actually ask.

Best for: D2C and Shopify brands, retailers, real-estate, education and service businesses answering the same questions on WhatsApp and the website every day
Timeline: Website bot in 2–4 weeks; WhatsApp bot in 3–6 weeks including Meta business verification and template approval
Engagement model: Fixed setup fee, then an optional monthly plan for content updates, tuning and analytics
Channels/platforms: Website chat widget, WhatsApp Business API and Instagram DMs; Shopify, CRM and helpdesk integrations

### What it is
An AI chatbot is a conversational assistant on your website or WhatsApp that answers customer questions in natural language using a large language model grounded in your own content — catalogue, FAQs, shipping and return policies — and that can look up live data such as order status or stock. A well-built one answers only from approved sources, admits when it does not know and passes the customer to a person instead of guessing.

At gaa-tha a chatbot project starts from your real customer conversations: we read past WhatsApp chats, emails and tickets to find the questions that repeat, then build the knowledge base, the flows for orders and leads, and the handoff rules. The bot is tested in English and the Indian languages your customers write in, connected to Shopify or your CRM, and reviewed every week in its first month using the conversation analytics.

### What's included
- Conversation audit — the top questions, intents and drop-off points from your existing chats and tickets
- Knowledge base built from your catalogue, FAQs, size guides and shipping, return and warranty policies, with retrieval (RAG)
- Website chat widget styled to your brand, on Shopify, WordPress or a custom-coded site
- WhatsApp Business API setup through Meta's Cloud API or a Business Solution Provider, with message templates and opt-in flows
- Product recommendation and guided selling from live catalogue data
- Order tracking, COD confirmation and return-request flows connected to Shopify and your shipping partner
- Lead capture and qualification pushed to your CRM, a sheet or your sales team on WhatsApp
- Replies in English, Hindi, Gujarati and Hinglish, in a tone set to your brand
- Human handoff to a shared inbox with full conversation context, plus business-hours rules
- Analytics on conversation volume, resolution rate, handoffs, unanswered questions and leads captured

### How we work
1. Read the conversations — We study your past chats, tickets and FAQs to list the questions that repeat and the ones that must always go to a person.
2. Build the knowledge and flows — Approved content is structured into a knowledge base, and flows are designed for recommendations, order tracking, lead capture and handoff.
3. Connect channels and systems — The bot is connected to your website, WhatsApp Business API number, Shopify, CRM and helpdesk, and message templates are submitted for Meta's approval.
4. Test in every language — Your team tests the bot with real questions in English, Hindi, Gujarati and Hinglish, including awkward and off-topic ones, and answers are corrected before launch.
5. Launch and tune — The bot goes live, unanswered questions and handoffs are reviewed weekly, and the knowledge base is updated as products, prices and policies change.

### Deliverables
- Conversation audit and intent map
- Live chatbot on your website and WhatsApp number
- Knowledge base and approved WhatsApp message templates
- Shopify, CRM and helpdesk integrations
- Handoff inbox and escalation rules
- Analytics dashboard, admin training and all credentials

Tools & platforms: WhatsApp Business API, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Shopify, Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), n8n, Firebase, Zoho CRM and HubSpot
Pricing model: Fixed setup fee based on channels, languages and integrations; WhatsApp messaging charges, provider fees and AI usage are billed to your own accounts, and monthly tuning is optional.

### FAQ
Q: What is the difference between an AI chatbot and a rule-based chatbot?
A: A rule-based chatbot follows pre-written menus and keywords, while an AI chatbot understands free-text questions and answers them in natural language from your own content. Rule-based bots break when a customer phrases something unexpectedly; AI bots handle variety but need grounding and testing so they stay accurate. We usually combine both — buttons for structured tasks such as order tracking, and AI for open questions.

Q: Can the chatbot run on WhatsApp?
A: Yes, through the official WhatsApp Business API with a verified business; the free WhatsApp Business app only offers simple greeting, away and quick-reply messages, not a real bot. Meta charges for business-initiated template messages by category, while replies to customers who message you first are generally free within the customer-service window — check Meta's current rates for India. Meta's policies also require the bot to serve your own customers, for support, orders or leads, rather than act as a general-purpose AI assistant.

Q: Can it reply in Hindi, Gujarati and Hinglish?
A: Yes. Current models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google handle Hindi, Gujarati and mixed Hinglish well, and the bot replies in the language the customer writes in. We test with the phrasing your customers actually use, including Hindi typed in Roman script, and keep product names and prices exactly as they appear in your catalogue.

Q: Will the chatbot make things up?
A: It is built not to: answers come only from your approved knowledge base and live data, and the bot is instructed to say it does not know and hand over rather than guess. We test it with off-topic and trick questions before launch and review unanswered questions weekly. Prices, stock and order status are read live from Shopify or your system, never from the model's memory.

Q: Does it integrate with Shopify?
A: Yes. The bot can read your Shopify catalogue for recommendations, look up order and fulfilment status for tracking questions, confirm COD orders and send cart reminders on WhatsApp to customers who have opted in. It can also pass on shipping updates from partners such as Shiprocket or Delhivery where their APIs allow.

Q: How much does an AI chatbot cost?
A: Setup cost depends on the channels (website, WhatsApp or both), the number of languages, the size of the catalogue and knowledge base, and integrations with Shopify, a CRM or a helpdesk. Running costs are WhatsApp message charges, any provider platform fee and AI model usage per conversation, all billed to your own accounts. We estimate the monthly running cost from your current chat volume before you commit.

Q: Can a person take over the conversation?
A: Yes, and they should for complaints, custom orders and high-value leads. Handoff rules send the chat to your team's shared inbox with the full conversation and customer details, the bot pauses while a person replies, and outside business hours it collects details and sets a callback.

Q: Is customer data safe with an AI chatbot?
A: Yes, when it is set up properly: conversations are stored in your accounts, access is role-based, and AI providers are used under API terms that do not train on your data by default. We collect only what each flow needs, show opt-in and privacy notices on WhatsApp and the website, and set retention rules so old chats are not kept indefinitely.


## ERP Development & Implementation
https://gaa-tha.com/services/erp-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha develops custom ERPs and implements and customises Odoo and ERPNext for manufacturers, distributors, FMCG, retail and service businesses. We map your processes first, then set up inventory, purchase, production and BOM, sales, dispatch, GST invoicing, accounts or Tally integration, HR and payroll, dashboards and mobile access — with data migration and training included.

Best for: Manufacturers, distributors, FMCG and food brands, multi-outlet retailers and service businesses outgrowing Tally, spreadsheets and disconnected apps
Timeline: Odoo or ERPNext in 6–16 weeks by scope; custom ERP in phases, with the first module live in 8–12 weeks
Engagement model: Phased project fee per module, then a monthly or annual support plan
Channels/platforms: Odoo (Community or Enterprise), ERPNext on Frappe, custom builds; Tally, Shopify, marketplace, bank and logistics integrations

### What it is
ERP development and implementation is the work of putting one system at the centre of a business — purchase, inventory, production, sales, dispatch, invoicing, accounts and people — so every department works from the same data instead of separate spreadsheets. Implementation configures an existing ERP such as Odoo or ERPNext to your process; development builds custom modules, or a whole ERP, where your process does not fit a standard product.

At gaa-tha an ERP project is system engineering before it is software: we map how orders, materials and money actually move, design the target process and data model, decide what stays in Tally or other tools and how it integrates, and only then configure or code. Rollout is phased module by module, with data migration, parallel runs and role-wise training, so the business keeps running while the system changes.

### What's included
- Process mapping and gap analysis across purchase, stores, production, sales, dispatch, accounts and HR
- Platform recommendation — Odoo, ERPNext, a custom build or a hybrid — with a licence and running-cost comparison
- Inventory and warehousing: multi-location stock, batches and expiry, serial numbers, barcodes and reorder levels
- Purchase, vendor management and goods receipt, with approval workflows
- Production: bills of materials (BOM), work orders, job work, material consumption and costing
- Sales, distributor and dealer orders, price lists and schemes, dispatch, delivery challans and e-way bills
- GST invoicing, e-invoicing and return-ready reports, with accounts in the ERP or integrated with Tally
- HR, attendance and payroll, plus role-based dashboards for owners, managers and the shop floor
- Mobile access for sales teams, warehouses and approvals, and integrations with Shopify, marketplaces, banks and logistics
- Data migration from Tally, Excel or an old ERP, user training, documentation and post-go-live support

### How we work
1. Map the business — We sit with each department to document how orders, materials and money move today, where data is re-entered and which reports owners actually use.
2. Design the system — We design the target process, data model, roles, integrations and reports, and recommend Odoo, ERPNext or a custom build with a phased plan.
3. Configure and build — Modules are configured and custom features developed in sprints, with a working demo on your own data at the end of each one.
4. Migrate and run in parallel — Masters, opening stock and balances are cleaned and migrated, and the new system runs alongside the old one until the numbers reconcile.
5. Go live and support — Users are trained by role, the old process is switched off module by module, and a support plan covers fixes, changes, upgrades and new modules.

### Deliverables
- Process maps, gap analysis and a solution design document
- Configured or custom ERP on your cloud account or servers
- Custom modules, reports and print formats for invoices, challans and labels
- Integrations with Tally, Shopify, marketplaces, banks or logistics partners
- Migrated and reconciled master data and opening balances
- Role-wise training, user manuals, admin documentation and credentials

Tools & platforms: Odoo, ERPNext and Frappe, Python, PostgreSQL and MariaDB, TallyPrime, Flutter, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, Power BI and Looker Studio, Docker
Pricing model: Phased project fee per module based on the process map; ERP licences where applicable, hosting and third-party connectors are paid by you directly, and support runs on a monthly or annual plan.

### FAQ
Q: Custom ERP vs Odoo vs ERPNext vs Tally — which is right for us?
A: Tally is accounting and inventory software that most Indian accountants know, Odoo and ERPNext are full ERPs that cover operations end to end, and a custom ERP fits when your process is genuinely unusual or is your competitive edge. Many small and mid-sized businesses do best with Odoo or ERPNext for operations, using either its built-in accounting or a Tally integration so the accountant keeps working in Tally. We recommend after mapping your process, not before.

Q: What is the difference between Odoo and ERPNext?
A: Both are open-source ERPs with strong inventory, manufacturing and accounting modules and Indian GST support. Odoo has a large app ecosystem and a polished interface, and comes in a free Community edition and a paid per-user Enterprise edition, with some features — including full accounting — reserved for Enterprise. ERPNext, built on the Frappe framework, is fully open source with no per-user licence and uses the India Compliance app for GST, which suits businesses with many users who are comfortable self-hosting or paying for managed hosting.

Q: How long does an ERP implementation take?
A: An Odoo or ERPNext implementation typically takes six to sixteen weeks, depending on the number of modules, locations and customisations and the state of your data. A custom ERP is built in phases, with the first module live in eight to twelve weeks. The biggest variables are data clean-up and how quickly process decisions are made, not the software itself.

Q: How much does ERP implementation cost?
A: Cost is driven by the number of modules and users, how much is custom development versus standard configuration, the integrations, the data-migration effort and the platform's licence model. Odoo Enterprise carries per-user subscription fees, ERPNext has no licence but needs hosting and support, and a custom ERP has no licence but a larger build. We quote module by module after process mapping so spending can be phased.

Q: Can we keep using Tally alongside the ERP?
A: Yes. A common set-up runs purchase, inventory, production, sales and dispatch in the ERP and keeps the books in TallyPrime, with invoices, receipts and ledgers synced automatically. Your accountant keeps the tool they know, and owners get operational data in one place. If you later move accounts fully into the ERP, that can be a separate phase.

Q: Does the ERP handle GST, e-invoicing and e-way bills?
A: Yes. Odoo and ERPNext both support Indian GST, and e-invoices and e-way bills can be generated from the ERP through the government systems, either directly or through a GST Suvidha Provider integration depending on the platform. We configure HSN codes, tax rules, place of supply and print formats, and test them with your accountant before go-live.

Q: Who owns the ERP, the code and the data?
A: You do. Custom modules sit in a repository in your name, the ERP runs on your cloud account or servers, and all admin credentials are handed over. With Odoo Community or ERPNext there is no lock-in to us or to a vendor, and any Odoo Enterprise subscription is held in your name.

Q: What support do we need after go-live?
A: Expect the first two to three months to bring small fixes, report changes and user questions, which is why post-go-live support is part of every project. After that, a support plan covers bug fixes, version upgrades, new reports and modules, and training for new staff, with agreed response times.


## Custom Software Development & System Integration
https://gaa-tha.com/services/custom-software-development
Last updated: 2026-10-22

gaa-tha builds custom software and connects the systems a business already runs: customer, dealer and vendor portals, internal platforms, APIs, and integrations between ERP, CRM, ecommerce, marketplaces and logistics. We handle the system engineering end to end — architecture on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or Firebase, CI/CD, security, legacy modernisation, documentation and support under an agreed SLA.

Best for: Growing companies whose ERP, CRM, store and logistics tools do not talk to each other, and businesses with workflows no off-the-shelf product fits
Timeline: Integrations in 2–6 weeks; portals and platforms in phases, with the first release in 8–12 weeks
Engagement model: Fixed-scope phases or a dedicated monthly team, plus an SLA-based support plan
Channels/platforms: Web apps and APIs; AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Firebase; ERP, CRM, Shopify, marketplace, payment and logistics integrations

### What it is
Custom software development is building software to a business's own specification — a dealer ordering portal, a vendor onboarding system, an internal operations platform — when off-the-shelf products do not fit the process. System integration is the companion discipline: connecting the ERP, CRM, ecommerce store, marketplaces, payment gateways and logistics partners through APIs so data is entered once and reaches everywhere it is needed.

At gaa-tha both are treated as system engineering. We start with an architecture view of every system, data flow and owner, decide what to build, buy or connect, then deliver in short releases with automated tests, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring and security reviews. Everything is documented so your own team, or any competent developer, can run and extend it after us.

### What's included
- Systems audit and architecture — current tools, data flows, owners, failure points and a target design
- Customer, dealer, distributor and vendor portals with ordering, ledgers, schemes, documents and support tickets
- Internal platforms and admin tools for operations, approvals, field teams and reporting
- REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks and middleware connecting ERP, CRM, Shopify, marketplaces, payment gateways and logistics
- Cloud architecture on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or Firebase, sized for current load and cost
- DevOps — version control, CI/CD pipelines, staging environments, infrastructure as code and automated backups
- Legacy modernisation: moving old desktop, PHP or spreadsheet-based systems to maintainable web platforms in stages
- Security by design — authentication, role-based access, encryption, audit logs, OWASP-based testing and data-protection practices
- Production monitoring, alerting and performance tuning
- Technical documentation, handover and support under an agreed SLA

### How we work
1. Audit and architect — We document every system, integration and data flow you run today, find the weak points and agree a target architecture with build, buy and connect decisions.
2. Specify and plan releases — Requirements become user stories, API contracts and a release plan, so each phase delivers something your team can use.
3. Build in short cycles — Development runs in one- or two-week cycles with demos on a staging environment, automated tests and code review on every change.
4. Harden and launch — Before go-live we run security, load and failure tests, set up monitoring and backups, and migrate data with a rollback plan.
5. Operate and evolve — After launch an SLA-based plan covers uptime monitoring, fixes, dependency and security updates, and new features from a shared backlog.

### Deliverables
- Architecture document and integration map
- Production software on your cloud account and domain
- Source code in your repository, with automated tests
- CI/CD pipelines, a staging environment and infrastructure configuration
- API documentation, runbooks and admin guides
- Monitoring, backups and an SLA-based support plan

Tools & platforms: Node.js and TypeScript, Python, React and Next.js, PostgreSQL, AWS, Google Cloud and Firebase, Microsoft Azure, Docker, GitHub Actions, REST and GraphQL APIs
Pricing model: Priced per phase from a written scope or as a dedicated monthly team; cloud hosting and third-party licences are billed to your accounts, and SLA support is a separate monthly plan.

### FAQ
Q: When should we build custom software instead of buying a SaaS product?
A: Build when the process is a genuine advantage, when several subscriptions plus workarounds cost more than owning a system, or when no product fits your data and integrations. Buy when the problem is common — accounting, email, basic HR — and a mature product already solves it. Often the right answer is to buy the core tools and build the portals and integrations around them.

Q: What is system integration and why does it matter?
A: System integration connects separate software — ERP, CRM, Shopify, marketplaces, payment gateways and logistics — so data moves between them automatically instead of being re-typed. Without it, teams reconcile orders, stock and payments by hand, and errors surface as stock-outs, wrong invoices or missed follow-ups. Integrations are built on official APIs and webhooks, with retries and alerts so a failure is noticed immediately.

Q: Which cloud should we use — AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or Firebase?
A: Use the cloud your team already knows or that matches your other systems; all four are reliable, and the differences lie mostly in managed services, pricing and available skills. Firebase suits fast web and mobile apps with real-time data, AWS and Google Cloud suit most custom platforms, and Azure fits businesses already on Microsoft 365. All the major clouds offer Indian regions where data residency matters.

Q: How much does custom software cost?
A: Cost depends on the number of user roles and screens, the integrations and the quality of their APIs, security and compliance requirements, data migration and the level of support you need. We split the work into phases with a fixed scope each, so you approve one release at a time. A reliable estimate only makes sense after a short discovery of your systems.

Q: Who owns the source code and intellectual property?
A: You do. The contract assigns the intellectual property in custom code to you, the repository and cloud accounts are in your name from day one, and documentation is part of every release. Open-source libraries keep their own licences, which we list at handover.

Q: Can you modernise our legacy system without stopping the business?
A: Yes, by replacing it in stages rather than in one big switch-over. We put APIs around the old system, move one module at a time to the new platform, migrate and reconcile data at each step and keep a rollback path. Users move across gradually, so daily operations continue throughout.

Q: What does maintenance and SLA support include?
A: An SLA-based plan covers monitoring, bug fixes within agreed response times by severity, security patches and dependency updates, backups with restore tests, and a monthly allowance for small changes. Response times and coverage hours are written into the SLA, so you know exactly what happens when something breaks out of hours.

Q: How do we choose a software development company?
A: Choose a team that asks about your process before proposing technology, can show architecture and documentation from past work, puts code and cloud accounts in your name and offers a written SLA. When comparing a freelancer, an offshore development shop and a long-term partner, ask who will maintain the system two years from now, not only what the build costs. Meet the engineers who will actually do the work before you sign.


## Custom Tools & Automations

gaa-tha builds custom tools and automations for small and mid-sized Indian businesses: lead trackers with WhatsApp follow-up, product batch-number lookup tools for customers, sales dashboards pulling from Google Sheets or your billing software, and automated quotes, catalogues and documents generated from a price list — scoped in days, built in weeks, and owned by you.

### What it is
Custom business tools and automations are small, purpose-built pieces of software that remove a specific piece of manual work — logging leads and chasing follow-ups, letting a customer check a batch number, compiling a daily sales report, or producing quotes and catalogues from a price list — usually by connecting the systems a business already uses. They are not an ERP; they are the missing piece between the ERP, the spreadsheet and WhatsApp.

At gaa-tha a tool starts with the task that is wasting the most hours, not with a technology. We map how the work happens today, agree the smallest tool that fixes it, build it on plain web technology and the services you already pay for (Google Sheets, WhatsApp, Firebase, your billing software), and hand it over with documentation and your own logins. Most tools are live within a few weeks and pay for themselves in saved time.

- Sales, stock or collection dashboards pulling from Google Sheets, Tally or your CRM

- Form-to-sheet-to-WhatsApp automations for enquiries, orders and dispatch updates
- Integrations with Google Workspace, WhatsApp Business, Zoho, Tally, Shopify and marketplaces via APIs, Zapier or Make

- Role-based access, backups and hosting setup
- Documentation, training and optional monthly support

2. Scope the smallest tool — We write a one-page scope — inputs, outputs, users, integrations — with a fixed price and a timeline, and agree what is out of scope for version one.

4. Test with the team — The people who will use it try it on real data, and the rough edges are fixed before launch.
5. Launch and support — The tool goes live with documentation, training and your own logins, with optional monthly support for changes and new features.

### Deliverables

Pricing model: Fixed project fee per tool based on the one-page scope; third-party services such as WhatsApp API, hosting or automation platforms are paid by you directly, and monthly support is optional.

### FAQ
Q: What are custom business tools and automations?
A: Small, purpose-built software that removes manual work: a lead tracker with a WhatsApp follow-up SOP, a product batch-number lookup for customers, a sales dashboard pulling from Google Sheets, or automated quotes and catalogues generated from a price list. gaa-tha scopes each one to a single task, builds it in weeks and hands it over with your own logins.

Q: Which tasks are worth automating first?
A: The ones that happen every day, involve copying data between two places and go wrong when someone is on leave — lead logging and follow-up, daily sales reports, quotes and proforma invoices, dispatch updates to customers. We map your process in a short session and rank tasks by hours saved and errors avoided.

Q: Do we need to change our software, Tally or CRM?
A: No. Tools are built to connect to what you already use — Google Sheets, Tally, Zoho, WhatsApp Business, Shopify, marketplaces — through their APIs or exports, or through Zapier and Make. If a system has no way to connect, we design around a simple export rather than asking you to migrate.

Q: How long does it take to build a tool?
A: Scoping takes a few days; most single-purpose tools are live in two to six weeks. A lead tracker or lookup tool sits at the short end; a dashboard with several data sources or a document generator with many templates at the longer end.

Q: How much does a custom tool cost?
A: Each tool is quoted as a fixed fee from a one-page scope, so the price is known before work starts and depends on the integrations, the number of users and screens, and whether you want ongoing support. Keeping version one small is how we keep the fee small.

Q: Who owns the code and the data?
A: You do. The tool runs on accounts in your name, the code and documentation are handed over at launch, and your data stays in your Google Workspace, Firebase project or server. There is no lock-in to gaa-tha.

Q: Will it work on mobile for our sales team in the field?
A: Yes. Tools are built as responsive web apps that work on any phone browser and can be added to the home screen, with WhatsApp as the notification channel because that is where your team already is.

Q: Is our customer and sales data secure?
A: Tools use role-based access, HTTPS, per-user logins and backups, and run on Google or Firebase infrastructure or your own hosting. We keep customer data inside your accounts rather than ours, and document who has access to what at handover.

## CDS Stores: CDS Stores: year-round Meta campaigns, city-wide outdoor and in-store marketing for a gifting retailer.
https://gaa-tha.com/work/cds-stores

gaa-tha is CDS Stores' 360° marketing partner in Vapi and Valsad — Meta campaigns, city-wide banners and print, in-store branding and screen content, festive campaigns with cinema ads and influencers, and the cdsstores.in website we built.

Industry: Retail / sweets, dry fruits & gifting. Services: Meta Ads Agency, Campaign Planning (Festive & Launch), Graphic Design, Cinema & Film Ads, AI Ads & AI Ad Shoots, Influencer & UGC Marketing, Social Media Marketing, Shopify Store Design & Development, Shopify Store Management & Maintenance.

# Guides from the gaa-tha blog
https://gaa-tha.com/blog


## AI agents for business: use cases and how to build one
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-agents-for-business-guide
Category: AI & Software. Published 2026-10-22.

An AI agent for business is software that uses a large language model to pursue a defined goal: it decides which steps to take, calls tools such as your CRM, Shopify store or ERP, remembers context, and works within guardrails you set. Unlike a chatbot, it acts; unlike fixed automation, it copes with variation. The best first agents do one narrow, repetitive job, such as qualifying leads or answering order-status queries, with a person approving anything risky.

### What is an AI agent, in plain terms?

An AI agent is a program that uses a large language model to reach a defined goal by choosing its own next step, calling tools to act on real systems, and checking the result before it moves on. Four parts make something an agent rather than a clever prompt:

- **A goal.** A specific job with a clear definition of done, such as “every new lead is scored, enriched and assigned within ten minutes”.

- **Tools.** Functions the agent can call: read an order in Shopify, search the CRM, query the ERP, send a WhatsApp template, create a draft purchase order.

- **Memory.** Short-term context for the current task (what the customer already said) and long-term knowledge (policies, past tickets, product data) retrieved when needed.

- **Guardrails.** Rules on what it may and may not do: spending limits, actions that need a human’s approval, topics it must refuse, and a step limit so it cannot loop forever.

The agent runs in a loop: read the situation, decide on an action, call a tool, look at what came back, and repeat until the goal is met or it hands over to a person. A simple example is an order-status agent on WhatsApp. A customer writes “mera order kab aayega?”; the agent finds the order by phone number in Shopify, pulls the latest scan from the courier, replies in Hinglish with the expected date, and, if the parcel is stuck in non-delivery, opens a ticket for the support team with the full context attached.

### How is an AI agent different from a chatbot or an automation?

An automation follows fixed rules, a chatbot answers questions, and an agent decides and acts across systems. The differences matter because each has a different cost, risk and maintenance profile.

| Aspect | Rule-based automation | AI chatbot | AI agent |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it does | Runs the same steps every time a trigger fires | Answers questions in natural language | Plans steps towards a goal and takes actions |
| Handles messy input | No; breaks on anything unexpected | Yes, for conversation | Yes, for conversation, documents and data |
| Acts on systems | Yes, but only the steps it was given | Rarely, or through fixed buttons | Yes, through tools it chooses between |
| Typical example | New Shopify order → Google Sheet row | Website FAQ assistant | Qualifies a lead, books the call, updates the CRM |
| Best when | The process is stable and rule-based | People need answers, not actions | Steps vary case by case but the goal is clear |
| Main risk | Silent failure when an input changes | Confident wrong answers | Wrong actions taken on real systems |

Most production systems combine them. A dependable pattern is a fixed workflow in n8n or code that calls an AI step only where judgement is needed, or an agent whose tools are themselves tested workflows. Our guides to [AI workflow automation](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-workflow-automation-n8n-make-zapier) and [AI chatbots for websites and WhatsApp](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-chatbot-for-website-and-whatsapp) cover the other two in depth.

### Where do AI agents pay off for Indian SMEs, D2C brands and B2B companies?

AI agents pay off on jobs that are frequent, follow a recognisable pattern but vary in detail, and currently eat hours of skilled staff time. These are the most common, with the systems involved:

| Use case | Who it suits | Tools the agent calls | Where a human checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead qualification | B2B manufacturers, exporters, real estate, education | IndiaMART or Meta lead forms, CRM (Zoho, HubSpot, LeadSquared), WhatsApp | Before quotes or prices are sent |
| Support and order status | D2C brands on Shopify | Shopify, courier tracking (Shiprocket, Delhivery), helpdesk | Refunds, replacements, angry customers |
| COD confirmation and NDR follow-up | D2C brands with high COD share | Shopify, WhatsApp templates, courier NDR data | Cancellations above a set value |
| Catalogue enrichment | Brands listing on Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra | PIM or Google Sheets, marketplace templates, image tools | Claims, HSN codes, sizing |
| Reporting | Founders and category managers | Shopify, Seller Central, ad platforms, quick-commerce reports | Anomalies it flags |
| Research | Exporters, sales and strategy teams | Web search, company databases, CRM | Before outreach |
| Procurement | Manufacturers and distributors | Email inbox, ERP or Tally, supplier price history | Every purchase order before release |

A good first candidate passes four tests: the volume is high enough to matter, the data it needs is reachable by API or export, a wrong output can be caught before it causes harm, and someone owns the outcome today and can judge whether the agent does it well. Lead qualification and order-status support usually pass all four. Fully autonomous procurement usually does not, so start it as a drafting assistant.

For D2C brands, support and COD agents sit on top of the store, so a clean [Shopify build](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) and reliable order data come first; the customer-facing layer is covered under [AI chatbot development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-chatbot-development), and our note on [COD vs prepaid](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/cod-vs-prepaid) explains why confirmation flows matter. For manufacturers and distributors, procurement and reporting agents need ERP access, which is why we cover [choosing between Tally, Odoo, ERPNext and custom ERP](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/custom-erp-vs-odoo-vs-erpnext-vs-tally) separately.

### How do you build an AI agent, step by step?

You build an AI agent by narrowing the job first and choosing technology last. The sequence we follow:

1. **Pick one job and define done.** Write the goal, the inputs, the expected output and three examples of success and failure. “Help sales” is not a job; “score and route every inbound lead within ten minutes” is.

2. **Map tools and data.** List every system the agent must read or write, how it connects (API, webhook, database, Tally’s XML interface, a spreadsheet) and the narrowest permission it needs. Read-only access first.

3. **Choose the model.** Match the model to the task’s difficulty, language and data-handling needs (see the next section).

4. **Choose orchestration.** Decide what runs the loop: a workflow tool, an agent framework or plain code.

5. **Connect tools and knowledge.** Expose tools through APIs or MCP, and ground answers in your own documents with retrieval (RAG).

6. **Build an evaluation set.** Collect 50 to 200 real past cases with the correct outcome, and score every version of the agent against them.

7. **Add human approval.** Decide which actions run automatically and which wait for a person.

8. **Launch in shadow mode.** Let the agent draft while people act, compare the two for a week or two, then hand over the actions it gets right.

9. **Monitor and control cost.** Log every step, watch cost per task and review failures weekly.

Steps 2, 6 and 7 take most of the effort. The prompt is rarely the hard part; reliable data access and honest testing are.

### Which model should power the agent: Claude, GPT, Gemini or open-source?

Choose the model by testing two or three candidates on your own evaluation set, because rankings change every few months and differ by task. As a starting point:

| Option | Commonly chosen for | Consider |
|---|---|---|
| Claude (Anthropic) | Tool use, long documents, careful instruction-following, coding-heavy agents | Available through Anthropic’s API and major clouds |
| GPT (OpenAI) | General-purpose agents, broad ecosystem, voice and vision features | Widest range of third-party integrations |
| Gemini (Google) | Very long context, multimodal input, Google Cloud and Workspace stacks | Natural fit if your data already lives in Google Cloud |
| Open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) | Self-hosting for data control, high-volume simple tasks | You run GPUs or a hosting provider, and own updates and safety tuning |

Three practical rules. First, route by task: a small, fast model can classify and extract, while a larger model handles multi-step reasoning, which often cuts running cost sharply. Second, test Indian languages explicitly; Hindi and Hinglish are handled well by the major models, Gujarati, Tamil and other Indic languages vary more, and Indic-focused models such as those from Sarvam are worth including in the test. Third, keep the model behind a thin layer of your own code so you can switch providers without rebuilding the agent.

### What do orchestration, MCP and RAG mean, and do you need them?

Orchestration, MCP and RAG are the plumbing that turns a model into a working agent; most business agents need a little of each.

### Orchestration

Orchestration is the code that runs the agent loop, passes tool results back to the model, enforces step limits and records what happened. Options range from the AI Agent node in n8n, to frameworks such as LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Claude Agent SDK and Google’s Agent Development Kit, to a few hundred lines of plain Python or TypeScript. For a single-job agent, simpler is better: fewer moving parts means easier debugging.

### MCP (Model Context Protocol)

MCP is an open standard, introduced by Anthropic and now supported across the major AI providers, for connecting models to tools and data. You describe a tool once as an MCP server, such as “look up order by phone number”, and any MCP-capable agent or assistant can use it. A growing number of SaaS products publish their own MCP servers. For a business, the benefit is reuse: the same Shopify or ERP connector can serve the support agent, the reporting agent and staff using an AI assistant.

### RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)

RAG means the agent searches your own knowledge, such as policies, product data, SOPs and past tickets, and answers from what it finds rather than from memory. It is the main defence against invented answers, and it is cheaper and easier to keep current than fine-tuning a model. Good RAG depends on clean, well-structured source documents more than on the choice of vector database.

### How do you test, approve and monitor an agent in production?

You test an agent against real past cases before launch, gate risky actions behind human approval, and log every step after launch. Concretely:

- **Evaluation.** Score each version on task success, wrong-action rate, escalation rate, cost per task and response time. Re-run the set after every prompt, model or tool change.

- **Approval tiers.** Read-only actions run freely; reversible actions (tagging a ticket, drafting a reply) run with a log; irreversible or money-related actions (refunds, discounts, purchase orders, messages promising delivery dates) wait for a person, usually with one-tap approval on WhatsApp or Slack.

- **Tracing.** Store the input, every tool call, every model response and the final output for each task, so any mistake can be replayed and explained.

- **Alerts.** Notify a named owner when failure rate, cost or escalations cross a threshold.

- **Weekly review.** Read a sample of conversations and every failure, add new cases to the evaluation set, and fix the cause rather than patching the prompt for one example.

### What are the risks of AI agents, and how do you control them?

The three main risks are invented answers, exposure of data and manipulation through prompt injection, and each is controlled by design rather than by a better prompt.

| Risk | What it looks like | Controls that work |
|---|---|---|
| Hallucination | A confident wrong delivery date, price or policy | Answer only from retrieved sources or tool results; structured outputs validated by code; say “I’ll check with the team” when unsure |
| Data security | Customer details sent where they should not go, or keys with too much access | Least-privilege API keys, masking personal data the model does not need, provider terms that exclude training on your data, audit logs |
| Prompt injection | An email, review or web page contains hidden instructions the agent obeys | Treat all external text as data, restrict tools while processing untrusted input, require confirmation before sending or paying |
| Runaway cost | A loop calls the model hundreds of times | Step limits, per-task budgets, alerts on spend |

Prompt injection is listed first in the OWASP Top 10 for large language model applications for good reason: any agent that reads emails, supplier PDFs or web pages can meet it. For personal data, Indian businesses should design to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its rules, and brands selling to Canada or Europe also to PIPEDA or GDPR. Check where each provider processes and stores data, and prefer business API tiers over consumer apps.

### What drives the cost of building and running an AI agent?

The cost of an AI agent is driven mostly by integrations, testing and volume, not by the model itself. The main drivers:

- **Build:** the number of systems it connects to, how clean and reachable your data is, the approval interface, the number of languages, and the depth of the evaluation set.

- **Running:** model usage (tokens per task multiplied by tasks per month), hosting, a search index for RAG, WhatsApp message charges where relevant, and logging.

- **Upkeep:** API changes in connected tools, model upgrades, new edge cases and periodic re-testing.

The useful comparison is cost per completed task against what the task costs today in staff time, delay and errors. Include the human review time the agent still needs. If an agent saves two minutes on a task done ten times a day, it is probably not worth building; if it saves twenty minutes on a task done two hundred times a day, it usually is.

### How do you choose an AI agent development company?

Choose an AI agent development company by how it tests and secures agents, not by its demos. The types you will meet are freelancers (fast and affordable, but a single point of failure), no-code automation agencies (quick for workflows, limited when custom code is needed), product engineering firms (strong code, sometimes thin on business process) and full-service agencies with an engineering team (closer to marketing and commerce operations). Whichever type you talk to, ask:

1. How will you measure whether the agent works, and can we see the evaluation set?

2. Which actions will run without approval, and why?

3. Who owns the code, prompts, connectors and data at the end?

4. Can we switch the model provider later without a rebuild?

5. Have you integrated the systems we use, such as Tally, Zoho, Shopify or our ERP?

6. What does monitoring and support look like after launch?

7. Will you start with a scoped pilot on one job?

At gaa-tha, our [AI agent development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-agent-development) work starts with exactly that: one job, a written definition of done and an evaluation set before any build. Agents that need a portal, an approval app or deeper system work sit with our [custom software development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/custom-software-development) team, and simpler, fixed processes often belong in [AI workflow automation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-workflow-automation) instead. The [AI and software engineering](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-software-engineering) hub shows how the pieces fit.

Q: What is the difference between an AI agent and ChatGPT?
A: ChatGPT is a general assistant that a person talks to, while a business AI agent is built for one job and can act on your systems. An agent has access to your tools and data, follows your rules, and works whether or not anyone is chatting with it, for example by processing every new lead as it arrives.

Q: How long does it take to build an AI agent for a business?
A: A narrow, single-job agent can usually reach a pilot in a few weeks, and an agent that spans several systems takes a few months. The timeline depends mainly on how quickly data access is set up and how long shadow-mode testing runs, not on writing prompts.

Q: Can an AI agent work with Tally, Zoho or our ERP?
A: Yes, if the system can be reached by API, database, export or a connector. Zoho, Odoo and ERPNext have documented APIs; Tally is usually connected through its XML interface or a connector running on the machine where Tally is installed. Start with read-only access and add write actions behind approval.

Q: Is it safe to give an AI agent access to customer data?
A: It can be, when the agent has the narrowest permissions it needs, personal data is masked where the model does not need it, and the provider’s business terms exclude training on your data. Log every action and keep irreversible steps behind human approval.

Q: Do we need to train or fine-tune our own model?
A: Almost never for a first agent. Retrieval over your own documents and good tool design solve most business needs, and they are easier to update than a fine-tuned model. Fine-tuning becomes worth considering only at high volume for a narrow, stable task.

Q: Will an AI agent replace our staff?
A: In practice, a well-scoped agent removes repetitive steps so staff spend their time on judgement, exceptions and customers. Most businesses use the time saved to handle more volume or respond faster, and they still need people to approve, review and improve the agent.

## AI chatbots for websites and WhatsApp: a guide for brands
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-chatbot-for-website-and-whatsapp
Category: AI & Software. Published 2026-10-22.

An AI chatbot for a website or WhatsApp answers customer questions in natural language from your own catalogue, FAQs and policies, looks up live data such as order status, captures leads and hands complex conversations to a person. Unlike older rule-based bots, it understands free text, including Hindi, Gujarati and Hinglish. For most Indian brands WhatsApp is the higher-value channel, but it needs the WhatsApp Business API, approved templates and customer opt-in.

### What can a modern AI chatbot do that old rule-based bots could not?

A modern AI chatbot understands free-text questions, answers from your own content and looks up live data, where an old rule-based bot could only follow button menus and keyword matches.

| Aspect | Rule-based bot | AI chatbot |
|---|---|---|
| Input | Buttons and exact keywords | Free text, voice notes, typos, mixed languages |
| Knowledge | Answers typed into a flow builder | Your catalogue, FAQs and policies, retrieved at answer time |
| Live data | Rarely | Order status, stock, delivery estimates by pincode, appointment slots |
| When it fails | Loops back to the menu | Can sound confident and be wrong, unless grounded and tested |
| Maintenance | Every new question needs a new branch | Update the source document; the bot follows |

Buttons still have a place: for payments, address confirmation or choosing a size, a tap is faster and safer than typing. The best bots mix free-text understanding with structured buttons where precision matters.

A typical exchange shows the difference. A customer writes “is the vitamin C serum ok for oily skin and will it reach Surat by Friday?”. A rule bot matches “serum” and shows a product menu. An AI chatbot answers the suitability question from the product’s own ingredient notes, checks the delivery estimate for the customer’s pincode, and offers a button to order or to ask a skincare adviser.

### How does the WhatsApp Business API work for brands?

The WhatsApp Business API, now called the WhatsApp Business Platform, lets a business connect WhatsApp to software, such as a chatbot, CRM or shared inbox, instead of replying from a phone app. The essentials:

- **Access.** Connect directly through Meta’s Cloud API, or through a Business Solution Provider (BSP) such as Gupshup, Interakt, AiSensy, WATI, Twilio or 360dialog, which adds an inbox, broadcasts, flow builders and support.

- **Set-up.** A Meta Business account, a verified business for higher limits, an approved display name and a dedicated phone number.

- **The 24-hour window.** When a customer messages you, you can reply freely for 24 hours. Outside that window you may only send pre-approved templates.

- **Templates.** Each template is approved by Meta and belongs to a category: marketing, utility (order updates, payment reminders) or authentication (one-time passwords). Each language version needs its own approval.

- **Opt-in.** Customers must agree to receive messages from you; collect consent at checkout or on forms and record it.

- **Pricing.** Meta used to charge per 24-hour conversation and moved in 2025 to charging per delivered template message, with rates by category and country; replies inside the customer service window are not charged. Rules and rates change, so check Meta’s current pricing for India and your BSP’s fees.

- **Quality and limits.** Blocks and reports lower your quality rating, which can reduce how many people you can message per day.

Meta’s terms also do not allow general-purpose AI assistants on the platform; a bot that serves your own customers about your products, orders and services is the intended use.

A website chat widget is simpler: no Meta approvals, no template rules and no per-message charges, and it can be added to a Shopify theme or any site with a script. It suits pre-purchase questions from web visitors and international customers, and it can hand the conversation over to WhatsApp when the customer prefers.

### How do you train a chatbot on your catalogue, FAQs and policies?

You train a business chatbot by connecting it to clean source content that it searches at answer time, not by retraining a model. The sources that matter:

- **Catalogue:** synced from Shopify or your ERP through the API, with prices, variants, stock, ingredients or specifications, so answers never go stale.

- **Policies:** shipping times by region, COD rules, returns, exchanges, warranty, cancellations.

- **FAQs and guides:** size charts, usage instructions, care, compatibility, B2B minimum order quantities.

- **Past conversations:** the questions customers really ask, mined from WhatsApp and email history.

Then write the rules: tone of voice, what it must never say (medical claims for skincare, promised delivery dates it cannot check, discounts it has no authority to give), and when to hand over. Before launch, test it against a hundred or more real questions and fix the source content, not just the prompt, wherever it gets something wrong. Policies written as short, direct question-and-answer pairs (“Can I return a product after opening it? No, except for damage in transit, reported within 48 hours.”) give far better answers than long legal pages. The approach is the same retrieval method described in our [guide to AI agents for business](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-agents-for-business-guide).

### Can an AI chatbot reply in Hindi, Gujarati and Hinglish?

Yes. Current large language models handle Hindi and Hinglish well and Gujarati reasonably well, but you must test with real customer messages before launch. Indian customers write in Devanagari, in Gujarati script and in romanised forms such as “maro order kyare aavse?”, often mixing English product names in the same sentence. Set the bot to reply in the language and script the customer used, transcribe voice notes, which are common on WhatsApp, and keep product names, prices and order numbers in a consistent form. Decide in advance how the bot handles prices and quantities, so “do sau rupaye” and “₹200” are read the same way. Remember that templates sent outside the 24-hour window need an approved version in each language you use. For international customers, the same set-up works for English, French or any other language you serve.

### How should handoff, order tracking and lead capture work?

### Human handoff

Hand over to a person whenever the customer asks for one, sounds angry, raises a refund or damage claim, or the bot fails to answer twice. Pass the full transcript and order details so the customer never repeats themselves, show business hours honestly, and route to a shared inbox in your BSP or helpdesk, such as Freshdesk, Zoho Desk or Gorgias.

### Shopify order tracking

Identify the customer by WhatsApp number or order number plus a verification detail, fetch the order from the Shopify Admin API, and pull the latest courier scan from Shiprocket, Delhivery or your aggregator. Explain the status in plain words with an expected date. The same flow can confirm COD orders and reschedule failed deliveries, which reduces return-to-origin losses; our post on [COD vs prepaid](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/cod-vs-prepaid) explains why. Clean order and tracking data starts with the [Shopify build](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) itself.

### Lead capture

For B2B and high-ticket brands, ask two or three qualifying questions in conversation, such as quantity, city and timeline, then create the lead in your CRM and offer a call slot. Click-to-WhatsApp ads on Meta feed this flow directly, and the routing behind it is covered in our guide to [AI workflow automation](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-workflow-automation-n8n-make-zapier).

### Which metrics show whether a chatbot is working?

Measure verified resolution and business outcomes, not the number of chats. Track:

- **Resolution rate:** conversations closed without a person, checked by sampling, not assumed.

- **Handoff rate and reasons:** which questions the bot cannot answer yet.

- **Wrong-answer rate:** from a weekly review of a random sample.

- **First response time and customer satisfaction.**

- **Commercial outcomes:** orders or leads from chat, COD confirmation rate, RTO change, lead-to-meeting rate.

- **Cost per conversation,** including model usage, BSP and Meta charges.

Review these weekly for the first two months, then monthly. The handoff reasons are the most useful list you will get: each one is either a gap in your content, a missing integration, or a question that genuinely needs a person.

### What mistakes should brands avoid with AI chatbots?

The common mistakes are about scope, data and honesty, not technology:

1. Launching on every channel at once instead of proving one.

2. Copy-pasting the catalogue into a prompt instead of syncing it, so prices and stock go stale.

3. Hiding the human option; customers who cannot reach a person leave.

4. Pretending the bot is a person; say it is an assistant.

5. Sending marketing templates without clear opt-in, which damages your quality rating.

6. Letting the bot promise refunds, discounts or delivery dates it cannot check.

7. Never reading the transcripts after launch.

8. Measuring success by chat volume rather than resolved questions and orders.

The clear, question-shaped answers you write for the bot also help elsewhere: the same FAQ content, published on your site, is what search engines and AI answer engines quote, which is the focus of our [SEO, AEO and GEO](https://gaa-tha.com/services/seo-aeo-geo) work.

gaa-tha designs and builds website and WhatsApp assistants under [AI chatbot development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-chatbot-development), connected to Shopify, CRMs and helpdesks, and extends them into [AI agents](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-agent-development) when they need to act across more systems.

Q: Can I use my existing WhatsApp Business app number with the API?
A: Often, yes. Meta now lets many businesses use the WhatsApp Business app and the platform on the same number, with some feature limits; otherwise the number moves from the app to the API. Check the current options with Meta or your BSP before you switch.

Q: What does a WhatsApp AI chatbot cost to run?
A: Running cost has four parts: the BSP subscription if you use one, Meta’s charges for template messages, AI model usage per conversation, and maintenance. Replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are not charged by Meta, so support-led bots cost far less to run than broadcast-heavy ones.

Q: Will an AI chatbot make up answers?
A: It can if it answers from the model’s general knowledge. Grounding answers in your own catalogue and policies, telling it to hand over when unsure, and reviewing transcripts weekly keeps wrong answers rare and quickly corrected.

Q: Should we start with a website chatbot or WhatsApp?
