| High-frequency category with loyalty or subscriptions | App builder to test, custom app once app revenue is proven |
| Unique experience: configurators, kit builders, try-on, content and community | Custom Flutter or React Native app on the Storefront API |
| Multi-brand or multi-city store with local delivery slots | Custom app with store and slot logic |
| Retailers or distributors reordering weekly | Custom B2B ordering app linked to Tally or ERP, or Shopify B2B |
| Field sales team taking orders at outlets | Custom field-sales app with offline mode |

If your store serves several locations, our guide to [one website for multiple store locations](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/one-website-for-multiple-store-locations) covers the logic an app would also need.

### Which metrics show whether your app is working?

An app is working if it creates incremental orders at a profit, and the only reliable way to see that is to compare app users with a similar group of web customers. App users are your most loyal customers to begin with, so raw “app users spend more” figures overstate the effect.

1. **Incremental repeat rate:** repeat purchase rate and order frequency of app users versus customers with a similar order history who did not install, measured over 90 days.

2. **Share of revenue from the app** and whether total revenue from those customers grew or simply moved channel.

3. **App conversion rate** versus mobile web conversion.

4. **Push opt-in rate** and revenue per push sent; falling opt-ins mean messages are not wanted.

5. **30- and 90-day retention** of active app users, and uninstall rate after campaigns.

6. **Crash-free sessions** above 99% and app store rating.

7. **Payback:** months until incremental contribution margin covers the build and running costs.

gaa-tha builds ecommerce apps on Shopify and custom stacks, and we start by checking whether your repeat data supports an app at all. See [ecommerce app development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-app-development), or [Shopify development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) if the store itself needs work first.

Q: Is a PWA good enough instead of a mobile app?
A: For most ecommerce brands, yes, at least at first. A PWA is installable, fast and supports web push, though on iPhone push works only after the customer adds it to the home screen. Move to a native or cross-platform app when repeat customers and loyalty features justify it.

Q: How much does a Shopify mobile app cost?
A: Shopify app builders charge a monthly subscription that rises with plan and features, so check current pricing. A custom Flutter or React Native app on the Shopify Storefront API typically costs ₹8–25 lakh to build in India as an indicative 2026 range, plus 15–25% a year to maintain.

Q: Will a mobile app increase my ecommerce sales?
A: Only if it makes existing customers buy more often. Apps mainly lift repeat purchases through push notifications, faster reordering and loyalty; they rarely bring new customers on their own.

Q: Do Apple and Google take a commission on products sold in my app?
A: Generally no for physical products and real-world services, which use your own payment gateway. Store billing and commissions usually apply to digital goods and subscriptions, and rules vary by region, so check current policy.

Q: Can my app use GoKwik, Razorpay or Shiprocket checkout?
A: Often yes, but confirm with the provider first. Shopify’s Checkout Kit brings Shopify checkout into native apps, while third-party checkouts each have their own mobile support, which decides how your app checkout is built.

Q: How do I get customers to download my brand’s app?
A: Ask existing customers at the moments they care about: order confirmation, delivery updates and loyalty rewards. Offer something app-only that is genuinely useful, such as early access or faster reordering, rather than buying installs from strangers.

## Hidden Shopify features most stores never switch on
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/hidden-shopify-features
Category: Shopify. Published 2026-10-22.

The hidden Shopify features most stores never switch on are already in the admin: search synonyms and boosts, metaobjects for size guides and ingredients, Flow templates, customer segments, draft orders as quotes, order editing, scheduled product availability, bulk redirects, theme previews and pincode delivery zones. None needs a paid app, and most take under an hour to set up. Here is what each does and where to find it.

### Which hidden Shopify features help shoppers find and choose products?

The features that help shoppers find products are search synonyms and boosts, metaobjects, rich product media and automated collections, and most stores leave all four half set up.

- **Search synonyms and boosts.** In the free Shopify Search & Discovery app, add synonym groups for the words customers type (“kurti, kurta”, “sneakers, shoes”, “moisturiser, moisturizer”) and boost the right product for a high-intent search. Check the no-results searches every month.

- **Metaobjects for size guides and ingredients.** Create a “size chart” or “ingredient” metaobject once, link it to products through a metafield and display it with a theme section. Update it once and every product page changes.

- **Video and 3D product media.** Product media supports uploaded video, YouTube or Vimeo embeds and 3D models that shoppers can rotate and, on supported phones, view in augmented reality. A 20-second texture or fit video often answers what a photo cannot.

- **Automated collection conditions.** Smart collections fill themselves from conditions on tag, product type, vendor, price, stock, metafield values and more, so “under ₹999”, “new this month” or “in-stock bestsellers” stay current without manual work.

### Which hidden features automate marketing and retention?

Shopify’s built-in segments, automations, Flow templates and gift cards cover most early retention work without a paid tool.

- **Customer segments with automations.** Build segments such as “bought twice, not in 90 days” or “spent over ₹5,000 in Maharashtra” and use them in Shopify Email campaigns, marketing automations and discount eligibility.

- **Abandoned checkout automation.** In marketing automations, switch on the abandoned checkout message with timing and copy that suit the brand. If a third-party checkout or WhatsApp provider runs its own recovery, keep one of them so buyers are not messaged twice; [Shopify integrations for Indian brands](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-integrations-for-indian-brands) covers those tools.

- **Flow templates.** Shopify Flow’s library holds hundreds of ready workflows: tag repeat buyers, flag risky orders, alert on low stock, cancel unpaid orders. Install three this week.

- **Gift cards and store credit.** Sell digital gift cards, issue them as goodwill, or offer store credit instead of a refund where policy allows. Festive gifting makes them worth setting up before Diwali.

### Which hidden features save hours in the Shopify admin?

The bulk editor, keyboard shortcuts, scheduled availability, redirect import and staff permissions are the features that save a small team the most admin time each week. None is new; most teams simply never look for them.

- **Bulk editor.** Select products and edit prices, compare-at prices, SKUs, weights, tags, SEO fields and metafields in a spreadsheet-like grid. Ideal before a sale.

- **Keyboard shortcuts.** The admin search opens from the keyboard, and Shopify’s Help Center lists navigation shortcuts; learning five saves real time on daily order work.

- **Scheduled product availability.** Set a future date for a product to appear on the online store so a launch goes live without anyone online at midnight. Shopify Plus adds Launchpad to schedule whole campaigns.

- **URL redirect bulk import.** Upload a CSV of old and new paths in the URL redirects area. Essential after renaming collections and during a [Shopify migration](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-migration), where missing redirects cost rankings.

- **Staff permissions and collaborator accounts.** Give each person only the permissions they need, and let agencies in through collaborator accounts you approve and can revoke, never the owner login.

### Which hidden features help with orders, quotes and delivery?

Draft orders, order editing, pincode-based local delivery and Translate & Adapt handle the order situations Indian stores meet daily: bulk enquiries on WhatsApp, COD changes, same-city delivery and regional-language buyers.

- **Draft orders as quotes.** Turn a bulk, corporate gifting or WhatsApp enquiry into a draft order, set an agreed price or discount, and email an invoice with a checkout link. The chat becomes a tracked order without a quotation app.

- **Order editing.** Add or remove items, change quantities or apply a discount after an order is placed, and Shopify recalculates the balance or refund. Useful when a COD buyer changes their mind on the confirmation call; check how edits reconcile with your gateway or third-party checkout.

- **Local delivery zones by pincode.** In shipping and delivery settings, local delivery can use a list of postal codes or a distance radius, each zone with its own minimum order and fee. A brand in Surat or Ahmedabad can offer same-day delivery only to the pincodes it can actually serve; see [one website for multiple store locations](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/one-website-for-multiple-store-locations).

- **Translate & Adapt.** Shopify’s free translation app manages store languages, with automatic translation for a limited number of languages and manual editing for the rest. Hindi or Gujarati versions of key pages can help tier-2 buyers; check which languages your theme and checkout support.

### How do you change a live Shopify store without breaking it?

Duplicate the live theme before every significant change, edit the copy and share its preview link for review. Shopify keeps the published theme untouched until you publish the duplicate, and the previous version stays in the theme library for a quick rollback. It is the cheapest insurance on the platform, and the step most often skipped.

1. Duplicate the live theme and rename it with the date and the change.

2. Make the edits on the copy, never on the live theme.

3. Share the preview link with whoever approves the change.

4. Check the preview on a mid-range Android phone, not only a laptop.

5. Run a mobile speed test and compare it with the live theme.

6. Publish at a quiet hour, then place a prepaid and a COD test order on the real checkout.

7. Keep the previous theme for at least two weeks before deleting it.

Our [Shopify speed and conversion checklist](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-speed-and-conversion-checklist) lists what else to test.

### Which hidden features should you switch on first?

Switch on the features that touch revenue first, then the ones that save time, then the ones that open new customers. A sensible order for most stores:

- **This week:** search synonyms, complementary products, abandoned checkout automation and two Flow templates (low-stock and high-risk order alerts).

- **This month:** a size guide or ingredient metaobject, product videos for hero products, automated collections and a lapsed-buyer segment.

- **Before the next sale:** bulk editor price changes, scheduled availability, gift cards and a duplicated theme for the campaign.

- **When operations need it:** draft-order quotes, order editing for the COD team, pincode delivery zones and translations.

Measure each change against the previous month so you know which ones paid off.

### Where do you find each hidden Shopify feature?

| Feature | Where it lives | First step |
|---|---|---|
| Search synonyms and boosts | Search & Discovery app | Add ten synonym groups from no-results searches |
| Complementary products | Search & Discovery app | Set “pair it with” for top sellers |
| Metaobjects | Settings, custom data | Create a size guide or ingredient entry |
| Product video and 3D | Product media | Add one video to each hero product |
| Automated collections | Collections | Build an “in-stock bestsellers” collection |
| Customer segments | Customers, segments | Create a lapsed repeat-buyer segment |
| Abandoned checkout automation | Marketing, automations | Turn it on and rewrite the copy |
| Flow templates | Shopify Flow app | Install low-stock and high-risk order alerts |
| Gift cards | Products, gift cards | Publish a festive gift card |
| Bulk editor | Products list | Edit sale prices for one collection |
| Scheduled availability | Product publishing | Schedule the next launch |
| URL redirect import | Navigation, URL redirects | Import redirects for renamed pages |
| Staff and collaborator access | Settings, users | Remove access nobody uses |
| Draft orders | Orders, drafts | Quote the next bulk enquiry this way |
| Order editing | Order page, edit | Train the COD confirmation team |
| Local delivery zones | Settings, shipping and delivery | List the pincodes you serve |
| Translate & Adapt | Shopify app | Translate the home and top product pages |
| Theme duplicate and preview | Online Store, themes | Duplicate before the next edit |

Admin menus move occasionally, so use the admin search if a path differs. For the bigger platform features behind these settings, read [the best Shopify features for ecommerce](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/best-shopify-features-for-ecommerce). If you would rather hand the list to a team, gaa-tha’s [Shopify store management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-store-management) and [conversion rate optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/conversion-rate-optimisation) services set these up on live stores.

Q: What is the most underused Shopify feature?
A: Search synonyms in the Shopify Search & Discovery app are probably the most underused feature, because few stores set them up and they decide whether shoppers find products. Metaobjects and Shopify Flow templates come close behind.

Q: Do these hidden Shopify features cost extra?
A: Most are included in Shopify plans or delivered through free Shopify apps such as Search & Discovery, Flow and Translate & Adapt. A few depend on plan, such as Launchpad on Shopify Plus, and Shopify Email charges beyond its free allowance.

Q: Can I use Shopify draft orders as quotations?
A: Yes. Create a draft order with the items and agreed price, then send the invoice; the customer pays through a checkout link and it becomes a normal order. For formal GST documents, pair it with a GST invoicing app or your accounting software.

Q: How do I set up delivery by pincode on Shopify?
A: Use local delivery in the shipping and delivery settings and define zones by postal code list or distance, each with a minimum order and delivery fee. For pan-India shipping, use a shipping aggregator such as Shiprocket or Delhivery alongside it for courier serviceability.

Q: Is it safe to edit a live Shopify theme?
A: It is safer to duplicate the theme, edit the copy and publish only after previewing it. The previous theme stays in the library, so you can roll back in minutes if something breaks.

## How to choose a Shopify agency in India: what top agencies do
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-shopify-agency-in-india
Category: Shopify. Published 2026-10-22.

To choose a Shopify agency in India, first decide which type of partner you need (freelancer, theme customiser, Shopify-only studio, full-service D2C agency, or Plus and headless specialist), then compare them on discovery, conversion-led design, tracking, speed, Indian checkout and COD expertise, and post-launch support. Ask for live stores, a written scope and full ownership in your name. Price matters, but scope and process decide the result.

### What types of Shopify partners are there in India?

Shopify partners in India fall into six broad types, and each is the right choice for a different job.

| Partner type | Best for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Freelancer | Small setups, quick fixes, tight budgets | Availability, a single point of failure, limited design or tracking depth |
| Theme customiser | Installing and adjusting a theme fast | Little strategy or conversion thinking; heavy reliance on apps |
| Shopify-only studio | Conversion-led builds, custom sections, migrations | May not handle ads, content or marketplaces |
| Full-service D2C agency | Store, brand, content, ads and retention under one plan | Check that Shopify depth is in-house, not outsourced |
| Shopify Plus and headless specialist | Checkout extensions, B2B, Hydrogen, ERP integrations | Higher cost; more than a first store needs |
| Offshore development shop | Large volumes of code at low hourly rates | Communication, D2C context and ownership of outcomes |

No type is better in general. Decide whether you need a website, a website plus growth, or engineering depth, then shortlist two or three partners of that type. For marketing-agency types, see our guide to the [best digital marketing agency in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog-best-digital-marketing-agency-india).

### What do the best Shopify agencies do differently?

The best Shopify agencies treat the store as a sales system rather than a design project, which shows up in seven habits.

- **Discovery before design.** They study your products, margins, buyers, competitors and current analytics, and write down what the store must achieve before opening Figma.

- **Conversion-led design.** Navigation by buyer need, product pages that answer objections, bundles that raise order value, mobile first, with every design choice explained by buyer behaviour rather than taste.

- **Tracking as a deliverable.** Meta Pixel with Conversions API, GA4 and Google Ads conversions, verified on a real order, including on third-party checkouts.

- **Speed discipline.** Fewer apps, custom sections instead of scripts, compressed media and a mobile performance target agreed upfront.

- **Indian checkout and COD.** Gateway choice, one-click checkout trade-offs, COD rules by pincode and order value, WhatsApp confirmation and shipping integration; see [Shopify integrations for Indian brands](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-integrations-for-indian-brands).

- **Content readiness.** Photography and copy are planned with the build, so the store launches complete.

- **Life after launch.** A bug-fix window, training, a [conversion rate optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/conversion-rate-optimisation) roadmap and optional [store management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-store-management).

A quick test: ask each agency what it would change on your current store or a store you admire. An average answer talks about colours and a new homepage; a strong one talks about product pages, checkout friction, COD rules, tracking gaps and the few pages that carry most of the revenue.

### What are the red flags when hiring a Shopify agency?

The biggest red flag is an agency that cannot show live Shopify stores and explain exactly what it did on each. Others to watch for:

- The store, domain, theme or app accounts set up in the agency’s name rather than yours.

- A quote without a list of templates, sections and integrations.

- Another app as the answer to every requirement.

- No mention of tracking, mobile speed or checkout testing.

- Guaranteed sales or rankings, or “number one agency” claims without evidence.

- A design copied wholesale from another brand’s store.

- No redirect and SEO plan when replacing an existing site.

- Vagueness about who will actually do the work, or undisclosed subcontracting.

Price itself can be a flag. A quote far below the others usually means content, tracking or integrations are missing from the scope; a quote far above them should come with features or depth the others do not offer. Ask either to explain the gap line by line.

### Which questions should you ask a Shopify agency before signing?

Ask questions that force specific answers about scope, process and ownership; vague answers to any of these are a warning.

1. Which live Shopify stores have you built, and what exactly did you do on each?

2. Will you customise a theme or build a custom one, and why is that right for us?

3. How many templates and custom sections are included?

4. Which gateway, checkout, shipping and WhatsApp integrations are included and tested?

5. How will you set up and verify Meta Pixel, Conversions API and GA4?

6. What mobile speed target will you meet, and how many apps will the store run?

7. Who supplies photography and copy?

8. How do you handle redirects and SEO in a [Shopify migration](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-migration)?

9. What happens in the first 30 days after launch, and what does ongoing support cost?

10. Will the store, theme code, accounts and files all be owned by us?

### How should you run the agency selection process?

Run Shopify agency selection as a short, structured process over two to four weeks, so you compare like with like.

1. **Write a one-page brief:** products and catalogue size, target buyers, must-have features, integrations, content you already have, budget band and launch date.

2. **Shortlist three partners** of the type that fits the job, from referrals, live stores you admire and the Shopify Partner Directory.

3. **Hold a 45-minute call with each** and listen to their questions; good agencies ask about margins, COD share and repeat rate before talking about design.

4. **Request written proposals** against the same brief and scope sheet.

5. **Call two references per agency** and test their live stores on a mid-range Android phone.

6. **Score with the scorecard below,** then negotiate scope rather than only price.

7. **Consider a paid discovery phase** for large builds, so both sides agree the plan before committing to the whole project.

### How do you score Shopify agencies side by side?

Score each shortlisted agency from 1 to 5 on the criteria below, multiply by the weight and compare totals before you compare price.

| Criterion | Weight | What a strong answer looks like |
|---|---|---|
| Relevant live work | 20% | Several live stores in a similar category, with the agency’s role explained |
| Discovery and strategy | 15% | A written discovery stage with analytics review and clear goals |
| Conversion-led design | 15% | Design rationale tied to buyer behaviour; mobile-first prototypes |
| Tracking and analytics | 10% | Pixel, Conversions API and GA4 verified on a real order |
| Speed and app discipline | 10% | A mobile performance target and a short app list |
| Indian checkout, COD and integrations | 10% | A clear gateway, checkout, COD and shipping plan |
| Post-launch support | 10% | A bug-fix window, training and an optional retainer |
| Scope clarity and ownership | 10% | Itemised scope, with all accounts and code in your name |

For example, an agency scoring 4 on live work (4 × 20 = 80), 3 on discovery (45), 4 on design (60) and 4 on each of the five 10% criteria (200) totals 385 out of a possible 500. Compare totals, then ask the top two to close their weakest gaps. A high score with a higher price usually costs less than a low score with a cheap quote, because rework, lost tracking and slow pages are expensive. To sense-check the numbers, read [how much a Shopify website costs in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-website-cost-in-india).

Q: How much does a Shopify agency charge in India?
A: Indicative 2026 Indian market ranges run from about ₹75,000 to ₹2.5 lakh for a studio-customised theme and ₹2.5 lakh to ₹8 lakh or more for a custom theme, with Shopify Plus and headless projects higher. These are not quotes; scope, integrations and content change the number.

Q: Should I hire a Shopify freelancer or an agency?
A: Hire a freelancer for a small, well-defined setup or quick fixes on a tight budget. Hire a studio or agency when you need design, conversion, tracking and integrations delivered together, or when the store must keep improving after launch.

Q: What is a Shopify Partner?
A: A Shopify Partner is a person or company registered in Shopify’s Partner Program to build stores, themes or apps for merchants. Registration on its own is not a quality signal, so judge partners on live work, process and references.

Q: How long should a Shopify agency take to build a store?
A: A customised theme typically takes four to eight weeks once content is ready, and a custom theme eight to fourteen weeks. Be wary of much shorter timelines for custom work, and of open-ended ones without milestones.

Q: Can the same agency run my Shopify store and my ads?
A: Yes, and it often helps, because tracking, landing pages, offers and creative are linked. Check that the agency has real depth in both and that its reporting connects store data with ad data.

Q: What should a Shopify agency contract include?
A: An itemised scope, a timeline with milestones, payments tied to those milestones, a change-request process, ownership of all accounts and code, post-launch support terms and confidentiality. Ask for it in writing before any work starts.

## How to choose a website and app development company in India
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-website-and-app-development-company-in-india
Category: Websites & Apps. Published 2026-10-22.

Choose a website and app development company by first matching the type of provider to your project, then scoring a shortlist on relevant live work, discovery process, technical quality, content and search skills, team continuity and contract terms. The best partners put code, accounts and intellectual property in your name, quote against a written scope and tell you what not to build. Price should be the final tie-breaker, not the first filter.

### What types of website and app development companies are there?

There are five main types of provider, and choosing the right type matters more than choosing between two firms of the same type.

| Provider type | Best for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Freelancer | Small sites, landing pages, theme-based stores, well-defined fixes | One person’s availability; you supply strategy, content and project management |
| Offshore dev shop | Clearly specified development work billed by the hour or by the developer | Builds what you specify, not what you need; design, content and product thinking are often thin |
| Design studio | Brand, portfolio and marketing sites where visual quality leads | Engineering depth, integrations and post-launch support vary |
| Full-service digital agency | Websites, stores and apps tied to brand, content, SEO and marketing | Check that development is in-house, not passed to a subcontractor |
| Product engineering firm | Complex web apps, SaaS platforms, enterprise systems, large teams | Higher cost and process overhead for a marketing website |

Many firms are hybrids, so ask who will actually design, write, build and support your project, and whether they are employees. A business that needs a website, a Shopify store and an app connected to its marketing gets most from a full-service team; a funded startup building a complex platform may need a product engineering firm; a clearly scoped landing page is often best value from a strong freelancer.

### What do the best development companies do differently?

The best development companies spend more time understanding the business before they quote, and more time on quality after the build is “done”.

- **They run discovery before pricing.** They ask about your customers, the action the site or app must drive, who will maintain it and what it must integrate with.

- **They push back.** They tell you which features to cut from version one and explain trade-offs between platforms such as Shopify, WordPress, Next.js, Flutter or React Native (see our [platform comparison](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/custom-website-vs-wordpress-vs-shopify-vs-webflow)).

- **They write, not just code.** Content structure and answer-first copy are part of the plan, because a beautiful site with weak words does not convert or get quoted by AI search; that is where [SEO, AEO and GEO](https://gaa-tha.com/services/seo-aeo-geo) starts.

- **They show designs for mobile first** and get approval before development starts.

- **They work on staging,** with version control in Git, and you can see progress weekly.

- **They test properly:** real Android and iOS devices, Core Web Vitals, accessibility, forms, payments and tracking.

- **They set accounts up in your name** and hand over documentation, credentials and code at launch.

- **They measure after launch,** connecting GA4, Search Console and lead or sales tracking so you can judge the result.

### How do you run the selection process, step by step?

A good selection process takes three to five weeks and moves from a long list to one partner through a shared brief, written proposals and a short paid discovery where the project is large.

1. **Write a one-page brief:** the business, the audience, the job of the site or app, must-have features and integrations, who will maintain it, a budget range and a deadline. Our [website cost guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/website-development-cost-in-india) includes a brief template.

2. **Build a long list of six to eight** from referrals, work you admire (check the footer or ask the owner who built it) and search, choosing the provider type first.

3. **Cut to three on evidence:** live work, relevant sector or complexity, and how well they respond to the brief in an introductory call.

4. **Ask the three for written proposals** against the same brief, including scope, team, timeline, milestones, exclusions and their standard contract.

5. **Score proposals on the scorecard below** and call references.

6. **For larger projects, buy a paid discovery** of one to three weeks from the front-runner: workshops, sitemap or user flows, a technical plan and a firm quote. It costs a fraction of the build, and you own the output even if you do not continue.

7. **Negotiate the contract, then the price.** Ownership, accounts and exit terms first; a lower fee is worth little if those are weak.

For a Shopify store specifically, our guide on [how to choose a Shopify agency in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-shopify-agency-in-india) adds platform-specific checks; for a marketing partner, see [how to choose a digital marketing agency in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog-best-digital-marketing-agency-india).

### How should you score development companies? A weighted scorecard

Score each finalist out of 100 using weighted criteria, ideally with two people from your side scoring independently before comparing.

| Criterion | Weight | What good looks like | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relevant live work | 20 | Comparable sites or apps live today, in your sector or of similar complexity | Open them on your phone; run PageSpeed Insights; download the app |
| Discovery and process | 15 | Structured discovery, written scope, sitemap or user flows before design | Ask for a sample scope document and project plan |
| Technical quality | 15 | Fast, accessible, secure builds on mainstream frameworks | Ask what stack and why; ask about testing and code reviews |
| Content, SEO and AEO | 10 | Copywriting, structured data and search set-up included | View page source on their work; look for schema and real headings |
| Team and continuity | 10 | Named in-house people who stay on the project | Meet the designer and lead developer, not just sales |
| Ownership and contract | 10 | IP assignment, source code, accounts in your name, clear exit terms | Read their standard contract before negotiating price |
| Communication | 10 | Clear weekly updates, one accountable contact, quick written answers | Notice how they handle the proposal stage |
| Support after launch | 5 | Warranty period, care plan, defined response times | Ask for the SLA in writing |
| Price and value | 5 | Itemised, matches the scope, no unexplained extras | Compare line by line, not by total |

Call two references for each finalist and ask what went wrong and how it was handled; every project has problems, and the answer tells you more than the praise. Adjust weights to your project: an app with payments should weight technical quality higher, a brand site should weight design and content higher.

### What questions should you ask before hiring a development company?

Ask questions that reveal how a company works, not just what it has made.

### About the work

- Which live projects are most like ours, and what was your exact role in each?

- What would you recommend we leave out of version one, and why?

- Which platform or framework would you choose here, and what would make you choose differently?

### About the team and process

- Who will design, write, build and test our project, and are they employees or subcontractors?

- How often will we see progress, and on what: a staging link, a test build, a demo call?

- How do you handle change requests and how are they priced?

- How do you test speed, accessibility, payments and tracking before launch?

### About ownership and after launch

- Will the domain, hosting, repositories, app-store and analytics accounts be in our name from day one?

- Will we receive the full source code and documentation, and when?

- What does the warranty cover and for how long, and what does support cost after it ends?

- If we part ways, what exactly do we receive and how quickly?

### What must a website or app development contract include?

A sound development contract fixes the scope, transfers ownership to you in writing, keeps every account in your name, ties payments to approved milestones and defines support after launch. Take legal advice for your situation; these are the clauses to look for.

- **Scope and acceptance criteria.** Pages, features, platforms and devices, with how “done” will be tested and accepted.

- **Intellectual property.** Under India’s Copyright Act, 1957, an outside contractor is generally the first owner of the work it creates, and an assignment must be in writing; if the assignment does not state its duration or territory, the Act can limit it to five years and to India. So the contract should assign all rights in designs, code and content to you, worldwide and permanently, on payment.

- **Source code.** Code is pushed to a Git repository (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket) owned by your organisation throughout the project, not handed over at the end.

- **Accounts in your name.** Domain registrar, DNS or Cloudflare, hosting, Shopify, Apple Developer and Google Play Console, Firebase, GA4, Meta Business, payment gateway and WhatsApp Business API accounts are owned by you, with the provider added as a user.

- **Third-party components.** A list of licensed themes, plugins, fonts and libraries, and who holds each licence.

- **Milestone payments.** A common structure is 25–40% on signing, a payment on design approval, a payment on staging or test-build approval, and the balance on launch and handover.

- **Change control.** How changes are requested, estimated and approved in writing before work starts.

- **Warranty.** A defect-fix period after launch, often 30–90 days, at no extra cost.

- **Support SLA.** Response and fix times by severity, as below.

- **Confidentiality and data protection.** Obligations under India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act and, for overseas users, GDPR or Canadian privacy law.

- **Exit and handover.** What you receive on termination, within how many days, and how disputes are resolved.

| Severity | Example | Typical response | Typical fix or workaround |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Site or app down, checkout or payments failing | Within 1–4 hours | Within 24 hours |
| Major | Key feature broken, forms not sending | Within 1 business day | Within 2–3 business days |
| Minor | Layout glitch, typo, small enhancement | Within 2–3 business days | Next scheduled release |

These SLA figures are common starting points for negotiation, not a standard; tighter terms cost more.

### What are the red flags when hiring a development company?

The clearest red flags appear before you sign, in how a company sells.

- A fixed price before any discussion of scope, content or integrations.

- Demands for 100% payment upfront, or most of it before design approval.

- Reluctance to put the domain, hosting or app-store accounts in your name.

- Vague answers on source code (“we provide the website, not the code”).

- A portfolio of screenshots with no live links, or live sites that are slow and broken on mobile.

- Claims of guaranteed first-page Google rankings or “#1” status.

- No questions about your customers or business goals.

- The person selling disappears once the contract is signed, and nobody can tell you who will do the work.

- Everything is “easy” and nothing is a trade-off.

- No staging site, no Git repository and no written change process.

- Recommending a client-side-only app for a marketing site that needs to be found in search.

- Pushing an app before the website or store works; read [does your ecommerce brand need an app?](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/does-your-ecommerce-brand-need-an-app) first.

### Should you hire an Indian development company from Canada or abroad?

Hiring an Indian development company from Canada, the UK, the Middle East or elsewhere works well when you choose for communication and process, not only for rates.

- **Time zones.** India is 9.5 to 10.5 hours ahead of Toronto depending on daylight saving, so agree a daily overlap window (Indian evening, Canadian morning) and written updates that do not need a meeting.

- **Contracts and payments.** Use a contract that names the governing law and dispute process, and invoice in USD or CAD where possible. Indian providers usually zero-rate exported services under a Letter of Undertaking, so Indian GST is generally not added; check your own country’s tax rules.

- **Local context.** Make sure the team understands your market: Canadian bilingual content, local payment methods and privacy expectations.

- **Same essentials.** Written scope, milestone payments, code and accounts in your name.

For example, gaa-tha’s team in India handled strategy, campaigns, Instagram, product scraping and the website for [New Rave](https://gaa-tha.com/work/new-rave), a Canadian trading-card retailer.
