Q: What is the best website and app development company in India?
A: There is no single best company; the best one is the provider whose type, experience and process fit your project. Shortlist by provider type, then score finalists on live work, process, technical quality, ownership terms and support. Be wary of any company that calls itself number one without evidence.

Q: Should I hire a freelancer or an agency to build my website or app?
A: Hire a freelancer for a small, clearly defined site where you can supply content and manage the project yourself. Hire an agency when you need strategy, design, copy, development and support from one accountable team, or when the site or app is central to your sales.

Q: Who owns the source code when an agency builds my website or app?
A: You should, but only if the contract says so. In India the creator of commissioned work is generally the first copyright owner, so insist on a written assignment of all rights to you, and on the code living in a repository your organisation owns.

Q: What is a fair payment structure for website or app development?
A: Milestone payments tied to approvals are fairest for both sides: an advance on signing, then payments on design approval, on staging or test-build approval, and on launch. Avoid paying everything upfront, and keep the final payment for handover of code and accounts.

Q: How long does it take to build a website or an app?
A: Corporate and brand websites typically take two to five weeks and larger sites six to eight. An app MVP usually takes eight to fourteen weeks and a SaaS MVP ten to sixteen, depending on features, integrations and how quickly decisions are made.

Q: How do I switch development companies in the middle of a project?
A: First secure access: confirm you own the domain, hosting, repositories and app-store accounts, and get the latest code and documentation. Then have the new provider audit the code before quoting, because taking over an unfinished project often reveals rework.

## Mobile app development cost in India (2026): Flutter vs native
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/mobile-app-development-cost-in-india
Category: Websites & Apps. Published 2026-10-22.

In 2026 a mobile app built in India typically costs ₹3–8 lakh for a simple app, ₹8–25 lakh for a mid-complexity app with accounts, payments and an admin panel, and ₹25 lakh to ₹1 crore or more for a marketplace or multi-app platform. These are indicative market ranges, not quotes. Features, integrations, backend, design depth and platforms drive the number, and running costs add roughly 15–25% of the build cost every year.

### How much does it cost to build a mobile app in India in 2026?

A mobile app built in India in 2026 usually costs between ₹3 lakh and ₹1 crore, and where a project lands depends mostly on how many user types, workflows and integrations it has. The table below gives indicative market ranges for a cross-platform build (iOS and Android from one codebase) by an experienced Indian team, including design, backend, admin panel, testing and store launch. They are typical ranges across the market, not a gaa-tha price list or a quote.

| Complexity | Typical examples | Indicative cost (INR, 2026) | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | Catalogue or content app, booking request app, event app, internal tool with OTP login and a handful of screens | ₹3–8 lakh | 6–10 weeks |
| Mid-complexity | Ecommerce app, appointment and payments app, loyalty app, field-sales ordering app, customer portal with notifications and an admin panel | ₹8–25 lakh | 3–5 months |
| Complex or marketplace | Multi-sided platform with separate customer, vendor and delivery apps, live tracking, chat, wallets, commissions and analytics | ₹25 lakh–₹1 crore+ | 6–12 months |

For international readers: one lakh is 100,000 rupees and one crore is 100 lakh. Two apps that look similar in a pitch deck can sit in different rows once the roles, rules and integrations are written down, which is why the brief matters more than the headline figure.

### How does the cost change with who builds it?

The same app can be quoted at very different prices because each type of builder includes different things and carries different risks. The ranges below are indicative for a mid-complexity app.

| Who builds it | Indicative cost | Strengths | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freelance developer | ₹2–8 lakh | Lowest cash cost, direct contact | Single point of failure; design, backend, QA and store launch often not included |
| Small app studio | ₹6–18 lakh | A small team with process, good for one-platform or cross-platform builds | Capacity limits; check who maintains the app after launch |
| Full-service agency | ₹10–30 lakh | UX, brand, development, launch and marketing under one roof | Make sure senior people work on the build, not only the pitch |
| Product engineering firm | ₹15–40 lakh+ | Strong architecture, security and scale practices | Higher cost; may be more than an MVP needs |
| In-house team | ₹3–8 lakh per month, ongoing | Full control and product continuity | Hiring time, management load and payroll before the app earns anything |

For clients in Canada, the US or Europe, Indian teams typically bill a fraction of local rates, and the saving is real when three things are in place: a written scope, a few hours of overlap each day, and source code, cloud accounts and store listings held in the client’s own name. Our guide on [how to choose a website and app development company in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-website-and-app-development-company-in-india) covers the questions to ask each type.

### What drives the cost of a mobile app?

App cost is driven by six things: features and user roles, integrations, the backend and admin panel, design depth, the number of platforms, and the quality bar. Hourly rates matter less than most buyers expect.

### Features and user roles

Every user type (customer, vendor, delivery partner, admin, sales rep) adds its own screens, permissions and edge cases. A marketplace is expensive mostly because it is three apps that must agree with each other.

### Integrations

Payment gateways such as Razorpay, PayU or Cashfree, SMS OTP, the WhatsApp Business API, maps, shipping aggregators, Shopify, Tally, Zoho or an ERP each add build and testing time. A poorly documented third-party API can cost more than a whole feature.

### Backend and admin panel

Someone has to manage products, users, orders, content and refunds. A backend on Firebase or Supabase is quicker to start; a custom Node.js or Python backend on AWS or Google Cloud suits complex rules and scale. Either way, budget for an admin panel, because spreadsheets do not scale.

### Design depth

A clean app built on a component library costs far less than a custom design system with motion, illustrations and accessibility testing. Both are valid; decide based on how much the experience is the product.

### Platforms and quality

iOS plus Android plus a web app plus tablet layouts multiplies testing. Offline mode, Hindi or Gujarati language support, automated tests, security reviews and device testing on budget Android phones all raise the quality bar and the cost.

| Feature | Relative effort | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Phone OTP or Google sign-in | Low | Mature services such as Firebase Auth; SMS in India needs DLT registration |
| Payments and refunds | Medium | Gateway SDK, webhooks, failure states, reconciliation |
| Push notifications and segments | Low to medium | Easy to send, harder to target and measure well |
| Chat or support inbox | Medium to high | Real-time sync, media, moderation |
| Live location tracking | High | Background location, battery, maps costs, OS permission rules |
| Offline mode with sync | High | Conflict handling when two devices edit the same record |
| AI features (chat, search, document reading) | Medium, varies | Model API costs, prompt design, guardrails and evaluation |

### Flutter vs React Native vs native: which should you choose?

For most business apps in 2026, Flutter or React Native is the right choice because one codebase serves both iOS and Android, often for 30–40% less build effort than two separate native apps; native Swift and Kotlin is worth it when the app depends on heavy device features, top-end performance or platform-specific experiences.

| Factor | Flutter | React Native | Native (Swift / Kotlin) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Language | Dart | JavaScript or TypeScript | Swift (SwiftUI) for iOS, Kotlin (Jetpack Compose) for Android |
| Backed by | Google | Meta, with Expo as the common framework | Apple and Google |
| Codebases | One | One | Two |
| UI approach | Draws its own UI, so it looks identical on every device | Renders real native components | Fully native look and behaviour |
| Performance | Very good for most apps | Very good, improved by the New Architecture | Best, especially for graphics, AR and heavy media |
| Device features | Plugins; custom native code when needed | Libraries; custom native modules when needed | Immediate access to every new OS feature |
| Sharing with web | Possible, less common | Strong when the web app is React or Next.js | None |
| Hiring in India | Large and growing talent pool | Large pool, overlaps with web React developers | Two specialist skill sets to hire and retain |
| Relative build cost | Lower | Lower | Highest |
| Best for | Brand-led UI, consistent design, ecommerce and booking apps | Teams already on React, apps sharing logic with a web product | Banking-grade security, AR, camera or Bluetooth-heavy, wearables |

Simple decision rules: if your web product is React or Next.js and the same team will own both, choose React Native. If design consistency and a polished custom UI matter most, Flutter is usually the faster route. If the app lives on hardware features, or you are building for Apple Watch or deep platform integrations, go native. Kotlin Multiplatform, which shares business logic while keeping native UI, is a maturing middle path worth considering for teams with Android experience. Our [mobile app development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/mobile-app-development) team works across all three and will tell you which fits rather than defaulting to one.

### What are the recurring costs after the app launches?

An app keeps costing money after launch: expect roughly 15–25% of the original build cost each year for maintenance, plus usage-based hosting, store and API fees.

| Cost | How it is charged | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Apple Developer Program | US$99 a year, billed in local currency | Needed to publish on the App Store; open it in your company’s name |
| Google Play Console | One-time US$25 registration | Organisation accounts need a D-U-N-S number and verification |
| Store commission | Typically 15–30% on digital goods and subscriptions | Physical products and real-world services (ecommerce, food, travel) generally sit outside in-app purchase rules; policies are changing by region, so check current terms |
| Hosting and backend | Monthly, scales with users and data | Firebase, Supabase, AWS or Google Cloud; small apps can start at a few thousand rupees a month |
| Third-party APIs | Per use | SMS OTP, WhatsApp Business API per-message charges, maps beyond free usage, email, AI model tokens |
| Payment gateway | Per transaction | Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree and others; check current pricing by payment method |
| Maintenance retainer | Monthly or yearly | Bug fixes, dependency upgrades, security patches, crash monitoring and small changes |

The maintenance line is not optional. Apple and Google release new OS versions every year, Google Play requires apps to target a recent Android API level to keep receiving updates, and payment and login SDKs deprecate old versions. An app that is not maintained for 18 months usually needs a costly catch-up project. A good maintenance plan includes crash monitoring with Firebase Crashlytics or Sentry, monthly dependency updates and a small budget for improvements users ask for.

### Why should you build an MVP first?

Building a minimum viable product first is the most reliable way to control app cost, because it puts one complete journey in front of real users before you pay for everything else. An MVP is not a cheap app; it is a narrow one, built properly.

| Phase | What happens | Typical duration |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Goals, user journeys, feature list ranked must-have and later, technical plan, clickable prototype | 2–4 weeks (often 5–10% of the build budget) |
| MVP build | One core journey end to end, admin panel, analytics, store launch | 6–14 weeks |
| Learn | Real usage data, support tickets, interviews, retention by cohort | 4–8 weeks |
| Phase two | Features users actually asked for, performance and scale work | Ongoing sprints |

A worked example: a regional food brand wants an ordering app with loyalty points, subscriptions, referrals, a recipe section and a delivery tracker. The MVP is browse, order, pay by UPI or card, track status and reorder in two taps, with push notifications. Loyalty and subscriptions follow once reorder rates justify them. If you are an ecommerce brand weighing this up, read [does your ecommerce brand need an app](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/does-your-ecommerce-brand-need-an-app) before committing to a full build, and if your product is a subscription software business, our [SaaS product development guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/saas-product-development-guide) covers MVP scoping in depth.

### How do you brief an app project to get accurate quotes?

An accurate quote needs a brief that describes users, journeys and integrations, not just a list of screens. Send every shortlisted team the same document so the quotes are comparable.

1. **The goal and the number:** what the app must achieve and how you will measure it (repeat orders, bookings, hours saved).

2. **Users and roles:** every type of user and what each can see and do.

3. **The top five journeys:** written step by step, for example “a retailer reorders last week’s stock and pays on credit”.

4. **Must-have versus later:** a ranked list, with the MVP line drawn.

5. **Integrations:** payment gateway, Shopify, Tally, Zoho, ERP, CRM, WhatsApp, SMS, maps, with links to their API documentation if you have them.

6. **Platforms and languages:** iOS, Android, web, tablet; English, Hindi, Gujarati or others.

7. **Admin needs:** who manages content, orders, users and reports.

8. **References:** two or three apps you like and what specifically you like about them.

9. **Budget band and deadline:** a range lets teams propose the right scope instead of guessing.

10. **Ownership:** source code repository, cloud accounts, Apple and Google developer accounts and domains in your name.

Red flags in quotes: a fixed price with no discovery, no mention of the backend or admin panel, no testing plan, store accounts opened in the developer’s name, and no maintenance terms. If the app needs a polished interface and prototype first, start with [app design and development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/app-design-development) so the build quote is based on approved screens.

### How can you reduce app development cost without cutting quality?

The cheapest way to reduce app cost is to remove scope, not to hire the cheapest team. These moves cut cost without leaving you with an app that has to be rebuilt.

- **Go cross-platform** with Flutter or React Native unless a clear native requirement exists.

- **Use managed services** for login, storage, notifications and analytics (Firebase, Supabase, OneSignal) instead of building them.

- **Reuse what you already run.** An ecommerce app can sit on your Shopify store through the Storefront API, so products, inventory and orders stay in one place; see [ecommerce app development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-app-development) and [Shopify development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development).

- **Consider a PWA or web app first** when users do not need the app daily; our guide to [website development costs in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/website-development-cost-in-india) shows how the numbers compare.

- **Launch in one language and one region**, then add Hindi, Gujarati or new cities once the core journey works.

- **Buy, do not build, the hard parts** such as chat, video calls and maps where good SDKs exist.

- **Keep internal tools off the app.** Many “app” ideas are really internal workflows better served by [custom software](https://gaa-tha.com/services/custom-software-development) or an [AI agent](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-agent-development) on WhatsApp.

gaa-tha builds mobile apps in Flutter and React Native for brands in India and abroad, alongside the branding, websites and marketing that bring users to them. If you want a second opinion on a brief or a quote, we are happy to review it with you; the starting point is the [mobile app development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/mobile-app-development) page.

Q: How much does a simple mobile app cost in India?
A: A simple app with a few screens, OTP login and content managed from an admin panel typically costs ₹3–8 lakh in 2026 as an indicative market range. The final figure depends on design depth, integrations and whether one or both platforms are included.

Q: Is Flutter cheaper than React Native?
A: Neither is reliably cheaper; both build iOS and Android from one codebase at similar effort. Choose React Native if your team already writes React for the web, and Flutter if a consistent custom UI matters most. Both are usually cheaper than two separate native apps.

Q: How long does it take to build a mobile app?
A: A simple app takes about 6–10 weeks, a mid-complexity app 3–5 months and a marketplace or multi-app platform 6–12 months. Discovery adds two to four weeks at the start, and store review adds a few days before launch.

Q: What is the yearly maintenance cost of an app?
A: Plan for roughly 15–25% of the original build cost each year. That covers OS updates, dependency upgrades, bug fixes, security patches and monitoring, while hosting, store fees and API usage are charged separately.

Q: Should I launch on iOS and Android at the same time?
A: With Flutter or React Native, launching both together adds testing effort but not a second build, so most Indian brands launch both. If budget is tight and your users are mostly on Android, launching Android first is a reasonable way to learn before iOS.

Q: Who should own the app’s source code and store accounts?
A: You should. Insist that the code repository, cloud accounts, Apple and Google developer accounts and domains are registered to your company, with the developer added as a user, so you can change teams without rebuilding.

Q: Do Apple and Google take a cut of sales made in my app?
A: For physical products and real-world services, generally no; you use your own payment gateway such as Razorpay. Digital goods and subscriptions usually go through the store’s billing with a commission of typically 15–30%, and these rules are changing in several regions, so check the current policy.

## What makes a great portfolio or brand website: a 2026 checklist
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/portfolio-and-brand-website-guide
Category: Websites & Apps. Published 2026-10-22.

A great portfolio or brand website makes one clear claim about who you help and how, proves it with three to six deep case studies, loads fast on a phone despite rich imagery and motion, and makes getting in touch effortless. For designers, architects, photographers, creators, consultants, founders and new brands, the site’s job is to turn a referral, a search or an AI recommendation into a qualified conversation.

### What should a portfolio or brand website say in the first five seconds?

The first screen should say who you work with, what you do for them and why that matters, in one sentence a stranger could repeat. “Creative solutions for all your needs” fails that test; specific claims pass it.

- **Architect:** “Residential and hospitality architecture in Ahmedabad and Mumbai, from site study to handover.”

- **Photographer:** “Product and campaign photography for beauty and food brands.”

- **Consultant:** “Export pricing and distributor strategy for Indian manufacturers entering Canada.”

- **New brand:** the product, the person it is for and the reason it exists, with the product visible.

Then curate. Show the work you want more of, not everything you have done, and order projects by relevance to your ideal client rather than by date. Positioning is a branding decision before it is a web decision; our [branding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/branding-agency) team often settles it before design starts.

**The pages most portfolio and brand sites need:** Home, Work (an index plus one page per case study), Services, About, Process, Journal or Insights, and Contact. A new consumer brand swaps Work for Shop, Story, Ingredients or Sourcing, Stockists and FAQ. Founders, consultants and creators also benefit from a press kit page with short and long bios, approved headshots and logos.

### How should you structure a case study?

A strong case study follows the story of a decision: the situation, the problem, what you chose to do and why, and what changed.

1. **Title with scope or outcome**, not just the client name.

2. **Context:** client type, sector, location, year, your role and who you worked with.

3. **The challenge**, ideally in the client’s own words.

4. **Two or three key decisions** and the reasoning behind each; this is what separates you from a gallery.

5. **The work:** finished images plus process (sketches, drawings, moodboards, before and after).

6. **The outcome:** real, permitted numbers or a plain description of what changed. Never invent metrics.

7. **Credits and a named testimonial**, then a link to the next project and to contact.

Architects can lead with drawings and site photography, photographers with a series and its brief, consultants with problem, approach and outcome. A workable length for most case studies is 400–900 words with 8–20 images. Under an NDA, anonymise the client (“a listed pharma company”), describe the process and ask permission before showing anything.

### How do you use storytelling and motion without slowing the site down?

Use motion to direct attention and reveal the story in order, and hold it to a performance budget: main content visible within 2.5 seconds (LCP), interactions responding within 200 milliseconds (INP) and no layout jumps (CLS under 0.1), tested on a mid-range Android phone on mobile data.

- Serve images as AVIF or WebP with responsive sizes, and lazy-load everything below the first screen.

- Replace heavy hero videos with short muted loops that have a poster image, or stream through Mux, Cloudflare Stream or Bunny Stream.

- Animate transform and opacity only; libraries such as GSAP are fine when used sparingly.

- Use Lottie or Rive for small vector animation; reserve Three.js or WebGL for moments that earn it, with a static fallback.

- Respect **prefers-reduced-motion** and avoid scroll-jacking, which frustrates visitors and hides content.

Budget page weight too: keep the first screen’s images and scripts to a few hundred kilobytes rather than several megabytes, and check every new effect in PageSpeed Insights before it ships.

Story is structure as much as effects: a clear sequence from claim, to proof, to the person behind the work, to the next step. That is the idea behind our name; gaa-tha (गाथा) means “story”.

### What proof and contact flow turn visitors into enquiries?

Visitors enquire when proof removes doubt and contacting you takes one obvious step.

**Proof that works:** client names or logos (with permission), named testimonials with role and company, publications and real awards, a clear process page, and for new brands the founder story, sourcing, certifications and genuine reviews.

Place proof near the decision point: a testimonial beside the contact form does more work than one buried on the About page.

**A contact flow that works:**

- One primary action repeated on every page: “Start a project”, “Book a call” or “Shop the range”.

- A short form: name, email or phone, project type, budget range and timeline. The budget field filters enquiries before the first call.

- WhatsApp click-to-chat for Indian visitors, and a booking link (Calendly or Cal.com) for consultants and international clients.

- An automatic reply that says what happens next and when.

- For new brands, a “where to buy” block linking to your store, Amazon or quick commerce listings, plus a launch-news sign-up.

- Form submissions, WhatsApp clicks and calls tracked as GA4 events, so you know which pages earn work. A bare email link cannot be measured.

### How do personal brands and new brands get found on Google and in AI answers?

Personal and new brands get found when search engines and AI assistants can identify them as a clear entity and read their work as text, not just images.

- Use one consistent name, description and location everywhere, and add **Person** or **Organization** schema (or **ProfessionalService** for studios with an address) with sameAs links to LinkedIn, Instagram, Behance and Google Business Profile.

- Publish every case study as its own indexable page with descriptive headings, alt text and file names, not as a PDF or an image-only gallery.

- Write an answer-first About page and service pages that state plainly what you do, for whom and where.

- Add FAQs that answer real client questions, and publish your thinking in articles; this is what AI assistants quote.

- Studios with an office should claim and complete a Google Business Profile, so map searches such as “interior designer near me” can find them.

- Keep Behance, Dribbble and Instagram as distribution, pointing back to your own site.

Regulated professions such as architects, chartered accountants and lawyers have council rules on advertising and solicitation in India, so keep their sites factual and check current guidance. Our [SEO, AEO and GEO](https://gaa-tha.com/services/seo-aeo-geo) service and the [SEO vs AEO vs GEO guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog-seo-aeo-geo-guide) go deeper.

### Which platform should a portfolio or brand website use?

Use custom code when distinctive motion, speed and search control matter most; Webflow or Framer when you will change layouts yourself; WordPress if you will publish articles weekly; and Shopify if the brand sells products. Squarespace, Cargo and Adobe Portfolio are reasonable starting points for a solo creative on a small budget. If you may sell later (prints, presets, courses or merchandise), pick a stack that can add commerce, such as Shopify or custom code using Shopify’s Storefront API. Whatever you choose, register the domain in your own name. The full comparison is in [custom vs WordPress vs Shopify vs Webflow](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/custom-website-vs-wordpress-vs-shopify-vs-webflow), and indicative budgets are in [website development cost in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/website-development-cost-in-india).

### The 2026 portfolio and brand website checklist

Use this checklist before launch and again every six months.

### Positioning and work

- A one-sentence positioning line on the first screen

- Three to six case studies, ordered by relevance to the clients you want

- Each case study shows context, challenge, decisions, work and outcome

- An About page with real people, a photograph and your story

### Performance and experience

- LCP under 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 ms and CLS under 0.1 on mobile

- AVIF or WebP images, lazy loading and streamed video

- Motion respects reduced-motion settings; no scroll-jacking

- Readable type, good contrast and keyboard-friendly navigation

### Proof and contact

- Named testimonials and client names used with permission

- One primary call to action on every page

- Short form with budget and timeline, plus WhatsApp or booking link

- Enquiries tracked in GA4

### Search, AI and ownership

- Person or Organization schema with sameAs links

- Indexable case-study pages with alt text and FAQs

- XML sitemap and Search Console set up

- Domain, hosting and code in your name

We design and build these sites as [portfolio and brand websites](https://gaa-tha.com/services/portfolio-brand-website-design), often alongside the identity itself, as on the [Colortek](https://gaa-tha.com/work/colortek) rebrand and website.

Q: How many projects should a portfolio website show?
A: Three to six well-documented projects usually work better than twenty thumbnails. Choose the projects closest to the work you want more of, and add a short archive page if you need to show range.

Q: Is a Behance or Instagram profile enough instead of a website?
A: No, not if you want to be found and trusted beyond your existing network. Platform profiles are useful distribution, but you do not own them, and their content is hard for Google and AI assistants to read as your work. Use them to point back to your own site.

Q: Do animations hurt SEO?
A: Animations do not hurt SEO when content is in the HTML and pages stay fast. Problems come from heavy scripts and videos that slow loading, or from text that only appears after animation code runs. Test Core Web Vitals on a real mobile phone.

Q: How much does a portfolio website cost in India?
A: Indicatively, a portfolio or brand website costs about ₹25,000–1.5 lakh from a freelancer, ₹1–4 lakh from a small studio and ₹2.5–10 lakh from a full-service agency in 2026. Original design, motion, copywriting and the number of case studies drive the difference.

Q: What should a new brand website include at launch?
A: A clear positioning line, the product or service with honest details, the founder story, proof such as reviews or certifications, and one obvious way to buy or enquire. Add analytics, schema and a sitemap from day one so search visibility starts building early.

Q: Can I show client work that is under an NDA?
A: Only with the client’s written permission. Without it, anonymise the client, describe the problem and your process in general terms, and show work that reveals nothing confidential.

## How to build a SaaS product: from MVP to first paying customers
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/saas-product-development-guide
Category: Websites & Apps. Published 2026-10-22.

To build a SaaS product that reaches paying customers, validate a painful problem with real buyers, scope an MVP around one core workflow, build on a proven stack, and get multi-tenancy, roles and billing right from day one. Then launch to a small group who pay, and price on the value delivered. With a focused team of three to five people, most B2B SaaS MVPs reach paying users in roughly three to five months.

### How do you validate a SaaS idea before writing code?

You validate a SaaS idea by proving that a specific type of buyer has a painful, frequent problem and will pay to solve it, before you build the product. Interest is cheap; payment is evidence.

1. **Interview 15–20 target buyers.** Ask how they handle the problem today, what it costs them in time or money, and what they have already tried. Do not pitch.

2. **Find the current workaround.** In India it is often Excel, WhatsApp groups, Tally exports or a person whose job is to stitch these together. A costly workaround is a strong signal.

3. **Test willingness to pay.** Offer a paid pilot, a pre-order at a founding-customer price, or a letter of intent. Five paying design partners beat five hundred newsletter sign-ups.

4. **Run a concierge version.** Deliver the outcome manually or with no-code tools for a few customers to learn the real workflow.

5. **Size the market honestly.** Indian SMB buyers are price-sensitive and expect support in their language; mid-market and enterprise buyers pay more but take months to sign. Global SMB markets (Canada, the US, the UK, Australia) often pay more per seat and buy self-serve.

Write down what would make you stop. If no one pays for a pilot after twenty conversations, change the problem, the buyer or the offer before changing the code.

### How do you scope an MVP that people will pay for?

A paid SaaS MVP solves one core workflow for one type of customer from start to finish, and leaves everything else for later. The test of scope: can a design partner use it every week without you on a call?

| In the MVP | Later |
|---|---|
| Sign-up, login, organisation and team invites | Single sign-on (SAML), SCIM provisioning |
| The one core workflow, end to end | Secondary workflows and nice-to-have screens |
| Basic roles: owner, admin, member | Custom roles and field-level permissions |
| Billing with one or two plans | Usage-based pricing, add-ons, reseller billing |
| One or two integrations customers cannot live without (for example Tally, Zoho, Shopify or Google Workspace) | An integrations marketplace and public API |
| CSV export, email notifications, onboarding checklist | Custom reports, dashboards builder |
| Internal admin panel and product analytics | Native mobile apps (a responsive web app is enough at first) |

Write the scope as user stories with acceptance criteria and a clear “not now” list. Most MVP overruns come from features that slipped in without a decision.

### Which tech stack should a SaaS MVP use?

A SaaS MVP should use a proven, widely hired stack with managed services, because speed of iteration and ease of hiring matter far more than novelty at this stage.

| Layer | Common choices | When to choose |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend | Next.js (React) with TypeScript | The default for web SaaS; good SEO for marketing pages and a large talent pool |
| Backend | Node.js (NestJS, Express) or Python (FastAPI, Django) | Node.js for one language across the stack; Python when AI, data or document processing is central |
| Database | PostgreSQL | Relational data, reporting, row-level security and pgvector for AI search in one place |
| Backend-as-a-service | Supabase (Postgres) or Firebase (NoSQL) | Fastest start for auth, storage and real-time; Supabase keeps you on Postgres if you outgrow it |
| Cloud | AWS, Google Cloud, Azure; Vercel for the frontend | Pick one; use the Mumbai or Hyderabad regions when Indian customers want data in India |
| Supporting services | Queues, email (Amazon SES, Postmark, Resend), Sentry, uptime monitoring | From the first release, not after the first outage |

Two rules save months. Use TypeScript end to end so the frontend and backend share types. And automate deployment, backups and environment setup in the first sprint; a product that only one developer can deploy is a business risk. Our [SaaS product development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/saas-product-development) work starts with this foundation before features.

### How should you handle multi-tenancy, authentication and roles?

Multi-tenancy, meaning many customer organisations sharing one product while seeing only their own data, should be designed in the first sprint, because adding it later touches every table, query and file.

| Model | How it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Shared database, tenant ID on every row | One database; Postgres row-level security enforces isolation | Most SMB and mid-market SaaS; cheapest to run |
| Schema per tenant | One database, a separate schema for each customer | Moderate isolation needs, fewer, larger tenants |
| Database per tenant | Each customer gets its own database | Enterprise, regulated sectors, customers who require data residency |

Start shared with row-level security, and keep the option to move a large customer to a dedicated database. Make everything tenant-aware: file storage paths, caches, search indexes, background jobs and logs.

For authentication, use a proven service such as Supabase Auth, Firebase Auth, Clerk, Auth0 or AWS Cognito rather than writing your own. Indian B2B users often expect phone OTP alongside email and Google sign-in; enterprise buyers in India and abroad will later ask for single sign-on through Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace. Model users, organisations, memberships and roles separately, so one person can belong to several organisations, and record an audit log of who changed what. Offer two-factor authentication for admins from launch.

### How do you set up billing, subscriptions and GST?

SaaS billing needs recurring payments, invoices, plan changes and failed-payment recovery, and for Indian founders it also needs GST and RBI e-mandate compliance built in.

| Option | Best for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Razorpay Subscriptions | Indian customers paying in INR | Cards, UPI AutoPay and e-mandates; GST-ready invoicing; also supports international cards |
| Stripe Billing | Global self-serve SaaS | Mature subscription tooling; onboarding for India-registered businesses has been invite-only since 2024, so check current status; some founders use a foreign entity |
| Merchant of record (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy and similar) | Selling to consumers and small businesses in many countries | The provider is the legal seller and handles VAT and sales tax worldwide, for a higher fee |
| Chargebee or similar billing layer | Complex plans across several gateways | Sits on top of gateways; worth it once pricing gets complicated |

**India specifics.** GST on SaaS sold to Indian customers is currently 18%; business customers need a GST invoice with their GSTIN to claim input tax credit. Exports of SaaS to overseas customers can be zero-rated under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) when conditions such as receiving payment in convertible foreign exchange are met. Under RBI’s e-mandate rules, recurring card and UPI AutoPay debits need a registered mandate and pre-debit notification, and debits above a set limit (₹15,000 for most categories at the time of writing) need the customer to authenticate each payment, so plan for annual-plan collection by invoice or bank transfer. **Selling abroad** brings local taxes: VAT in the UK and EU, GST/HST registration for digital services to consumers in Canada above a threshold, and US state sales tax in some states. Confirm your setup with a chartered accountant; the rules change and depend on your entity.

Whatever you choose, build proration, trials, dunning emails for failed payments, downloadable invoices and a self-serve billing page from launch.

### Which analytics and AI features belong in a SaaS MVP?

Every SaaS MVP needs product analytics that track activation and retention, while AI features belong only where they remove real work from the core workflow.

### Analytics

Use PostHog, Mixpanel or Amplitude for product events and GA4 for the marketing site. Define an activation event, the moment a new account first gets value (first invoice sent, first report shared), and track time to activation, weekly active accounts, feature usage and retention by monthly cohort. Pair the numbers with session recordings and a short in-app survey.

### AI features

AI earns its place when it drafts, extracts, classifies, summarises or answers questions inside the workflow the customer already uses. Good first features: reading invoices or purchase orders into structured data, drafting replies or reports, natural-language search over the customer’s own records using retrieval with pgvector, and an assistant that can take actions with the user’s permission. Build them on model APIs such as Claude, GPT or Gemini, keep the provider swappable, meter AI usage per tenant so heavy users do not erase your margin, and add evaluation tests and human review for anything that touches money or customers. Check each provider’s data-use terms for API traffic and say clearly in your privacy policy how customer data reaches the model. For deeper patterns, see our [AI agents for business guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-agents-for-business-guide), [AI workflow automation with n8n, Make and Zapier](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-workflow-automation-n8n-make-zapier), and [AI agent development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-agent-development).

### What security and compliance do you need: DPDP Act, GDPR and beyond?

A SaaS product handling personal data in India must comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, and products with users in the EU or UK must also meet GDPR; the engineering basics behind both are the same.

- **DPDP Act:** clear notice and consent for personal data, use only for the stated purpose, honour access, correction and erasure requests, apply reasonable security safeguards, and notify the Data Protection Board and affected users of breaches. The DPDP Rules were notified in November 2025 with obligations phasing in over roughly 18 months, and penalties can reach ₹250 crore, so build for them now. As a B2B SaaS you will often be a data processor for your customers, so offer a data processing agreement.

- **CERT-In directions:** certain cyber incidents must be reported to CERT-In within six hours, and logs retained for 180 days.

- **GDPR basics:** a lawful basis for processing, a data processing agreement, a published list of sub-processors, safeguards for transfers outside the EU such as standard contractual clauses, data subject rights, and breach notification within 72 hours. Canadian customers will ask about PIPEDA and provincial privacy laws.

- **Engineering basics:** encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access, secrets in a vault rather than code, tested backups and restores, dependency scanning, rate limiting and an audit log.

- **Enterprise proof:** a penetration test before your first large deal, then SOC 2 or ISO 27001 when buyers start asking for it.

This is a practical summary, not legal advice; have a lawyer review your privacy policy, terms and data processing agreement before launch.

### How should you launch and price a SaaS product?

Launch a SaaS product to a small group of paying design partners first, then open it up once onboarding works without hand-holding, and price on the value delivered rather than on your costs.

1. **Private beta:** 5–10 design partners on paid pilots, with a weekly feedback call and a shared roadmap.

2. **Self-serve readiness:** onboarding checklist, help articles, sample data and a working trial.

3. **Public launch:** a marketing site built for search and AI answers, comparison and use-case pages, LinkedIn and community launches, and outbound to your ideal customer list. Our [SEO, AEO and GEO guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog-seo-aeo-geo-guide) covers how buyers now find software.

On pricing, pick a value metric customers understand (per seat, per location, per invoice or per active project), offer two or three tiers, and discount annual plans. Indian SMB plans usually need INR pricing with GST shown clearly and a lower entry point; global plans can be priced in USD at higher levels, and regional pricing is normal. Free trials suit products that show value within days; freemium suits products that spread through teams. Avoid lifetime deals early; they fund the launch but tax every month after. Revisit pricing after the first 20–30 paying customers.

Indian founders selling globally should also plan support hours that overlap with customer time zones, USD invoicing and collection, and whether a foreign entity is needed for payments or investors; take tax and legal advice before incorporating abroad.

### What timeline, team and budget should you plan?

A focused B2B SaaS MVP typically takes three to five months from validation to first paying customers, with a core team of three to five people.

| Phase | Duration | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Validation | 2–4 weeks | Interviews, paid pilot commitments, problem statement |
| Product design | 2–4 weeks | User flows, clickable prototype, technical plan, scope with a “not now” list |
| MVP build | 8–14 weeks | Core workflow, auth, roles, billing, admin, analytics, two-week releases to design partners |
| Beta and launch | 4–6 weeks | Onboarding, help content, pricing page, first paying customers |

The core team: a founder acting as product owner, a product designer, two full-stack engineers, part-time QA and part-time DevOps. As an indicative 2026 Indian market range, a SaaS MVP built with an experienced agency or product studio costs ₹10–35 lakh, depending on workflow complexity, integrations and AI features; it is not a quote. An in-house team costs a similar amount every few months, which is why many founders build the MVP with a partner and hire as revenue arrives. Plan the user interface early with [app design and development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/app-design-development), and if a mobile companion app is on the roadmap, our [mobile app development cost guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/mobile-app-development-cost-in-india) sets out the numbers and our [mobile app development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/mobile-app-development) team can build it on the same backend.

### Should you build with no-code or custom code?

No-code is right for validating an idea and for internal tools; custom code is right once you have paying customers who need multi-tenancy, complex permissions, integrations and performance you control.

| Approach | Examples | Use it when | Move on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| No-code app builders | Bubble, Softr, Glide, FlutterFlow | Testing demand, concierge MVPs, simple workflows | Per-user costs climb, logic gets tangled, or buyers ask about security and data location |
| Internal tool builders | Retool, Appsmith | Admin panels and operations tools behind the product | Rarely; they often stay useful |
| Automation platforms | n8n, Make, Zapier | Glue between systems while the product is young | Volume or reliability needs justify proper backend jobs |
| Custom code | Next.js, Node.js or Python, Postgres | A product customers pay for and depend on | Not applicable |

A hybrid is common: custom code for the customer-facing product, an internal tool builder for operations, and automation for the long tail. Investors and enterprise buyers will ask who owns the code and how data is protected, so plan the move to custom before it becomes urgent.

If you have an idea or a no-code prototype, start with our [SaaS product development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/saas-product-development) page.

Q: How much does it cost to build a SaaS MVP in India?
A: As an indicative 2026 market range, a SaaS MVP built by an experienced Indian agency or product studio costs ₹10–35 lakh. The number depends on how complex the core workflow is, how many integrations it needs and whether AI features are included; it is a market range, not a quote.

Q: How long does it take to build a SaaS product?
A: A focused B2B SaaS MVP usually takes three to five months from validation to first paying customers. That covers two to four weeks of validation, two to four weeks of design, eight to fourteen weeks of build and a short beta.

Q: What is the best tech stack for a SaaS startup?
A: For most SaaS startups, Next.js with TypeScript on the frontend, Node.js or Python on the backend and PostgreSQL as the database is the safe default. Supabase or Firebase can speed up the first version, and AWS or Google Cloud handles scale.

Q: Is GST charged on SaaS in India?
A: Yes. SaaS sold to customers in India currently attracts 18% GST, and business customers need a GST invoice to claim input tax credit. Exports to overseas customers can be zero-rated under an LUT when conditions are met, so confirm the setup with a chartered accountant.

Q: Can an Indian SaaS company use Stripe?
A: Stripe’s onboarding for India-registered businesses has been invite-only since 2024, so check its current status before planning around it. Indian founders commonly use Razorpay for INR and international cards, a merchant-of-record provider such as Paddle for global sales, or a foreign entity with Stripe.

Q: Does the DPDP Act apply to my SaaS product?
A: Yes, if you process personal data of people in India, and also if you offer goods or services to people in India from abroad. Plan for consent, purpose limitation, data rights, security safeguards and breach notification, and offer customers a data processing agreement.

Q: Should I build my SaaS with no-code first?
A: No-code is a good way to test demand and run a concierge MVP cheaply. Move to custom code once paying customers need multi-tenancy, fine-grained permissions, integrations and security guarantees you control.

## Shopify integrations in India: payments, shipping, WhatsApp, ERP
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-integrations-for-indian-brands
Category: Shopify. Published 2026-10-22.

Indian Shopify brands need integrations in seven areas: payment gateways (Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue, PhonePe), one-click checkout and COD verification (GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout, Razorpay Magic Checkout), shipping (Shiprocket, Delhivery, Shipway, NimbusPost), WhatsApp (Interakt, WATI, AiSensy, Gallabox), GST invoicing and accounting (Tally, Zoho), marketplace sync, and tracking. Choose one tool per job, test it on a real order, and remove what you do not use.

### Which integrations does an Indian Shopify store need?

An Indian Shopify store needs one tool in each of ten categories at most, and many stores need fewer. Use this table to map your stack and spot gaps or overlaps.

| Category | Common options | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| Payment gateway | Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue, PhonePe | Rates by method, UPI success rate, settlement time, EMI and international cards |
| One-click checkout | GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout, Razorpay Magic Checkout | Pricing model, COD controls, discount and bundle support, tracking events |
| COD verification | Checkout-provider RTO tools, WhatsApp confirmation flows | Confirmation rate, RTO reduction, effect on conversion |
| Shipping | Shiprocket, Delhivery, Shipway, NimbusPost | Pincode coverage, courier mix, NDR handling, COD remittance cycle |
| WhatsApp | Interakt, WATI, AiSensy, Gallabox | Shopify triggers, template approvals, Meta message costs, team inbox |
| GST invoicing | GST invoice apps, accounting software | GSTIN capture, HSN codes, place of supply, credit notes |
| Accounting and ERP | Tally connectors, Zoho Books, Zoho Inventory, Odoo, ERPNext | Sync direction and frequency, SKU and ledger mapping, returns |
| Marketplaces | Multichannel order and inventory systems | Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and quick commerce coverage, stock buffers |
| Reviews and loyalty | Judge.me, Loox, Okendo, Nector, Smile.io | Speed impact, photo reviews, points on COD orders |
| Analytics and ads | GA4, Facebook & Instagram channel, Google & YouTube channel | Conversions API, deduplication, checkout events, consent |

Check what Shopify does natively before adding any of these; the [best Shopify features](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/best-shopify-features-for-ecommerce) guide lists the built-in tools.

### Which payment gateway and one-click checkout should you use?

Start with one reliable Indian gateway on Shopify checkout, and add a one-click checkout only when data shows checkout friction or COD losses. Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue and PhonePe all support UPI, cards, net banking and wallets; compare them on effective rates for your payment mix, UPI success rates, settlement speed, international card support and the quality of their Shopify integration. If you sell abroad from India, confirm which gateway accepts international cards and how foreign-currency payments settle; a brand registered in Canada or another Shopify Payments country can usually use Shopify Payments and Shop Pay instead.

One-click checkouts such as GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout and Razorpay Magic Checkout replace or overlay Shopify’s checkout with phone-number login, saved addresses across their network, prepaid offers and COD rules. They can raise conversion for mobile-first buyers, but check four things first:

1. Whether discounts, bundles and gift cards behave as they do on Shopify checkout.

2. Whether purchase events reach Meta, Google and GA4 with values, once each.

3. How orders, payment status and COD flags appear in Shopify and downstream tools.

4. The effective cost per order at your prepaid and COD mix.

The [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz) store pairs GoKwik checkout with Meta Pixel and Conversions API tracking, a common setup for Indian D2C brands.

### How do you handle COD verification and shipping?

Verify risky COD orders before dispatch and ship through one aggregator that covers your pincodes, because return-to-origin (RTO) on unverified COD orders is the largest avoidable cost in Indian D2C.

- **COD verification:** confirm orders above a set value or from high-RTO pincodes by automated WhatsApp message or call. One-click checkouts and shipping platforms offer RTO risk scores, and Shopify Flow can tag orders that need a check.

- **COD rules:** limit COD by order value or pincode, add a small COD fee, or offer a prepaid discount. [COD vs prepaid](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/cod-vs-prepaid) explains the economics.

- **Shipping aggregators:** Shiprocket, Shipway and NimbusPost connect many couriers with rate comparison, labels and tracking; Delhivery can also be integrated directly. Judge them on pincode coverage, non-delivery report (NDR) workflows, COD remittance timelines and branded tracking pages.

- **Pincode checker:** show delivery estimates and COD availability on the product page, before checkout.

### Which WhatsApp integration fits a Shopify store?

Choose a WhatsApp Business API provider with native Shopify triggers for orders, abandoned carts, COD confirmation and delivery updates; Interakt, WATI, AiSensy and Gallabox are common choices in India. Compare them on Shopify triggers, flow builder, shared team inbox, chatbot options, segmentation and support quality.

Costs have two parts: the provider’s subscription and Meta’s per-message charges, which vary by message category (marketing, utility, authentication) and by country. Roll out in this order:

1. Order confirmation and shipping updates (utility templates).

2. COD confirmation with one-tap confirm or cancel buttons.

3. Abandoned cart and checkout recovery.

4. Review requests timed to when the product has been used.

5. Campaigns to segments, such as lapsed buyers or a festive list, rather than blasts to everyone.

For bots that answer product questions, see [AI chatbots for website and WhatsApp](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/ai-chatbot-for-website-and-whatsapp).

### How do you connect Shopify to GST invoicing, Tally, Zoho and marketplaces?

Connect accounting and marketplaces through as few sync points as possible, with Shopify or your ERP named as the single source of truth for stock.

- **GST invoicing:** Shopify’s default order confirmations are not full GST invoices. Use a GST invoice app, a customised Order Printer template or your accounting software to issue invoices with GSTIN, HSN codes, place of supply and the correct CGST, SGST or IGST split, and capture the buyer’s GSTIN for B2B orders. Businesses above the e-invoicing turnover threshold also need IRN generation for B2B invoices.

- **Tally:** connectors push Shopify orders, payments and returns into Tally as vouchers; check how they map SKUs, ledgers, gateway settlements and COD remittances.

- **Zoho:** Zoho Books and Zoho Inventory offer Shopify integrations for orders, items and stock.

- **ERP:** Odoo, ERPNext or a custom ERP connect through the Shopify Admin API; see [custom ERP vs Odoo vs ERPNext vs Tally](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/custom-erp-vs-odoo-vs-erpnext-vs-tally) and our [ERP development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/erp-development) service.

- **Marketplaces:** a multichannel order and inventory system syncs stock and orders across Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and quick commerce, with buffers to prevent overselling. The [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee) engagement is an example of one team running a Shopify website alongside Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart.

### Which reviews, loyalty and tracking integrations are worth it?

Reviews and tracking are worth setting up at launch; loyalty is worth adding once repeat purchase is part of the model.

- **Reviews:** Judge.me, Loox, Okendo or Yotpo for photo and video reviews, review requests by email and WhatsApp, and star ratings in Google. Pick the one that loads lightest on mobile.

- **Loyalty and referrals:** Nector, Smile.io or similar. Decide whether COD orders earn points only after delivery, to avoid rewarding RTO.

- **Analytics:** GA4 through the Google & YouTube channel or a tag manager, with ecommerce events checked on a real order.

- **Meta Conversions API:** Shopify’s Facebook & Instagram channel sends server-side events at its higher data-sharing settings; third-party checkouts need their own Conversions API setup, deduplicated against the Pixel.

Tracking errors are the most expensive silent failure in a Shopify stack. Reconcile Shopify orders with Meta and Google purchases weekly, as described in the [D2C ecommerce growth guide](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/d2c-ecommerce-growth-guide).

### How do you choose Shopify integrations without bloating the store?

Give every integration one job, one owner and one review date. Rules that keep a store fast and affordable:

1. Use native Shopify first (Search & Discovery, Flow, Bundles, Shopify Email, Inbox) and add an app only to fill a real gap.

2. One tool per job: one primary gateway, one checkout, one shipping aggregator, one WhatsApp provider, one reviews app.

3. Prefer apps that use theme app blocks and embeds, which remove cleanly, over apps that inject code.

4. Test mobile speed before and after each install; the [Shopify speed and conversion checklist](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-speed-and-conversion-checklist) shows how.

5. Test each integration on real orders: prepaid, COD, discounted and returned.

6. Review apps and bills every quarter and remove anything that has not earned its fee.

A sensible **launch stack** is one gateway, one shipping aggregator, one reviews app, a WhatsApp provider for order updates and COD confirmation, a GST invoice app, and the Facebook & Instagram and Google & YouTube channels. Add a one-click checkout, loyalty, Tally or ERP sync and a marketplace order system in the **growth stack**, once order volume or a measured problem justifies each one.

gaa-tha sets up and maintains these stacks through [Shopify development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) and [Shopify store management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-store-management), and builds custom connectors or [AI workflow automation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ai-workflow-automation) where no app fits.

Q: Which is the best payment gateway for Shopify in India?
A: There is no single best gateway: Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue and PhonePe all integrate with Shopify and support UPI, cards and net banking. Choose on effective rates for your payment mix, UPI success rates, settlement speed and support, and renegotiate as volume grows.

Q: Should I use GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout or Razorpay Magic Checkout?
A: All three offer one-click login, address prefill and COD controls, so the right one depends on pricing at your order mix, RTO features, compatibility with your discounts and bundles, and how cleanly it sends tracking events. Pilot one and compare conversion and RTO against Shopify checkout before committing.

Q: Can Shopify sync with Tally?
A: Yes, through third-party connectors that push orders, payments and returns into Tally. Check ledger and SKU mapping and how gateway settlements and COD remittances are recorded; larger businesses often route Shopify through an ERP or order management system instead.

Q: Does Shopify generate GST invoices?
A: Shopify’s default order confirmations are not full GST invoices. Use a GST invoice app, a customised Order Printer template or your accounting software to issue invoices with GSTIN, HSN codes and the correct tax split.

Q: How many apps should a Shopify store have?
A: As few as the business genuinely needs; there is no fixed number. What matters is that each app has a clear job, is used, and does not slow the mobile storefront, so review the list every quarter.

Q: Can Indian Shopify stores use Shopify Payments?
A: Shopify Payments and Shop Pay are not generally available to Indian-registered stores. Indian stores use third-party gateways such as Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue or PhonePe, often alongside a one-click checkout.

## How much does a Shopify website cost in India in 2026?
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-website-cost-in-india
Category: Shopify. Published 2026-10-22.

The best budget for a first Shopify D2C store in India is usually about ₹75,000 to ₹2.5 lakh for the build, meaning a premium theme customised by a specialist studio, plus roughly ₹5,000 to ₹20,000 a month for Shopify, apps and upkeep before payment fees and marketing. These are indicative 2026 market ranges, not a quote. A DIY store can launch for far less; a custom-designed theme typically costs ₹2.5 lakh to ₹8 lakh or more.

### What is the best budget to create a Shopify website in India?

For a first D2C brand selling a focused range, ₹75,000 to ₹2.5 lakh for the build is the budget that usually buys the most: a premium Shopify theme customised by a team that understands Indian checkout, COD and tracking, with a handful of custom sections where they matter. That is an indicative 2026 market range, not a gaa-tha price list; your number depends on catalogue size, integrations and content.

Why this band? Below it, stores are usually a theme with products dropped in: fine for testing demand, weak on conversion, tracking and speed. Above it, you are paying for a custom design system, complex features or Shopify Plus capabilities that a first-year brand rarely needs. The money saved is better spent on product photography, the first months of ads and retention.

Three situations justify spending more from day one: a brand with existing revenue migrating from another platform (see [Shopify migration](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-migration)), a product that needs a custom tool such as a configurator or kit builder, and a brand whose positioning depends on a distinctive design. If you are still choosing a platform, read [why Shopify is the best ecommerce platform for most brands](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/why-shopify-is-best-for-ecommerce) first.

### What goes into the cost of a Shopify website?

A Shopify website’s cost is the sum of one-time build costs and recurring running costs, and a quote that shows only one of them misleads. The components:

1. **Shopify subscription.** A monthly plan fee, priced in INR for Indian stores, with a discount for annual billing. Plans and prices change, so check Shopify’s current India pricing page. Shopify Plus is a separate, much higher tier.

2. **Theme.** Shopify’s own themes are free. Premium themes in the Shopify Theme Store are a one-time purchase, typically in the low hundreds of US dollars (roughly ₹15,000 to ₹45,000 at current exchange rates), with updates included.

3. **Design and development.** The largest one-time cost: site structure, page design, theme customisation or a custom theme, custom sections, integrations, tracking and testing.

4. **Apps.** Reviews, WhatsApp, loyalty, subscriptions, upsells, GST invoices. Most bill monthly, many in US dollars.

5. **Payment gateway fees.** A percentage per transaction charged by Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, CCAvenue or PhonePe, varying by payment method and negotiable at volume. Shopify Payments is not generally available to Indian-registered stores, and Shopify may charge its own transaction fee on orders through third-party gateways depending on plan; confirm on the current pricing page.

6. **One-click checkout.** GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout and Razorpay Magic Checkout are usually priced as a percentage of order value or a per-order fee, sometimes with monthly minimums.

7. **Content and photography.** Product photos, lifestyle images, short videos, and copy for products, collections and key pages.

8. **SEO setup.** Site structure, redirects, metadata, structured data, collection copy and Google Search Console.

9. **Maintenance and support.** Theme and app updates, fixes, new landing pages and campaign changes after launch.

10. **Smaller items.** A domain (a .com or .in costs roughly ₹800 to ₹1,500 a year), business email, WhatsApp Business API message charges and shipping aggregator fees.

### How much does a Shopify website cost in India by tier?

Shopify website costs in India fall into five tiers, from a founder-built store on a free theme to a Shopify Plus or headless build. All figures below are indicative 2026 Indian market ranges for the one-time build, not quotes.

| Tier | Indicative build cost (INR) | Typical timeline | What you get | Suits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DIY on a free or premium theme | ₹0–₹40,000 (mostly the theme) plus your time | 1–3 weeks | Theme set up by the founder, products uploaded, gateway and shipping connected | Testing demand with a small catalogue |
| Freelancer template setup | ₹25,000–₹75,000 | 2–4 weeks | Theme configured, pages and products set up, gateway and shipping app connected | Very small budgets with a clear brief |
| Studio theme customisation | ₹75,000–₹2.5 lakh | 4–8 weeks | Premium theme adapted to the brand, custom sections, Indian checkout and COD rules, tracking, speed work, training | Most first D2C stores |
| Custom theme by an agency | ₹2.5 lakh–₹8 lakh+ | 8–14 weeks | Bespoke UX and design, custom-coded theme, metaobject content model, builders and selectors, conversion-led templates | Funded or established brands, design-led categories |
| Shopify Plus or headless | ₹8 lakh–₹30 lakh+ plus the Plus subscription | 3–6 months | Checkout extensions, B2B, expansion stores, Hydrogen storefront, ERP integrations | High-volume brands and complex operations |

Rates in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR tend to sit higher than in tier-2 cities, and agencies abroad typically charge several times more for the same scope. See [Shopify development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) and [Shopify Plus and headless development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-plus-headless-development) for what each scope includes.

### What does it cost to run a Shopify store every month?

A small Shopify store in India typically costs ₹5,000 to ₹20,000 a month to run before payment fees and marketing, and a scaling D2C brand with retention tools and a management retainer can spend ₹40,000 to ₹1 lakh or more. These are indicative ranges; the mix below decides your number.

| Item | Indicative monthly range (INR) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Shopify plan | Check current India pricing | Annual billing is cheaper; upgrade when reports, staff accounts or lower fees justify it |
| Apps | ₹3,000–₹25,000 | Reviews, WhatsApp, loyalty, subscriptions, upsell, invoicing; many billed in US dollars |
| Payment gateway | A percentage of prepaid sales | Rates differ by method (UPI, cards, international cards, EMI) and fall with negotiated volume |
| One-click checkout | A percentage of orders or a per-order fee | Compare the effective rate on your prepaid and COD mix |
| WhatsApp messaging | ₹2,000–₹20,000+ | Provider subscription plus Meta’s per-message charges, which depend on message category |
| Email | Free allowance, then usage-based | Shopify Email or a dedicated platform |
| Maintenance | ₹10,000–₹60,000 | Fixes, updates and landing pages; full store management costs more |

Over three years, running costs usually exceed the build fee. That is why a lean app list and a theme that does more natively save more money than haggling over the build quote. The [best Shopify features](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/best-shopify-features-for-ecommerce) guide lists the native tools that replace paid apps.

### What does a realistic first-year Shopify budget look like?

A realistic first-year budget for a studio-built Shopify store in India lands around ₹5 lakh to ₹6 lakh before the Shopify plan, payment fees and advertising, in the illustrative example below. It is a worked example using mid-points of the indicative ranges above, not a quote, for a skincare brand launching 25 products.

| Line item | Illustrative year-one cost (INR) | Assumption |
|---|---|---|
| Build: studio theme customisation | ₹1,50,000 | Premium theme, six custom sections, checkout, shipping and tracking |
| Premium theme licence | ₹30,000 | One-time Theme Store purchase |
| Product photography | ₹60,000 | White-background and lifestyle images for 25 products |
| Copy for products and key pages | ₹25,000 | Product, collection, about and FAQ copy |
| Apps | ₹96,000 | About ₹8,000 a month: reviews, WhatsApp, invoicing, upsell |
| WhatsApp message charges | ₹60,000 | About ₹5,000 a month in Meta template charges |
| Maintenance after launch | ₹1,35,000 | About ₹15,000 a month for nine months |
| Total before plan, fees and ads | ≈ ₹5,56,000 | Add the Shopify plan, gateway and checkout fees, and media spend |

Notice that the build is only about a quarter of year-one spend. That is the point of the exercise: a brand that spends its whole budget on the build has nothing left for content, retention and the fixes that real data will demand.

### What hidden costs catch Indian Shopify stores out?

The hidden costs that hurt most are app creep, COD returns, missing content and broken tracking, because none of them appears in a build quote.

- **App creep.** Every trial app left installed bills monthly, and some leave code in the theme after removal.

- **Dollar billing and GST.** Many apps and themes bill in US dollars, so exchange rates move the cost, and GST applies to imported digital services; check how it appears on your invoices.

- **Transaction fees.** Model the gateway fee and any Shopify fee on third-party gateways together, at your real order volume.

- **COD and RTO.** Return-to-origin shipments cost two-way shipping and packaging; a high COD share without verification is the most expensive hidden cost in Indian D2C. See [COD vs prepaid](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/cod-vs-prepaid).

- **Content gaps.** Many quotes assume you supply photos and copy; if you cannot, the launch slips or the store goes live with weak content.

- **Migration losses.** Moving from WooCommerce or a custom site without redirects and customer and order history costs rankings and repeat sales.

- **Theme upkeep.** Heavily edited themes are harder to update; budget a little each year to keep the theme current.

- **Tracking fixes.** A broken Meta Pixel, Conversions API or GA4 setup silently wastes ad budget; pay for verification, not just installation.

### How should a first D2C brand phase its Shopify budget?

Phase Shopify spend in three stages so each rupee follows evidence rather than guesses.

### Phase 1: launch (months 0–2)

A premium theme customised to the brand, product pages with real photography, an Indian payment gateway with COD rules, shipping integration, Meta Pixel with Conversions API, GA4, basic SEO and no more than eight to ten apps. Spend most of the one-time budget here but hold back 20 to 30 percent.

### Phase 2: learn (months 3–6)

Use analytics and session recordings to find where buyers drop off, then spend on the specific fixes: a bundle or kit section, better product page content, a one-click checkout if prepaid conversion is weak, WhatsApp flows. This is where [conversion rate optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/conversion-rate-optimisation) earns its fee.

### Phase 3: scale (months 6–18)

Once the store converts and the unit economics hold, invest in a custom theme or design refresh, loyalty and subscriptions, marketplace and ERP integrations, and international selling. Shopify Plus, a headless storefront or a [mobile shopping app](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-app-development) belong here, and only when order volume justifies them.

### Why do Shopify website quotes in India vary so much?

Shopify quotes vary because they describe different scopes, not because some providers are cheap and others greedy. The biggest drivers:

- Custom design versus theme customisation.

- The number of unique templates: home, collections, product types, landing pages, about, blog.

- Custom features such as combo builders, kit selectors, pincode checkers, quizzes and subscription flows.

- Integrations: one-click checkout, shipping, WhatsApp, Tally or ERP, marketplaces.

- Catalogue size and data work: products, variants, metafields, and migrating customers and orders.

- Content: who writes copy and who shoots the products.

- Tracking and speed work: Pixel, Conversions API, GA4 and Core Web Vitals.

- Post-launch support: bug-fix window, training and any retainer.

The [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz) store shows the custom-feature end of the range: a concern-led store with a kit selector, combo builder, pincode checker, GoKwik checkout and Pixel and Conversions API tracking, all of which add scope beyond a theme setup.

### How do you compare Shopify quotes fairly?

Compare Shopify quotes by putting every provider on the same scope sheet and asking the same questions.

| Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Which theme, and will you customise it or build a custom one? | Decides cost, speed and future updates |
| How many templates and custom sections are included? | The real measure of design and development work |
| Which integrations are included and tested? | Checkout, gateway, shipping, WhatsApp and tracking are where launches slip |
| Who supplies photos and copy? | Content is often excluded without saying so |
| Is tracking set up and verified on a real order? | Broken tracking wastes ad spend from the first day |
| What mobile speed target will you meet? | Apps and heavy media slow stores; ask for a benchmark |
| How long is the post-launch support window? | Bugs surface after real orders |
| Who owns the store, theme code and accounts? | You should own everything, in your name |

Then compare price per included item, not the headline figure. For a full checklist and scorecard, read [how to choose a Shopify agency in India](https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-shopify-agency-in-india).

### Does building in India make sense for an international Shopify store?

Yes, for many brands in Canada, the UK, the Gulf and elsewhere, an Indian Shopify team offers strong value, provided the brief, time zones and communication are managed well. The cost picture differs abroad: Shopify Payments and Shop Pay are available in many countries, which simplifies checkout and fees, while apps and plans bill in local currency or US dollars. Ask an Indian partner about overlapping working hours, experience with your market’s payments, taxes and shipping, and who owns the accounts.

Q: What is the cheapest way to start a Shopify store in India?
A: The cheapest way is a free Shopify theme you set up yourself, with an Indian payment gateway, a shipping aggregator and only essential apps, which costs little beyond the monthly plan. It works for testing demand; expect to invest in design, tracking and conversion once sales start.

Q: How much does a Shopify developer charge in India?
A: Indicative 2026 market rates vary widely: freelancers often quote from about ₹25,000 for a template setup, while studios and agencies quote from about ₹75,000 to several lakh depending on scope. Compare providers on a fixed written scope rather than on hourly rates.

Q: How much does Shopify cost per month in India?
A: Shopify’s plans are priced in INR for Indian stores, with a discount for annual billing; check the current India pricing page because plans and prices change. Add apps, gateway fees, messaging and maintenance to estimate the real monthly cost.

Q: Is a custom Shopify theme worth it for a new brand?
A: Usually not in the first year. A premium theme customised with a few custom sections delivers most of the benefit at a fraction of the cost; a custom theme makes sense once the brand knows what converts or needs a distinctive experience.

Q: How long does it take to build a Shopify website?
A: A customised theme typically takes four to eight weeks with content ready, a custom theme eight to fourteen weeks, and Shopify Plus or headless projects three to six months. Content and integration readiness decide the timeline more often than development.

## Website development cost in India: a 2026 pricing guide
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/website-development-cost-in-india
Category: Websites & Apps. Published 2026-10-22.

In 2026, most Indian businesses should budget roughly ₹50,000–₹2 lakh for a professionally built 5–10 page website, ₹1.5–10 lakh for a corporate or B2B site, ₹75,000–2.5 lakh for a first Shopify store and ₹5 lakh upward for a custom web app. These are indicative market ranges, not quotes. Then set aside 15–25% of the build cost every year for hosting, maintenance and content, because that is what keeps the site earning.

### How much does a website cost in India in 2026?

A website in India costs anywhere from about ₹10,000 for a freelancer-built landing page to ₹60 lakh or more for a custom web application built by a full-service agency or engineering firm. The table shows typical 2026 market ranges by website type and by who builds it.

| Website type | Usually includes | Freelancer | Small studio | Full-service agency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Landing page | One page, enquiry form or WhatsApp button, tracking | ₹10,000–40,000 | ₹30,000–1 lakh | ₹75,000–2 lakh |
| Small business website | 5–10 pages, theme or light custom design, editable CMS, forms | ₹20,000–75,000 | ₹50,000–2 lakh | ₹1.5–4 lakh |
| Corporate or B2B website | 15–50 pages, product catalogue, RFQ forms, CRM link, two or more languages | ₹75,000–2 lakh | ₹1.5–5 lakh | ₹3–12 lakh+ |

| Custom web app or portal (MVP) | Logins, dashboards, workflows, integrations | ₹2–8 lakh | ₹5–25 lakh | ₹15–60 lakh+ |

**These are indicative 2026 Indian market ranges, not a quote and not a gaa-tha price list.** They exclude 18% GST, domain, hosting and paid third-party software. Treat the ranges as a sense check: a quote far below the bottom of a range usually leaves something out, and one far above should explain what extra it delivers.

### Why do freelancers, studios and agencies quote so differently?

Quotes differ because you are buying different amounts of strategy, design, writing, engineering and accountability, not just “a website”. A website is effort in disguise: a 10-page site with original design and written content is typically 60–150 hours of discovery, structure, copy, design, development, testing and launch work.

- **Freelancer.** One person, often strongest at one skill, usually development or design. Lowest cost and direct contact; you supply content, project management and decisions, and you depend on one person’s availability.

- **Small studio.** Two to ten people covering design and development, sometimes copy. A good middle ground for brand and small business sites; check who handles content and what happens after launch.

- **Full-service digital agency.** Strategy, branding, copywriting, photography, development, SEO and marketing under one roof. Higher cost, but one accountable team and a site connected to the campaigns that will send it traffic.

- **Product engineering firm.** Larger engineering teams for web apps, portals and SaaS. Strong process and scale; often more than a marketing site needs.
