Out-of-stocks on quick commerce are fixed by treating availability as a weekly operation: tracking fill rate per dark store rather than per city, responding to purchase orders fast, concentrating on a short list of hero SKUs, and planning stock around festivals and weekends. Repeated unavailability lowers ranking and wastes ad spend, so availability comes before content and ads in any growth plan.

### Why are out-of-stocks so damaging on quick commerce?

When a customer opens the app in a neighbourhood and your product shows as unavailable, they buy a competitor and the platform records a lost conversion against your listing. Do that often enough and placement drops. If ads are running, the click is paid for anyway. The damage compounds quietly because dashboards report averages that look fine.

It also undermines every other investment. Better thumbnails, stronger titles and search ads all depend on the product being there when the customer looks, which is why availability is the first lever in any quick-commerce growth plan.

### How do you measure availability properly?

Platform dashboards show stock and availability per dark store. Pull that view weekly for each hero SKU and record fill rate per store, not per city. A city at 85 percent availability may contain ten stores at zero, and those are usually the stores with the most demand.

Set a simple threshold for action, and assign one person to look at the report every week. This is the core routine in our [Blinkit](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-account-management) and [Instamart account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/instamart-account-management) work.

### What causes out-of-stocks and how do you fix each cause?

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Late or short purchase-order fulfilment | Fixed dispatch rhythm; PO acknowledgement within a day |
| Too many SKUs spread thinly | Cut to hero SKUs; earn expansion with velocity |
| Demand spikes at festivals and weekends | Seasonal stock plan agreed with the category team in advance |
| Inbound rejections (damaged, mislabelled, short shelf life) | Packaging and labelling QC before dispatch |
| Store not mapped for the SKU | Review store mapping with the platform; request additions where demand exists |

### What does a weekly availability routine look like?

Monday: pull store-level availability for hero SKUs and flag stores below threshold. Tuesday: reconcile open purchase orders and dispatch status. Midweek: chase inbound issues and confirm next PO quantities against velocity. Friday: review ratings and any listing changes. Monthly: reconcile POs, invoices and deductions.

The routine is unglamorous, which is why it is often skipped, and why brands that do it gain share. A manufacturer supplying bulk and packaged snacks, like [Ghanshyam Snacks](https://gaa-tha.com/work/ghanshyam-snacks), would build its dispatch calendar around it. [Quick commerce management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency) runs this routine across platforms.

Q: What is a good fill rate on quick commerce?
A: Aim for near-complete availability on hero SKUs in your priority stores, and judge yourself at store level rather than by a city average. Any store with repeated zeros needs a specific fix.

Q: Should I pause ads when a SKU is out of stock?
A: Yes, in the affected cities. Paying for clicks on an unavailable listing wastes budget and worsens the platform’s view of your conversion rate.

Q: How far ahead should I plan stock for festivals?
A: Agree quantities with the category team several weeks before the season, because the platform’s buying calendar runs ahead of the consumer calendar and inbound capacity tightens near festivals.

Q: Can an agency manage purchase orders and availability for me?
A: Yes. Availability tracking, PO coordination and monthly reconciliation are core parts of quick-commerce account management, alongside content, promotions and ads.

## Flipkart ads guide: PLA, PCA and sale-event planning
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/flipkart-ads-guide
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Flipkart ads are sponsored placements bought through Flipkart’s advertising platform: Product Listing Ads (PLA) that promote individual listings in search and browse results on a cost-per-click basis, and Product Contextual Ads (PCA) that place banner-style creative in contextual slots. They work best on listings that already convert, and they need separate plans and budgets for Flipkart’s sale events, when traffic and competition both rise.

### What ad formats does Flipkart offer?

| Format | How it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Product Listing Ads (PLA) | Sponsored listings in search and browse, cost per click | Everyday demand capture on hero SKUs |
| Product Contextual Ads (PCA) | Banner creative in contextual placements, cost per impression or click | Launches, ranges, sale-event visibility |
| Other placements | Brand and event-linked options that change over time | Check current availability with the platform |

Formats and buying models change periodically; the principles below hold.

### How should Flipkart campaigns be structured?

Separate campaigns for brand keywords, category keywords and competitor terms, so bids and budgets can differ. Group SKUs by margin so that ad spend is capped where margins are thin. Use automatic targeting only to discover new search terms, then move the winners into manual campaigns and add negatives weekly.

Listing quality comes first: Flipkart’s catalogue QC is strict, and a listing with weak images or incomplete attributes will convert poorly whatever the bid. [Listing optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-listing-optimisation) precedes ads in our process.

### How do you plan for Flipkart sale events?

Flipkart’s sale events concentrate demand into a few days. Prepare weeks ahead: confirm event participation and pricing with the category team, secure stock in Flipkart’s warehousing where used, build event creative for PCA, and set higher daily budgets for the event window with a plan to taper afterwards. Expect higher cost per click during the event and judge it on total contribution over the window, not on daily ROAS.

### How do you measure Flipkart ads properly?

Track return on ad spend per SKU, cost per click trend, and the share of sales from ads versus organic. Watch organic rank and sales for the two weeks after a paid push; the aim is for paid velocity to lift organic placement. Fold ad spend into a monthly marketplace P&L alongside fees and returns, so decisions reflect profit rather than platform metrics. [Marketplace ads management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-ads-management) and [Flipkart seller management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/flipkart-seller-management) cover this end to end. A value-led fashion or home brand growing on Flipkart, or a D2C brand like [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz) adding marketplaces to its store, would apply the same rules.

Q: What is the difference between PLA and PCA on Flipkart?
A: PLA promotes individual listings in search and browse results on a cost-per-click basis. PCA places banner creative in contextual slots for range or launch visibility. Most brands run PLA always-on and PCA around events.

Q: How much should I budget for Flipkart ads?
A: Start with a small daily budget on brand and close category terms and scale on per-SKU return. Costs are auction-based and vary by category and season, rising during sale events.

Q: Do Flipkart ads work for new listings with no reviews?
A: They can generate initial traffic, but conversion is usually low without reviews and strong images. Fix the listing and gather early reviews before increasing spend.

Q: Should I participate in every Flipkart sale event?
A: No. Participate where the event fits your category and the required pricing still leaves a positive contribution. Plan stock and creative in advance for the events you choose.

## Flipkart Minutes vs Amazon Now vs Blinkit: which first?
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/flipkart-minutes-vs-amazon-now-vs-blinkit
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Blinkit is a standalone quick-commerce network with wide category coverage; Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now are quick-delivery services built on top of Flipkart and Amazon, so brands already selling on those marketplaces can often extend into them faster. For a brand starting from nothing, Blinkit is usually the first test. For a brand with a strong marketplace presence, the marketplace-linked service is the lower-effort addition.

### How do the three services differ for a brand?

| Aspect | Blinkit | Flipkart Minutes | Amazon Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foundation | Standalone quick-commerce network | Flipkart marketplace and logistics | Amazon marketplace and fulfilment |
| Onboarding route | Brand or distributor partnership with category review | Linked to Flipkart seller or brand relationship | Linked to Amazon seller account and Brand Registry |
| Best starting point for | Brands with retail or D2C demand in metros | Existing Flipkart sellers | Existing Amazon sellers with strong reviews |

Coverage, categories and terms change often on all three; treat this as orientation.

The practical difference is effort. A standalone network means a separate relationship, separate catalogue submission and separate operations. A marketplace-linked service can reuse much of what you already have, but it inherits the marketplace’s account health rules and listing quality.

### Which should a brand launch on first?

If you already sell on Amazon with Brand Registry and good ratings, Amazon Now is the natural extension. If Flipkart is your stronger marketplace, Flipkart Minutes follows the same logic. If you have neither, Blinkit gives the clearest read on whether your product suits quick commerce at all.

Whichever you choose, the same preparation applies: a short list of hero SKUs with clear margins after platform terms, spec-ready images, complete barcodes and licences, and a plan for who watches availability each week. Our [Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/flipkart-minutes-amazon-now-onboarding) and [Blinkit onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-onboarding) pages cover the specifics.

### Can the same catalogue serve all three?

Largely, yes. Pack shots, titles with pack sizes and attribute data carry over, with adjustments to each platform’s image dimensions and field structure. Marketplace-linked services may pull from your existing marketplace listings, so those listings need to be quick-commerce ready: legible thumbnails, accurate pack sizes and current pricing. [Listing optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-listing-optimisation) on the marketplace side therefore helps the quick-delivery side too.

### How does this fit a wider channel plan?

Treat quick delivery as one layer of a channel plan in which the D2C store owns the range and the relationship, marketplaces carry hero SKUs, and quick commerce carries compact packs in proven cities. A brand with a large catalogue, like [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee), would pick a handful of packs for quick delivery rather than mirror the marketplace range. [Quick commerce management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency) runs the platforms as one operation.

Q: Do I need a Flipkart seller account for Flipkart Minutes?
A: Flipkart Minutes is built on Flipkart’s marketplace and logistics, so an existing Flipkart relationship is the usual route. Requirements and routes change, so confirm the current process before planning.

Q: Is Amazon Now available everywhere in India?
A: No. Quick-delivery coverage is limited to select cities and expands over time. Check current coverage in your target cities before committing stock.

Q: Is Blinkit better than Flipkart Minutes or Amazon Now?
A: None is universally better. Blinkit is a dedicated quick-commerce network; the other two are extensions of marketplaces. The right first choice depends on where your existing accounts and demand are.

Q: Can one agency manage all three?
A: Yes. The operating rhythm of availability, purchase orders, content, promotions, ads and reconciliation is similar across platforms, which is why we run them as one operation.

## Getting approved on Myntra, Nykaa Fashion and AJIO
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/getting-approved-on-myntra-nykaa-fashion-ajio
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Myntra, Nykaa Fashion and AJIO are curated platforms: a brand is approved on the strength of its identity, catalogue quality, imagery and commercial fit before it sells a single unit. Approval takes weeks rather than days and depends on presentation. Brands that arrive with a clear story, consistent model photography, complete size and attribute data and realistic pricing are approved faster and placed better.

### What do fashion and beauty marketplaces look for?

Category teams assess whether the brand adds something to their assortment: a distinct positioning, a price band that fits the platform’s customers, a catalogue deep enough to merchandise, and imagery that meets the platform’s standard without rework. They also check brand ownership, existing sales channels and the ability to fulfil at the platform’s service levels.

The application is therefore a brand presentation as much as a form. A brand built with a clear identity from the start, such as [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz), has most of what an eligibility review asks for already in hand.

### What documents and data are required?

Typically GST, PAN, bank details, a registered trademark or a pending application with authorisation, and for beauty products the applicable manufacturing or import licences and ingredient declarations. Product data includes style codes, colours, sizes with a size chart, fabric or ingredient details, care instructions and MRP. Requirements differ by platform and change over time; verify the current list before applying. Our [Myntra](https://gaa-tha.com/services/myntra-onboarding), [Nykaa](https://gaa-tha.com/services/nykaa-onboarding) and [AJIO onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/ajio-onboarding) pages keep the checklists current.

### How should the catalogue and imagery be prepared?

Each platform publishes image specifications: model shots against a specified background, a set of angles per style, a detail shot, and consistent lighting and cropping across the range. Submissions that fall short are sent back, which is the most common reason approval takes longer than expected.

Plan one shoot to cover all three platforms plus your own store, producing the required angles for each. [Ecommerce product photography](https://gaa-tha.com/services/product-photography-ecommerce) plans shoots against platform specs, and AI-assisted imagery can extend a range where a full model shoot is not practical.

### What happens after approval?

Listings go live style by style after catalogue QC. From then on the work is keeping style data accurate, managing sizes and returns, planning seasonal drops, participating in the platform’s events and running ads where they pay. Pricing and assortment often need to differ slightly per platform. [Fashion marketplace growth](https://gaa-tha.com/services/fashion-marketplace-growth) is the plan that ties these together across Myntra, Nykaa Fashion, AJIO and Flipkart.

Q: How long does Myntra approval take?
A: Several weeks is typical, and longer if the catalogue or images need to be resubmitted. A complete application with spec-ready imagery and full attribute data is the fastest route.

Q: Can a new brand get on Nykaa Fashion?
A: Yes, if the brand fits the platform’s positioning and price band and presents a coherent identity and catalogue. Existing D2C or retail sales strengthen the case but are not the only factor.

Q: Do I need a trademark to sell on Myntra or AJIO?
A: A registered trademark, or a pending application with supporting authorisation, is normally required as proof of brand ownership. Apply for the trademark before approaching the platforms.

Q: Should I apply to all three at once?
A: You can, but it is often better to secure one approval, learn the catalogue and operating requirements, and then apply to the next with a stronger, proven submission.

## How to sell on Blinkit: a brand’s step-by-step guide
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-blinkit
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

To sell on Blinkit, a brand applies through the platform’s seller or brand-partner route, passes a category review, submits business and brand documents, uploads a spec-compliant catalogue, agrees commercial terms and fulfils a first purchase order into the cities chosen for launch. The process takes several weeks. This outline covers each step and the first-month priorities that decide whether the listing survives.

### Who can sell on Blinkit?

Blinkit works with brands and their authorised distributors across grocery, snacks, beverages, personal care, home care, baby care, pet supplies and a growing range of general merchandise. The platform’s category teams look for products with proven velocity, compact packaging and margins that can carry platform terms and promotions.

New brands are not excluded, but they need a clear story: where the product sells today, why a Blinkit customer would pick it, and which packs are built for a ten-minute basket.

### What documents and data does Blinkit onboarding need?

Expect to provide GST registration, PAN, bank details, a trademark certificate or brand authorisation letter, an FSSAI licence for food and beverages, and product-level data such as EAN barcodes, MRP, shelf life, dimensions and weight. Requirements vary by category and can change; confirm the current checklist with the platform or with your agency before submitting.

Mismatched barcodes and missing licence numbers are the most common reasons an application stalls. A single master sheet per SKU prevents most of it.

### How should the catalogue and images be prepared?

Blinkit listings are seen as small thumbnails in a fast scroll, so the pack shot must be clean, front-facing and legible at a small size. Titles should carry the brand, product and pack size; descriptions cover ingredients, usage and claims that the label supports. Our [q-commerce catalogue and creative](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content) service produces these to spec, and [product photography](https://gaa-tha.com/services/product-photography-ecommerce) handles the shoot.

### How do city and dark-store mapping and the first purchase order work?

After commercial terms are agreed, the brand and the platform decide which cities go live first. Stock is then supplied against a purchase order to the platform’s warehouse or distribution point, from where it moves to dark stores. Start with the cities where you already have demand so early velocity data is strong; expansion follows evidence, not ambition.

### What should a brand do in the first month after go-live?

Watch availability per store weekly, respond to replenishment POs fast, collect early ratings, and run a small search campaign on your own brand terms. Review per-SKU velocity at the end of the month and prune or add packs accordingly. A regional snack brand with a large range, such as [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee), would typically launch a short list of hero packs rather than the full catalogue.

Ongoing work such as PO coordination, promotions, ads and reconciliation is what [Blinkit account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-account-management) covers; onboarding itself is described on our [Blinkit seller onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-onboarding) page.

Q: How long does Blinkit onboarding take?
A: Usually several weeks from application to first order, depending on category review, document checks, catalogue approval and the first purchase order. Clean paperwork and spec-ready images shorten it.

Q: Is there a fee to list on Blinkit?
A: Commercial terms, including margins, promotional contributions and any onboarding charges, vary by category and change over time. We share the current structure for your category before you commit.

Q: Can a new brand with no online sales get on Blinkit?
A: It is possible if the product fits the category and the packaging, pricing and story are strong, but existing retail or D2C sales make approval and placement noticeably easier.

Q: Which products do best on Blinkit?
A: Fast-moving, compact, impulse-friendly products in snacks, beverages, personal care, home care and everyday essentials, with pack sizes and prices suited to top-up shopping.

Q: Do I need FSSAI to sell food on Blinkit?
A: Yes. Food and beverage products require a valid FSSAI licence and compliant labelling, and the platform will ask for the licence number during onboarding.

## How to sell on Swiggy Instamart: a guide for brands
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-swiggy-instamart
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

To sell on Swiggy Instamart, a brand applies through Swiggy’s partner route, completes a category and documentation review, submits a catalogue to Instamart’s image and data specifications, agrees commercial terms and fulfils a first purchase order for its launch cities. Instamart sits inside the Swiggy app, so its audience arrives with food and beverage habits, which suits snack, drink, dessert and meal-adjacent brands particularly well.

### Why is Instamart different from other quick-commerce apps?

Instamart shares an app with Swiggy’s food delivery, so many of its customers are already in a food mindset. Brands that pair naturally with a meal or an evening in, such as snacks, beverages, ice cream, bakery, condiments and party supplies, tend to find a receptive audience. Everyday essentials sell too, but the food link is the distinctive opportunity.

That audience also shapes timing. Orders cluster around meal times, evenings and weekends, which affects how stock should be planned and when promotions and banners are most useful.

### What does Instamart onboarding involve?

Application and category review, followed by business and brand documents (GST, PAN, bank details, trademark or authorisation, FSSAI for food), commercial terms, catalogue submission, city selection and a first purchase order. Timelines run to several weeks and vary by category. Our [Swiggy Instamart onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/swiggy-instamart-onboarding) page lists the current checklist.

Commercial terms, including margins, promotional contributions and any onboarding charges, vary by category and change over time. Ask for the current structure in writing and check the per-SKU contribution before agreeing.

### How should a brand prepare its catalogue for Instamart?

Thumbnails must be clean and legible at small size; titles carry brand, product and pack size; nutrition, ingredient and allergen information must match the label. Occasion-led combos, such as a snack and drink pairing or a party pack, are worth listing as their own SKUs. [Q-commerce creative](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content) covers thumbnails, titles and pack strategy.

Launch with a short list of hero SKUs rather than the full range. It keeps availability manageable, gives cleaner velocity data per store, and makes the case for expansion easier to argue with the category team.

### How do you manage availability and growth after launch?

Track fill rate by store weekly, coordinate replenishment purchase orders, monitor ratings, and start search ads on brand terms once availability is stable. Evening and weekend demand spikes are pronounced on a food-led platform, so stock planning should follow the order curve. A snack manufacturer such as [Ghanshyam Snacks](https://gaa-tha.com/work/ghanshyam-snacks) would plan pack sizes and stock around those peaks. [Instamart account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/instamart-account-management) handles the ongoing operation.

Q: How long does Swiggy Instamart onboarding take?
A: Typically several weeks from application to first order, depending on category review, document checks and catalogue approval. Food products with complete FSSAI and labelling information move faster.

Q: Which products sell best on Instamart?
A: Snacks, beverages, desserts, bakery, condiments and party or occasion products benefit most from Instamart’s food-led audience, alongside everyday essentials.

Q: Is there a listing fee on Swiggy Instamart?
A: Commercial terms vary by category and can include margins, promotional contributions and onboarding charges, and they change periodically. Confirm the current structure before you sign.

Q: Can I be on Instamart, Blinkit and Zepto at the same time?
A: Yes. Most brands eventually list on all three, but it is easier to launch on one, establish availability and velocity, then add the others with the learnings.

## How to sell on Zepto: onboarding, catalogue and first orders
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-zepto
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

To sell on Zepto, a brand applies to the platform’s brand partnership team, clears a category and eligibility review, submits business and brand documents, delivers a catalogue built to Zepto’s image and data specifications, and supplies stock against a first purchase order for the launch cities. Zepto’s metro-focused, impulse-led audience suits new-age consumer brands with distinctive packaging and clear pack sizes.

### What does Zepto look for in a brand?

Zepto’s category teams prioritise products that match how its customers shop: quick top-ups, snacks and beverages, personal care, home essentials and a growing premium and D2C range. Packaging that reads clearly at thumbnail size, pack prices suited to a small basket, and evidence of demand from D2C, retail or another platform all strengthen an application.

### What are the onboarding steps and documents?

The sequence is application, category review, documents, commercial terms, catalogue, city mapping and first purchase order. Documents typically include GST, PAN, bank details, trademark or brand authorisation, FSSAI for food, and SKU-level data such as barcodes, MRP, shelf life and dimensions. Requirements change; verify the current list before submitting. Our [Zepto onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/zepto-onboarding) page keeps the checklist current.

Commercial terms are agreed at this stage: margin structure, promotional contributions, payment terms and any onboarding charge. These vary by category and change over time, so get the current structure in writing and run the per-SKU arithmetic before you accept.

### How should you build the Zepto catalogue?

Each SKU needs a front-facing pack shot on a plain background, a title with the pack size, and complete attribute data. Combos and multipacks should be created as separate SKUs with their own barcodes and imagery. Because the customer decides in a second or two, the thumbnail does most of the selling; we treat it as a creative task under [q-commerce catalogue and creative](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content).

Choose the launch SKUs deliberately. Five to ten packs with clear margins and a reason to be in a small basket will outperform a full-range upload, and they make availability far easier to manage in the first weeks.

### How do you turn a listing into repeat orders?

Availability is the first lever: track per-store fill rate weekly and respond to purchase orders without delay. Ratings are the second: early reviews shape placement, so product quality and packaging integrity in delivery matter. Ads are the third, and only once the first two are stable. A brand with a strong D2C story, such as [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz), would carry the same imagery and claims from its own store into the Zepto listing so the customer sees one brand everywhere.

Ongoing operations, promotions, ads and monthly reconciliation are handled under [Zepto account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/zepto-account-management).

Q: How long does it take to get listed on Zepto?
A: Several weeks is typical, covering category review, document verification, catalogue approval and the first purchase order. Delays usually come from incomplete documents or images that fail specification checks.

Q: What documents does Zepto require?
A: Business documents such as GST, PAN and bank details, proof of brand ownership or authorisation, an FSSAI licence for food, and SKU-level data including barcodes and shelf life. The list varies by category and can change.

Q: Are there listing fees on Zepto?
A: Commercial terms differ by category and include margins, promotional contributions and in some cases onboarding charges. They change over time, so ask for the current structure in writing before signing.

Q: Should I launch on Zepto or Blinkit first?
A: Choose the platform that is stronger in the cities where you already have demand and whose category team is actively listing your product type. Many brands launch on one, prove fill rate and velocity, then add the other.

## LinkedIn outreach for exporters: a practical playbook
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/linkedin-outreach-for-exporters
Category: B2B & Manufacturing. Published 2026-09-25.

LinkedIn outreach for exporters is a structured programme of connection requests and short messages to a curated list of overseas companies and decision-makers, supported by a credible profile, a catalogue and regular proof posts. It is slower than advertising but reaches buyers that ads cannot, and it compounds: every reply, even a no, improves the list and the message for the next round.

### What should the profiles say before outreach begins?

A buyer who receives a message checks the sender’s profile first. It should state what the company makes, for which industries and countries, with certifications, capacity and a link to the catalogue or website. The company page should match. Recent posts showing the plant, dispatches and applications turn a cold message into a plausible introduction. [Copywriting](https://gaa-tha.com/services/content-writing-copywriting) for profiles and posts is a small investment with a large effect on reply rates.

### How do you build the target list?

Start from the ideal buyer profile: industries that use your product, countries where you have a cost or quality advantage, company sizes that match your minimum order. Use LinkedIn search or Sales Navigator to find companies, then the procurement, plant, quality or ownership contact at each. Record company, country, contact, product fit, status and notes in a tracker. Fifty to a hundred well-chosen companies is enough to begin; quality of fit matters more than volume.

### What does a message sequence look like?

1. **Connection note:** one line on who you are and why this company specifically.

2. **Follow-up after acceptance:** a specific reason the product fits their business, with one proof point and a catalogue link.

3. **Second follow-up:** an offer, such as a sample, a spec sheet for their application or a short call.

4. **Final touch:** a polite close that leaves the door open.

Space the messages over two to four weeks, personalise the first line, and never paste a brochure into the message. For [GI PackTech](https://gaa-tha.com/work/gi-packtech), an industrial and export packaging manufacturer, the programme took the form of a 50-company outreach tracker with curated messages and a Meta plus LinkedIn playbook, run through Sales Navigator.

### How do you track and improve results?

Log every outcome: accepted, replied, interested, not now, wrong contact, no response. Review weekly which countries, industries and message variants earn replies, and adjust the next batch. Move interested contacts into the sales pipeline with the same 24-hour qualification rule used for ad leads. Support the programme with the catalogue and company profile buyers expect, produced under [catalogues and sales kits](https://gaa-tha.com/services/catalogues-presentations). [B2B lead generation and export outreach](https://gaa-tha.com/services/b2b-lead-generation) runs the list, the sequences and the tracker as one service.

Q: Does LinkedIn outreach work for Indian exporters?
A: Yes, when it is run as a structured programme with a credible profile, a targeted list, short message sequences and consistent follow-up. It is slower than ads but reaches decision-makers directly.

Q: Do I need Sales Navigator?
A: It helps with finding the right contacts and saving lead lists, and it is usually worth it once the programme is running. A free account can start with a smaller, manually built list.

Q: How many messages should I send per day?
A: Enough to work the list steadily without triggering LinkedIn’s limits or looking automated. Consistency over weeks matters more than volume in any single day.

Q: What reply rate should I expect?
A: It varies widely by industry, country and message quality, so track your own rate by batch and improve it. The tracker will show which segments respond within a few weeks.

Q: What should I send when someone replies?
A: A short, specific answer to their question, the relevant spec sheet or catalogue page, and a proposal for the next step such as a sample or a call. Reply within a day.

## Marketplace vs D2C for FMCG brands: which channel first?
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/marketplace-vs-d2c-for-fmcg
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

For most FMCG brands the answer is not marketplace or D2C but marketplace and D2C with different jobs. Marketplaces and quick commerce bring reach, trust and impulse purchase for hero SKUs; a D2C store carries the full range, bundles, gifting and the customer relationship, at a better margin per order. The sequence depends on where demand already exists and on how much margin each channel can carry.

### What does each channel do well for an FMCG brand?

| Channel | Strength | Cost of that strength |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon and Flipkart | Search demand, trust, logistics, national reach | Fees, ad competition, no customer relationship |
| Quick commerce | Impulse and top-up purchase, city-level velocity | Margin pressure, availability operations, limited SKUs |
| D2C store | Full range, bundles, gifting, margin, customer data | You buy the traffic; conversion is your problem |

Few FMCG brands sell single low-value packs profitably on their own store; few sell gift hampers profitably on quick commerce. The channel plan follows the product.

### How do the economics compare?

On a marketplace, the brand pays referral and fulfilment fees plus ads, but does not pay for the traffic that the platform already has. On D2C, the brand keeps the margin the platform would have taken but pays to acquire every visitor and to convert them. Quick commerce sits between: platform terms are significant, but velocity can be high in dense cities.

Work out contribution per order for each channel using current fee structures, which vary and change. For low-value single packs the marketplace often wins; for bundles and gifting at a higher order value, D2C often wins. Our guide on ROAS versus MER versus contribution margin sets out the arithmetic.

### Which should an FMCG brand launch first?

If the brand already sells in retail and people search for it, Amazon first captures that demand cheaply. If the brand is new and needs to be explained, a D2C store plus Meta ads builds the story, with Amazon added once reviews exist. Quick commerce follows in the cities where demand has been proven through either route. A regional brand with a wide range, like [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee), uses the D2C store for the full catalogue and corporate gifting, with hero packs on other channels.

### How do you run all three without them fighting?

Keep pricing consistent, so no channel undercuts another. Give the store exclusives: bundles, larger packs, gifting, launches. Reuse keyword research and imagery across channels so the brand looks the same everywhere. Report on one blended view of revenue, marketing cost and contribution. [D2C brand launch](https://gaa-tha.com/services/d2c-brand-launch), [Amazon onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/amazon-onboarding) and [quick commerce management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency) are designed to run as one plan.

Q: Is D2C worth it for a low-price FMCG product?
A: Rarely for single packs, because acquisition and shipping costs exceed the margin. D2C works for FMCG when the order value is raised through bundles, multipacks, subscriptions or gifting.

Q: Will selling on Amazon hurt my D2C store?
A: Not if pricing is consistent and the store offers something the marketplace does not, such as bundles, exclusives or gifting. Many customers discover on Amazon and later buy direct.

Q: Should an FMCG brand be on quick commerce before marketplaces?
A: Usually after, because quick-commerce platforms favour brands with proven demand and because availability operations are demanding. Brands with strong city-level retail presence are the exception.

Q: How do I keep pricing consistent across channels?
A: Set one MRP and one everyday selling price policy, plan promotions per channel for defined windows, and check listings weekly. Platforms and customers both notice discrepancies.

## One website for multiple store locations: how it works
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/one-website-for-multiple-store-locations
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

One website can serve multiple store locations by asking the customer for a location or pincode, assigning the order to the nearest outlet, and notifying that outlet instantly, usually by WhatsApp. Each outlet controls its own availability, while pricing and branding stay unified. This is how sweet shops, snack chains, bakeries, pharmacies and franchise brands sell online without building a separate site per store.

### Why not build a separate site for every store?

Separate sites split the brand, the SEO authority and the maintenance effort, and customers do not know which one to use. A single site with location logic keeps one brand and one catalogue while letting each outlet fulfil its own orders. It is also easier to market: one URL on every banner, one Google Business Profile link per store pointing to the same site with the location preselected.

### How does location-based routing work?

1. The customer enters a pincode or picks a location, or the site suggests one from the browser.

2. The site maps the pincode to an outlet using a serviceable-area table.

3. The catalogue shows what that outlet has switched on.

4. At checkout, the order is tagged to the outlet and a WhatsApp or email notification goes to the outlet team.

5. The outlet confirms, prepares and delivers or hands over for pickup.

This is the core of our [multi-location and local-delivery Shopify builds](https://gaa-tha.com/services/multi-location-shopify-local-delivery).

### What controls do outlets and head office need?

Outlets need a simple availability toggle per product, order notifications, and a way to mark orders as ready or delivered. Head office needs unified pricing, design and catalogue, reporting by outlet, and rules for prepaid-only or COD by outlet and by order value. Perishable categories often run prepaid-only for larger orders and allow COD for small local ones.

Keep the outlet interface as light as possible; store staff will not use a complicated dashboard during a festive rush.

### What else should the build include?

Pickup and delivery slot selection, delivery charges by distance or zone, per-outlet Google Business Profile links with the location preselected, and tracking so that marketing can be measured per outlet. Festive gifting, corporate orders and combos usually deserve their own pages. Each outlet should also have its own [Google Business Profile](https://gaa-tha.com/services/local-seo-google-business-profile) pointing to the site, so "near me" searches land on the right store. A sweets and gifting retailer with more than one city, such as [CDS Stores](https://gaa-tha.com/work/cds-stores), is the typical use case; [Shopify development](https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development) and [custom tools](https://gaa-tha.com/services/business-tools-automation) cover the build and the routing logic.

Q: Can Shopify handle multiple store locations?
A: Yes. Shopify supports multiple inventory locations, and with custom development it can capture the customer’s location, route orders to the right outlet and notify that outlet automatically.

Q: Can each outlet have different prices?
A: It is possible, but most brands keep unified pricing to avoid confusion and to protect the brand. Availability and delivery charges are the usual per-outlet differences.

Q: How do outlets receive orders?
A: Typically by WhatsApp or email notification with the order details, plus a simple order list they can update. The aim is that store staff act on an order within minutes without training.

Q: Does this work for franchises with separate owners?
A: Yes. Orders are tagged to the franchise outlet, reporting is split by outlet, and settlement can follow the brand’s franchise agreement. The brand keeps control of design, catalogue and pricing.

## Pack size and pricing for 10-minute delivery
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/pack-size-and-pricing-for-10-minute-delivery
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

On quick commerce, pack size and price decide whether a product gets into the basket and whether the brand makes money when it does. A small trial pack at an accessible price point drives first purchase; a larger pack protects margin on repeat orders; a combo lifts basket value. The right answer is found per city from velocity and contribution data, not from the pack that sells in general trade.

### Why does pack size matter more on quick commerce than in stores?

A customer on Blinkit or Zepto is topping up, not stocking up. The basket is small, the decision is quick, and the thumbnail must communicate the pack at a glance. Dark stores also hold limited space per SKU, so the platform prefers packs that turn quickly and stack easily.

The general-trade pack that works at a kirana counter is often the wrong shape or price for this behaviour. Treating pack architecture as a channel decision, rather than a factory decision, is the first step.

### How do you choose trial, repeat and combo packs?

A trial pack is the smallest size that still delivers the product experience, priced to make the first purchase easy. A repeat pack is the size a satisfied customer buys next, priced so that the margin per order is healthy. A combo pairs two products or flavours to raise basket value and to move a slower SKU alongside a faster one.

Start with one of each for a hero product, list them as separate SKUs with their own barcodes and imagery, and let the data show which earns its shelf space. [Q-commerce catalogue and creative](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content) covers combo design and thumbnail treatment.

### How should you price for 10-minute delivery?

Begin with the platform’s current commercial terms for your category, then subtract promotional contributions, logistics to the platform, expected damages and any ad spend per unit. What remains is the contribution margin. If it is thin at the intended price, change the pack rather than the discount. Terms vary and change, so this calculation has to be repeated when they do.

Keep pricing consistent with your own store and with marketplaces. Customers compare, and platforms notice when a product is cheaper elsewhere.

### How do you read the results and adjust?

Look at units per store per week and contribution per unit, by pack and by city. A pack that sells well in one city and poorly in another is a signal about local price sensitivity or competition, not a verdict on the product. Prune packs that fail on both velocity and margin, and give the winners more availability. Our [quick commerce management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency) reporting is built around this per-SKU view.

A snack brand with many pack sizes, such as [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee), would use this method to pick a small quick-commerce range from a large catalogue.

Q: What is the best pack size for quick commerce?
A: There is no universal answer. A smaller trial pack at an easy price point and a larger repeat pack that protects margin is the usual starting pair; the data per city then shows which to keep.

Q: Can I sell the same pack on quick commerce as in retail?
A: You can, but the retail pack is often the wrong shape or price for a small, frequent basket. Test a channel-specific pack alongside it before deciding.

Q: Should I discount to win on quick commerce?
A: Discounting without knowing the contribution margin after platform terms is how brands lose money on every order. Adjust the pack and the price point first; use promotions for defined windows.

Q: How often should I review pack and pricing decisions?
A: Monthly, and whenever platform terms change. Velocity and contribution per SKU per city are the two numbers to review.

## Quick-commerce ads explained: search, category and banners
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/quick-commerce-ads-explained
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Quick-commerce ads are sponsored placements inside apps such as Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart: search ads shown against keywords, category or listing ads shown while browsing, and banners for launches and festivals. They are bought on cost-per-click or cost-per-impression models and reported against attributed sales. They work best after availability and content are stable, and they should be judged on return per SKU and on organic rank lift, not on clicks.

### What ad formats do quick-commerce platforms offer?

| Format | Where it appears | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Search ads | Results for a typed keyword | Brand terms, close category terms, competitor terms with care |
| Category or listing ads | Category pages and product carousels | Discovery for hero SKUs in relevant aisles |
| Banner placements | Home and category banners | Launches, festivals, combo offers |

Names and buying models differ by platform and change periodically; the logic is stable.

Search ads are the workhorse because intent is highest: a customer typing a product name is ready to buy. Category and banner placements are for discovery and for moments when the whole category is in demand, such as a festival week.

### When should a brand start running ads?

After fill rate is consistent on the SKUs you intend to promote and the thumbnails and titles are strong. A click that lands on an unavailable or unconvincing listing costs money twice: once for the click and again in the platform’s view of your conversion rate. Our sequence is availability, then [content](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content), then ads.

A useful readiness test: would you be happy for a stranger to see the listing exactly as it is today, in every city you plan to advertise in? If the answer is no, fix that first.

### How should campaigns be structured?

Separate brand keywords from category keywords so budgets and bids can differ. Begin with a small daily budget on brand terms, add close category terms, then generic terms as the data shows which convert. Keep a list of terms that spend without selling and exclude them where the platform allows. Rotate creative for banners with each festival or launch. The full approach is described under [quick commerce ads](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-ads).

### How do you measure quick-commerce ads honestly?

Read return on ad spend by SKU and by city rather than as one account average, and watch what happens to organic rank and sales when ads pause. Paid velocity that lifts organic placement is a good investment; paid sales that vanish the moment ads stop are a subsidy. Feed the ad numbers into the same per-SKU contribution view used for [the whole channel](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency). A multi-SKU brand such as [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee) would concentrate spend on a few packs rather than spread it thinly.

Q: How much do quick-commerce ads cost?
A: Rates are auction-based and vary by platform, category and keyword competition, and they change over time. Start with a small daily budget on brand terms and scale on the basis of per-SKU return.

Q: Do quick-commerce ads improve organic ranking?
A: Paid velocity can improve organic placement on several platforms, but only when the listing converts and stays in stock. Test by watching organic sales after a period of paid activity.

Q: Should I bid on competitor brand names?
A: It can work for discovery in crowded categories, but conversion is usually lower and platform policies vary. Test with a small budget and keep it only if the return holds.

Q: What is a good ROAS on quick commerce?
A: It depends on the SKU’s margin after platform terms. Work out the return each SKU needs to stay profitable and judge campaigns against that, not against a general benchmark.

## Quick commerce for brands in India: the 2026 guide
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/quick-commerce-for-brands-in-india-guide
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Quick commerce is the sale of everyday products through apps that deliver in roughly ten to thirty minutes from small local warehouses called dark stores. In India the main platforms are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket. For a brand, winning here means getting listed, keeping the right pack sizes in stock at every dark store that matters, and being visible in a two-second scroll. This guide covers each step, from eligibility to ads, without hype.

### What is quick commerce and why does it matter for brands in 2026?

Quick commerce (often shortened to q-commerce) is a delivery model where a platform stocks a limited, high-velocity range in dark stores inside a city and delivers orders in minutes rather than days. The customer is not searching a giant catalogue; they are refilling a basket while the kettle boils. That changes everything about how a product needs to be packed, priced and presented.

For brands, the channel matters for three reasons. It has become a habitual purchase route for urban households in snacks, beverages, personal care, dairy, staples and home care. It gives a new brand shelf space without a distributor network in every city. And it produces fast feedback: you learn within weeks whether a pack size sells in a neighbourhood. The trade-off is that the platforms control listing, placement and stock, so a brand has to run the channel as an operation, not a one-time upload. Our [quick commerce management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency) practice exists for exactly that reason.

### Which quick commerce platforms should a brand be on?

Six platforms matter for most Indian brands in 2026. They overlap in categories but differ in city coverage, how they buy stock and how they treat new brands. Begin with one or two, chosen by where your existing demand is.

| Platform | What it is | Typical fit for a brand |
|---|---|---|
| Blinkit | Zomato-owned, one of the earliest and widest dark-store networks | Grocery, snacks, personal care, home and small electronics; brands with metro demand |
| Zepto | Independent quick commerce app with a strong metro presence | Impulse and premium everyday products; new-age D2C brands |
| Swiggy Instamart | Quick commerce inside the Swiggy app | Food-adjacent and beverage brands that benefit from a food-ordering audience |
| Flipkart Minutes | Flipkart's quick delivery service | Brands already selling on Flipkart; grocery and general merchandise |
| Amazon Now | Amazon's quick delivery service in select cities | Brands already on Amazon with a Brand Registry and strong reviews |
| BigBasket / BB Now | Tata-owned grocery platform with scheduled and quick delivery | Staples, packaged food, larger household packs |

City coverage and category priorities change frequently, so treat this as orientation rather than a rulebook. We cover the onboarding differences in dedicated guides for [Blinkit](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-onboarding), [Zepto](https://gaa-tha.com/services/zepto-onboarding), [Swiggy Instamart](https://gaa-tha.com/services/swiggy-instamart-onboarding), [Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now](https://gaa-tha.com/services/flipkart-minutes-amazon-now-onboarding) and [BigBasket](https://gaa-tha.com/services/bigbasket-onboarding).

### Is my product right for the ten-minute basket?

Not every good product is a good quick commerce product. Before you apply, check the SKU against the conditions the channel rewards.

- **Velocity.** Dark stores hold limited shelf space. A SKU that sells slowly gets delisted, quietly, per store.

- **Compact packs.** Small, stackable, sturdy packaging survives bike delivery and fits the storage racks.

- **Impulse or refill behaviour.** Products people buy without research (snacks, drinks, essentials) outperform products that need comparison.

- **Margin headroom.** Platform commissions, ad spend, promotions and returns all come out of your price. If the SKU cannot absorb that, it is not ready.

- **Shelf life and compliance.** Food needs FSSAI licensing and clear best-before dating; cosmetics need their own compliance.

- **Existing demand.** Brands with retail or D2C sales in a city onboard faster and get better placement than unknown names.

A regional snack brand with dozens of SKUs, like [Charliee](https://gaa-tha.com/work/charliee), is a good example of where selection matters: a handful of hero packs belong on quick commerce, the full range does not.

### How does quick commerce onboarding actually work?

Onboarding follows a similar shape on every platform, even though the portals and the people differ. Expect several weeks from first application to first order, longer if documents or images need rework.

1. **Eligibility and category review.** The platform's category team decides whether the brand fits. Existing sales data, retail presence and packaging quality all help.

2. **Documentation.** GST registration, PAN, bank details, brand ownership or authorisation (trademark certificate or a brand authorisation letter), FSSAI licence for food, and any category-specific licences.

3. **Commercial terms.** Margin or commission structure, payment terms, promotional commitments and, on some platforms, a listing or onboarding charge. These vary by category and change; we share the current structure before you commit.

4. **Catalogue and content.** Titles with pack size, clean thumbnails on a plain background, ingredient and nutrition panels, barcodes (EAN/GTIN) mapped correctly.

5. **City and dark-store mapping.** Which cities go live first and which stores get stocked. Start narrow.

6. **First purchase order and go-live.** Stock reaches the platform's warehouse or is placed directly at dark stores, listings switch on, and the real work begins.

The most common delays are mismatched barcodes, images that fail spec checks and unclear brand ownership paperwork. Fix those before applying.

### How do the economics work: margins, pack sizes and pricing?

Quick commerce is a margin business before it is a marketing business. Work out the per-unit picture for every SKU you plan to list, using the platform's current terms, before the first purchase order.

| Line | What to account for |
|---|---|
| Selling price | Usually anchored to MRP, with platform-led discounts you may be asked to fund partly or fully |
| Platform margin or commission | Varies by category and platform; confirm the current rate card in writing |
| Promotions and visibility | Festive schemes, buy-more offers and ad spend you choose to run |
| Logistics to the platform | Freight to the platform's warehouse or to city hubs, plus any inbound rejection costs |
| Returns, damages and expiry | Small per unit, but real across thousands of orders |
| Contribution margin | What is left after all of the above; this is the number that decides whether the SKU stays |

Pack size is the biggest lever you control. Many brands find that a smaller trial pack at an accessible price point drives first purchase, while a larger pack protects margin on repeat orders. Test both, and read the data per city rather than as one national average. Our note on [catalogue and pack strategy](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-content) goes deeper.

### How do you stay in stock across hundreds of dark stores?

Availability is the first growth lever on quick commerce, ahead of content and ads. If a customer opens the app in a neighbourhood and your product shows as unavailable, no amount of advertising helps, and repeated out-of-stocks lower your ranking. Managing this well means treating the channel like distribution.

- **Track fill rate per store, not per city.** Platform dashboards show availability at store level; someone on your side needs to look at them every week.

- **Respond to purchase orders quickly.** A late or short-shipped PO becomes an empty shelf ten days later.

- **Prioritise a short list of hero SKUs.** It is better to be always in stock on five packs than sometimes in stock on twenty.

- **Plan for festivals and weather.** Snacks, beverages and gifting spike in predictable windows; the platform's buying team will not plan your stock for you.

- **Reconcile monthly.** Match POs, invoices, deductions and payouts so that leakage is caught early.

This is the core of [Blinkit](https://gaa-tha.com/services/blinkit-account-management), [Zepto](https://gaa-tha.com/services/zepto-account-management) and [Instamart account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/instamart-account-management): less glamorous than ads, and more valuable.

### How do quick commerce ads work and when should you start them?

Each platform sells sponsored placements inside its app: search ads that appear when a customer types a keyword, category or listing ads that appear while browsing, and banner placements for larger campaigns. They are bought on cost-per-click or cost-per-impression models and reported against sales attributed to the ad.

Start ads only once availability and content are solid. Otherwise you pay for clicks that land on an out-of-stock listing or a poor thumbnail. A sensible sequence is search ads on your own brand terms and close category terms first, then generic category keywords, then banners for launches or festivals. Judge results on return on ad spend at the SKU level and on whether organic rank improves after a period of paid velocity. We explain the formats and how we run them in [quick commerce ads](https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-ads).

### What does a quick commerce agency do, and when do you need one?

A quick commerce agency handles the parts of the channel that need daily attention and platform know-how: onboarding, catalogue and imagery, availability tracking, purchase-order coordination, promotions, ads, ratings and monthly reconciliation. Some brands run this in-house with a dedicated key-account person; many find that one person cannot cover five platforms and a dozen cities.

You probably need outside help if listings are live but sales are flat, if you cannot say what your fill rate was last week, or if you are funding discounts without knowing the contribution margin. gaa-tha runs all six platforms as one operation, with imagery produced in-house through [product photography](https://gaa-tha.com/services/product-photography-ecommerce), and reports monthly on availability, sales, ad efficiency and ratings. Fees are usually a one-time onboarding charge plus a monthly management fee, with ad spend paid directly to the platform.

### What should a 90-day quick commerce launch plan look like?

A realistic first quarter is narrow and disciplined. The aim is to prove that a small set of SKUs sells at a healthy margin in a few cities, then to earn the right to expand.

| Weeks | Focus | What good looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | SKU selection, unit economics, documents, imagery and catalogue prep | Five to ten SKUs with clear margins and spec-compliant assets |
| 3–6 | Applications on one or two platforms, commercial terms, city mapping, first PO | Listings live in the cities where you already have demand |
| 7–10 | Availability tracking, replenishment rhythm, ratings, first search ads on brand terms | Consistent fill rate on hero SKUs; early velocity data per store |
| 11–13 | Review per-SKU contribution, prune or add packs, plan the next platform or city | A written decision on what to scale and what to drop |

If you would like this plan built for your brand, start with a conversation about your SKUs, cities and margins.

Q: What is quick commerce?
A: Quick commerce is the sale and delivery of everyday products within minutes through apps that stock goods in small local warehouses called dark stores. In India the main platforms are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket.

Q: Which quick commerce platform should a brand launch on first?
A: Start with the one or two platforms that are strongest in the cities where you already have demand and whose category team is actively listing your type of product. Proving fill rate and velocity on one platform makes the next onboarding easier.

Q: What documents are needed to sell on Blinkit, Zepto or Instamart?
A: Typically GST registration, PAN, bank details, proof of brand ownership or authorisation, an FSSAI licence for food products, and product-level details such as barcodes and shelf life. Requirements vary by platform and category and can change.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
A: Commercial terms differ by platform and category and include margins or commissions, promotional contributions and, in some cases, onboarding or listing charges. They change over time, so we share the current structure for your category before you sign anything.

Q: How long does quick commerce onboarding take?
A: Usually several weeks from application to first order, depending on category approval, document checks, catalogue quality and how quickly the first purchase order is fulfilled. Clean documents and spec-ready images shorten the process.

Q: How do you measure success on quick commerce?
A: Track availability or fill rate per dark store, units and revenue per SKU per city, contribution margin after platform costs, ad return on spend, and ratings. Availability is the leading indicator; everything else follows it.

## ROAS vs MER vs contribution margin: which number to run on
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/roas-vs-mer-vs-contribution-margin
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

ROAS measures revenue attributed by one ad platform against spend on that platform; MER (marketing efficiency ratio) measures total revenue against total marketing spend; contribution margin measures what is left after product, shipping, payment, returns and marketing costs. Run the business on contribution margin, manage the blend on MER, and use ROAS only to compare campaigns within a platform.

### What does each metric actually measure?

| Metric | Formula | Use it for | Weakness |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROAS | Platform-attributed revenue ÷ platform spend | Comparing campaigns and creatives inside one platform | Attribution overlap; ignores costs |
| MER | Total revenue ÷ total marketing spend | Judging the whole marketing mix month to month | Says nothing about margin |
| Contribution margin | Revenue − COGS − shipping − payment fees − returns − marketing | Deciding whether to scale, hold or cut | Needs accurate cost data |

### Why does platform ROAS mislead?

Meta and Google each claim the purchases they touched, so the same order can appear in both dashboards. Platforms also count some purchases that would have happened anyway, particularly from brand searches and retargeting. And ROAS treats a ₹1,000 order with a ₹200 margin the same as one with a ₹600 margin. A campaign can show a healthy ROAS while the business loses money on every order.

Fixing tracking with Conversions API and consistent UTMs helps, but the structural problem remains. That is why our [D2C performance marketing](https://gaa-tha.com/services/d2c-performance-marketing) reporting leads with blended numbers.

### How do you set targets in the right order?

1. Work out contribution margin per order before marketing, from real cost data.

2. Decide how much of that margin can go to marketing while leaving the profit the business needs.

3. That gives a target MER for the month.

4. Split the marketing budget by channel and derive the platform ROAS each channel must achieve for the blend to hit the MER.

5. Review weekly; when MER slips, look at creative, conversion rate and returns before cutting spend.

A concern-led brand selling kits at a higher order value, such as [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz), will tolerate a lower ROAS than a brand selling single low-value packs, because the margin per order is higher.

### What else changes when you run on contribution?

Bundles and kits become priorities because they raise margin per order. Returns and COD refusals get measured and reduced, because they destroy contribution. [Conversion rate optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/conversion-rate-optimisation) is valued correctly, because a higher conversion rate lowers cost per order across every channel. And retention becomes visible: a repeat order carries little or no marketing cost and lands almost entirely in contribution. See the D2C ecommerce growth guide for how these fit together.

Q: What is a good ROAS for a D2C brand in India?
A: It depends entirely on margin per order. Derive it from your contribution target rather than from a benchmark: a brand with high-margin kits can accept a lower ROAS than one selling low-margin single packs.

Q: What is MER in marketing?
A: Marketing efficiency ratio is total revenue divided by total marketing spend across all channels for a period. It shows how efficiently the whole mix turns spend into revenue, without relying on platform attribution.

Q: How do I calculate contribution margin for an ecommerce order?
A: Take the order revenue and subtract cost of goods, packaging, shipping, payment gateway fees, expected returns or refusals and the marketing cost to acquire it. What remains is the contribution before fixed costs.

Q: Should I stop looking at ROAS altogether?
A: No. ROAS remains useful for comparing campaigns, audiences and creatives inside one platform. It is simply the wrong number to run the business on.

## Selling on Amazon, Flipkart & Myntra: the brand playbook
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/selling-on-amazon-flipkart-myntra-brand-playbook
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.

Selling on Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra as a brand means registering as a seller, proving you own or are authorised to sell the brand, building listings that rank for the words customers search, and then managing stock, ads, reviews and account health every week. The platforms differ in category strength and in how they treat fashion versus general merchandise. This playbook walks through the decisions in order, so that a brand can launch on the right marketplace and grow without losing its margin.

### Which marketplace should a brand start with?

Start where your category is strongest and where you can support the operation. Amazon and Flipkart are broad marketplaces that cover almost every category; Myntra is a fashion and lifestyle destination with its own catalogue standards; Nykaa and AJIO are specialist platforms for beauty and fashion. A brand rarely needs all of them on day one.

| Marketplace | Strength | Good first choice for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amazon | Search-led buying, Brand Registry, A+ content, FBA logistics | Packaged food, home, electronics accessories, books, personal care, B2B-friendly categories | Crowded categories; ad costs rise with competition |
| Flipkart | Strong in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, sale events, fashion and electronics | Value-led products, apparel, home and kitchen, festive-driven categories | Listing QC is strict; returns in fashion can be high |
| Myntra | Fashion-first audience, curated brand presence, style-based catalogue | Apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty with a fashion angle | Approval is selective; image and attribute specs are demanding |
| Nykaa / Nykaa Fashion | Beauty and premium fashion audience | Skincare, cosmetics, wellness, premium apparel | Brand curation; expect an eligibility review |
| AJIO | Reliance-backed fashion platform | Fashion brands broadening reach beyond Myntra | Similar approval process to other fashion platforms |
| Meesho / JioMart | Value and reseller-led demand; grocery on JioMart | Low-price, high-volume products | Thin margins; positioning matters |

For most non-fashion brands, Amazon first and Flipkart second is the common path. For fashion, Myntra approval is the prize, with Flipkart as volume support. Our [Amazon onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/amazon-onboarding), [Flipkart](https://gaa-tha.com/services/flipkart-seller-management) and [Myntra onboarding](https://gaa-tha.com/services/myntra-onboarding) pages list the specific steps for each.

### What does a brand need before it can be onboarded?

Every marketplace asks for the same core documents, and each adds a few of its own. Get them in one folder before you begin.

- **Business identity:** GST registration, PAN, a current-account bank statement or cancelled cheque, and a business address for pickups.

- **Brand ownership:** a registered trademark, or a trademark application together with a brand authorisation letter if you are selling someone else's brand. Amazon Brand Registry needs a trademark that is registered or pending.

- **Category approvals:** some categories (food, cosmetics, supplements, electronics) require licences such as FSSAI or BIS, and product-level safety or ingredient information.

- **Product data:** barcodes (GTIN/EAN) for each SKU, dimensions and weights, HSN codes, MRP and manufacturing details for the label.

- **Imagery to spec:** white-background main images at the required resolution, plus lifestyle and infographic images. Fashion platforms specify model shots, angles and backgrounds.

Timelines vary from a few days for a straightforward Amazon or Flipkart registration to several weeks when category approvals or a Myntra eligibility review are involved.

### How do you build listings that rank and convert?

A marketplace listing ranks on two things at once: how relevant it looks to the search engine and how well it converts once shown. The two feed each other, which is why a listing with the right keywords and poor images still sinks.

1. **Keyword research per platform.** Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra searches differ. Pull terms from search suggestions, competitor listings and your own ad search-term reports.

2. **Title structure.** Brand, product type, key attribute, size or pack, variant. Front-load what customers search; avoid stuffing.

3. **Bullets and description.** Bullets answer the buying questions in order of importance (what it is, who it is for, what is inside, how to use, why this one). The description carries the story and the secondary keywords.

4. **Backend keywords and attributes.** Fill every attribute field; filters on Myntra and Flipkart depend on them.

5. **Image stack.** Main image on white, then infographics for benefits, a size or pack visual, a lifestyle scene, and a comparison or "what is in the box" image.

6. **Price and offers.** Consistent pricing across channels avoids losing the buy box or being flagged.

This is the work we do under [listing and catalogue optimisation](https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-listing-optimisation), with images produced through [ecommerce product photography](https://gaa-tha.com/services/product-photography-ecommerce).

### When do A+ content and a Brand Store pay for themselves?

A+ content (Amazon's enhanced description modules) and a Brand Store add rich imagery, comparison tables and brand storytelling below or alongside the listing. They tend to pay when a product needs explanation, has several variants, or sits in a category where trust matters more than price. A commodity SKU competing on price alone gains less.

Prioritise A+ for hero SKUs that already get traffic, and use the modules to answer the objections that appear in reviews and customer questions. A Brand Store is worth building once you have a range to cross-sell and are running Sponsored Brands ads that can point to it. Flipkart offers its own rich-content options with similar logic.

### How do marketplace ads work on Amazon and Flipkart?

Both platforms sell sponsored placements auctioned on cost per click. On Amazon the main formats are Sponsored Products (individual listings in search and on product pages), Sponsored Brands (a headline banner with several products or a store link) and Sponsored Display (retargeting and audience placements). Flipkart's Product Listing Ads and Product Contextual Ads follow the same idea.

A sensible structure separates brand keywords, category keywords and competitor keywords into their own campaigns, with automatic campaigns used only to discover new search terms. Negative keywords are added weekly. Budgets move toward the SKUs with the best return and the best organic-rank lift, not simply the lowest cost per click. Sale events on Flipkart and festive windows on Amazon deserve their own plans and budgets. We run this under [marketplace ads management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-ads-management).

### How do you manage inventory, fulfilment and account health?

Operations decide whether a listing keeps its rank. Marketplaces reward sellers who ship on time, keep stock available and keep cancellations, returns and complaints low.

- **Fulfilment model.** Amazon FBA or Flipkart's warehousing services take over storage and delivery for a fee; self-ship keeps control but demands discipline. Many brands use both by SKU.

- **Stock planning.** Forecast by SKU and marketplace, with buffers for sale events. A stock-out on a ranking listing can take weeks to recover.

- **Account health metrics.** Late shipment rate, order defect rate, cancellation rate and policy compliance. Set alerts and act on them the same day.

- **Returns and claims.** File claims for damaged or lost inventory within the window; reconcile settlement reports monthly.

Our [Amazon account management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/amazon-account-management) service covers this operational layer alongside listings and ads.

### How do reviews and ratings shape marketplace sales?

Reviews are both a ranking input and a conversion input. A new listing with no reviews converts poorly regardless of price; a listing with a steady flow of honest reviews earns rank and holds it. The only sustainable approach is policy-compliant: use the platform's own review request tools, include a well-designed package insert that invites feedback without offering incentives, and respond to every negative review with a fix rather than an argument.

Ratings problems are usually product or packaging problems in disguise. Read the one- and two-star reviews monthly, group them by cause, and fix the cause. We manage this loop under [reviews and ratings management](https://gaa-tha.com/services/reviews-ratings-management).

### How do you read the numbers: a monthly marketplace P&L?

Marketplace dashboards report sales and ad performance, but not profit. A brand should build a simple monthly P&L per marketplace that turns gross sales into contribution.

| Line | Source |
|---|---|
| Gross sales (units × selling price) | Order reports |
| Less returns and cancellations | Returns reports |
| Less marketplace fees (referral, closing, shipping, storage) | Settlement reports |
| Less ad spend | Ad console |
| Less cost of goods and packaging | Your own costing |
| Contribution margin | What remains; track by SKU where possible |

Fee structures differ by category and change over time, so use the platform's current fee calculator rather than a remembered percentage. Once the P&L exists, decisions become simpler: which SKUs get ad budget, which get discounted, which get delisted.

### When should a brand add Myntra, Nykaa or AJIO?

Fashion and beauty brands should apply to specialist platforms once their catalogue, imagery and sizing data are ready, because those platforms judge brands on presentation before they judge on sales. Approval is selective, and a strong brand story, consistent model photography and complete attribute data improve the odds.

Once live, the operating rhythm is similar to Amazon and Flipkart, with more emphasis on style-level catalogue accuracy, size charts, seasonal drops and event participation. Growth across several fashion platforms benefits from a shared plan that adapts assortment, pricing and content per platform, which is what our [fashion marketplace growth](https://gaa-tha.com/services/fashion-marketplace-growth) service does. A concern-led D2C brand such as [Kitcoz](https://gaa-tha.com/work/kitcoz) illustrates the wider point: the marketplace listing and the brand's own store should tell the same story, so that a shopper who researches on one and buys on the other feels no gap.

Q: Do I need a trademark to sell on Amazon or Flipkart?
A: You can register as a seller without one, but brand protection features such as Amazon Brand Registry require a registered or pending trademark. If you sell another company’s brand, you need a brand authorisation letter. We recommend filing the trademark before launch.

Q: What is marketplace account management?
A: It is the ongoing operation of a brand’s presence on a marketplace: listings, pricing, stock, ads, account health, reviews and monthly reconciliation. The aim is to hold rank, protect margin and grow sales without the brand’s own team watching dashboards every day.

Q: How much does it cost to sell on Amazon in India?
A: Amazon charges referral fees by category plus closing, shipping and storage fees depending on the fulfilment model, and the rates change periodically. Use the platform’s current fee calculator for your category and build a per-SKU P&L before listing.

Q: My listings are live but not selling. What should I check first?
A: Check whether the listing shows for the keywords customers use, whether the main image and price are competitive in the search results, and whether reviews and stock are in place. In most cases the fix is a rebuilt listing and a steady review flow before any ad spend.

Q: How long does Myntra onboarding take?
A: Longer than a general marketplace, because Myntra reviews brand eligibility and catalogue quality before approval. Expect several weeks, with time added for image reshoots or attribute corrections if the first submission falls short of spec.

Q: Should I run marketplace ads from day one?
A: Run a small brand-keyword and discovery campaign early to gather search-term data, but hold larger budgets until the listing converts on its own. Ads scale a listing that works; they rarely fix one that does not.

## Shopify speed and conversion checklist for Indian stores
https://gaa-tha.com/blog/shopify-speed-and-conversion-checklist
Category: Commerce. Published 2026-09-25.
